name: arg_base_bound519
header:
private lemma arg_base_bound519 (N : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hα : |α| ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ)) :
    |Complex.arg ((((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))| ≤
      Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi)
doc:
/-- The principal argument of the base `1 / N + 2 pi alpha i` of the Mellin power factor
stays `1 / (16 * pi)` away from `pi / 2` when `|alpha| ≤ 4 / N`: the modulus of the base is at
most `(1 / N) sqrt (1 + (8 pi) ^ 2)`, so its cosine is at least `1 / sqrt (1 + (8 pi) ^ 2)`,
which is at least `1 / (16 pi)`, which is at least `sin (1 / (16 pi))`. -/

name: mellin_base_bound519
header:
theorem mellin_base_bound519 (N : ℕ) (α t : ℝ) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
    (hα : |α| ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ)) :
    ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
        (-(mellinLine519 N t))‖ ≤
      Real.exp 1 * Real.sqrt N *
        Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. First step of the parent proof, the modulus of the power factor.
For N at least two and alpha at most four over N the base of the power has
real part one over N and imaginary part at most eight pi over N, so the
imaginary part of its logarithm is at most pi over two minus one over
sixteen pi; its modulus is at least one over N, and N to the power a half
plus one over log N is at most e times the square root of N. No Gamma
factor, no logarithm of N, no integral here. -/

name: log_cube_split519
header:
theorem log_cube_split519 (N : ℕ) (t : ℝ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
    Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3 ≤
      8 * Real.log N ^ 3 + 8 * Real.log (|t| + 2) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Second step of the parent proof, the split of the logarithm.
For N at least two the logarithm of N times the sum of absolute t and two
is the sum of two nonnegative logarithms, so its cube is at most eight
cubes of log N plus eight cubes of the logarithm of the sum. -/

name: integrable_exp_neg_abs519
header:
private lemma integrable_exp_neg_abs519 (b : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-b * |t|))
doc: /-- `exp (-b * |t|)` is integrable on the line for `b > 0`. -/

name: shift_pow_five_le_exp519
header:
private lemma shift_pow_five_le_exp519 (e : ℝ) (he : 0 < e) :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 ≤ K ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, (|t| + 4) ^ 5 ≤ K * Real.exp (e * |t|)
doc:
/-- A fifth power is dominated by a constant times `exp (e * |t|)` for every `e > 0`: this is
Taylor's inequality `v ^ 5 ≤ 5 ! exp v` at `v = e * (|t| + 4)`, together with
`e * (|t| + 4) = e * |t| + 4 * e`. -/

name: integrable_majorant519
header:
private lemma integrable_majorant519 :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => (|t| + 4) ^ 5 * Real.exp (-(1 / (16 * Real.pi)) * |t|))
doc:
/-- The majorant `(|t| + 4) ^ 5 exp (-|t| / (16 pi))` of the twisted Gamma mass is
integrable on the line. -/

name: continuous_mellinLine519
header:
private lemma continuous_mellinLine519 (N : ℕ) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => mellinLine519 N t
doc: /-- `mellinLine519 N` is continuous in `t`. -/

name: gamma_line_uniform519
doc:
/-- The Gamma factor on the shifted Mellin line decays exponentially in `|t|` for every
`N ≥ 2`. For a line with real part at most `3 / 2` this is `gamma_absolute_decay519`; otherwise
the real part is at most `5 / 2` and `Gamma s = (s - 1) Gamma (s - 1)` moves it into the strip. -/

name: gamma_twist_pointwise519
header:
private lemma gamma_twist_pointwise519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) (t : ℝ) :
    Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi))) *
        ‖Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)‖ * (1 + Real.log (|t| + 2) ^ 3) ≤
      Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * 2 *
        ((|t| + 4) ^ 5 * Real.exp (-(1 / (16 * Real.pi)) * |t|))
doc: /-- Pointwise domination of the twisted Gamma mass with a logarithm factor. -/

name: continuous_gamma_mellin519
header:
private lemma continuous_gamma_mellin519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)
doc:
/-- `Gamma` composed with the shifted Mellin line is continuous: the line has positive real
part, so it stays away from the poles of `Gamma`. -/

name: gamma_twist_mass519
header:
theorem gamma_twist_mass519 :
    ∃ G : ℝ, 0 < G ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N →
      Integrable (fun t : ℝ =>
        Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi))) *
          ‖Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)‖) ∧
      Integrable (fun t : ℝ =>
        Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi))) *
          (‖Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)‖ * Real.log (|t| + 2) ^ 3)) ∧
      (∫ t : ℝ, Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi))) *
        ‖Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)‖) ≤ G ∧
      (∫ t : ℝ, Real.exp (|t| * (Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (16 * Real.pi))) *
        (‖Complex.Gamma (mellinLine519 N t)‖ *
          Real.log (|t| + 2) ^ 3)) ≤ G
doc:
/-- LEAF. Third step of the parent proof, the twisted Gamma mass. The
Gamma factor on the line, weighted by the exponential gap of the power
factor and by the cube of the logarithm of the sum of absolute t and two,
is integrable for every N at least two, and both of its integrals are at
most one constant independent of N and of alpha. This is the analytic core
of the parent proof and the only place where the decay of Gamma is used. -/

name: kernel_mass_integrable519
header:
theorem kernel_mass_integrable519 (N : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hN : 32 ≤ N)
    (hα : |α| ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ)) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => ‖mellinKernel519 N α t‖ *
      Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Fourth step of the parent proof, the integrability half of the
parent conclusion. The modulus of the kernel times the cube of the
logarithm of N times the sum of absolute t and two is integrable, for N at
least thirty two and alpha at most four over N. This is the first
conjunct of the parent statement on its own, without any estimate of the
integral. -/

name: mass_constant519
header:
theorem mass_constant519 (N : ℕ) (G : ℝ) (hN : 32 ≤ N) (hG : 0 < G) :
    8 * Real.exp 1 * Real.sqrt N * (Real.log N ^ 3 * G + G) ≤
      8 * Real.exp 1 * G * (1 + 1 / Real.log 2 ^ 3) * Real.sqrt N *
        Real.log N ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Fifth step of the parent proof, the bookkeeping of the constant.
For N at least thirty two and a positive constant G, eight e times the
square root of N times the cube of log N times G plus G is at most the
cube of log N times the square root of N times the constant eight e G
times one plus the inverse cube of log two. The last factor absorbs the
additive G because the cube of log N is at least the cube of log two. -/

name: central_kernel_mass519
header:
theorem central_kernel_mass519 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ α : ℝ, |α| ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ) →
        Integrable (fun t : ℝ => ‖mellinKernel519 N α t‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ∧
        (∫ t : ℝ, ‖mellinKernel519 N α t‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ≤
            C * Real.sqrt N * Real.log N ^ 3
doc:
/-- The parent statement central_kernel_mass442, reassembled from the five
leaves above. No use of the parent theorem, no sorry. -/

name: continuous_mellin_integrand519
header:
theorem continuous_mellin_integrand519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N)
    (M : ℝ → ℂ) (hM : Continuous M) :
    Continuous (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => mellinKernel519 N p.1 p.2 * M p.2)
doc: /-- P0093 page 157 equation 4.4. The signed kernel with a continuous coefficient is jointly continuous in alpha and the finite line parameter. -/

name: stronglyMeasurable_mellinU519
header:
theorem stronglyMeasurable_mellinU519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N)
    (M : ℝ → ℂ) (hM : Continuous M) :
    StronglyMeasurable (mellinU519 N M)
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 4.1. Parameter integration of the continuous signed kernel makes the full Mellin value strongly measurable. -/

name: mellin_reflection519
header:
theorem mellin_reflection519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (M : ℝ → ℂ) (α : ℝ) :
    mellinU519 N (fun t => (starRingEnd ℂ) (M (-t))) α = (starRingEnd ℂ) (mellinU519 N M (-α))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 final sentence after equation 4.8. Reflecting alpha
conjugates the Mellin integral and reflects and conjugates its coefficient.
Positive N keeps the complex power base away from its branch cut.
No GRH or line bound is assumed. -/

name: reflected_line_bound519
header:
theorem reflected_line_bound519 (N : ℕ) (B0 : ℝ) (M : ℝ → ℂ) (hM : Continuous M)
    (hb : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) :
    Continuous (fun t => (starRingEnd ℂ) (M (-t))) ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
      ‖(starRingEnd ℂ) (M (-t))‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 final sentence after equation 4.8. Reflecting and
conjugating a coefficient preserves continuity and the cubic logarithmic
line bound with the same constant. -/

name: mellin_negative_square519
header:
theorem mellin_negative_square519 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (M : ℝ → ℂ) (r : ℝ) :
    (∫ α in -r..0, ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) =
      ∫ α in 0..r, ‖mellinU519 N (fun t => (starRingEnd ℂ) (M (-t))) α‖ ^ 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 final sentence after equation 4.8. The negative
half square integral equals the positive half square integral for the
reflected conjugate coefficient. Interval orientation is retained. -/

name: central_mellin_bound519
header:
theorem central_mellin_bound519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
        ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
        ∀ α : ℝ, |α| ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ) →
          ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ≤ K * Real.sqrt N * Real.log N ^ 3
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 before equation 4.8. The clean central absolute
kernel bound controls every coefficient with the cubic logarithmic line bound. -/

name: central_square_mass519
header:
theorem central_square_mass519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
        ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
        IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) (Set.Icc 0 (4 / (N : ℝ))) ∧
        (∫ α in 0..(4 / (N : ℝ)), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤ C * Real.log N ^ 6
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 equation 4.8. The positive central interval has
integrable square mass at most a constant times log to the sixth N.
This follows from the clean square root N pointwise bound and interval length. -/

name: lemma2_outer_square519
header:
theorem lemma2_outer_square519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2)
            (Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) ∧
          (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 10)
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 158 equation 4.7, from the signed double frequency
calculation of pages 157 and 158 equations 4.4 through 4.6. Only the positive
outer interval remains. The Mellin integral stays signed before squaring.
There is no central interval, negative half, prime, character or GRH here. -/

name: lemma2_positive_square519
header:
theorem lemma2_positive_square519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) (Set.Icc 0 (1 / R)) ∧
          (∫ α in 0..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 13)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 equations 4.7 and 4.8. The full positive half interval
is assembled from the clean central part and the signed outer estimate.
CONDITIONAL ON lemma2_outer_square519. -/

name: grh_mellin_transfer519
header:
theorem grh_mellin_transfer519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ∃ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
            ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ∧ ∀ α : ℝ,
              ‖characterPrime519 χ N α - mellinU519 N M α‖ ≤ B * Real.sqrt N
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 159 before equation 5.1. GRH supplies the logarithm
of L on the vertical line with its uniform cubic logarithmic bound. The
Mellin identity retains the prime power correction bounded by square root N.
This is the corrected transfer already recorded for mellin_transfer1622.
There is no arc integral or rational system in this input. -/

name: lemma2_square519
header:
theorem lemma2_square519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) (Set.Icc (-(1 / R)) (1 / R)) ∧
          (∫ α in -(1 / R)..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 13)
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 156 through 158 Lemma 2 equations 4.1 through 4.8.
The diagonal square estimate is assembled from the clean central interval,
the signed outer estimate and the proved conjugate reflection.
CONDITIONAL ON lemma2_outer_square519. No GRH or prime occurs here. -/

name: nonprincipal_mass519
header:
theorem nonprincipal_mass519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
            (∫ α in -(1 / R)..(1 / R), ‖characterPrime519 χ N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
              C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 13)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.2. The corrected Mellin transfer and the
abstract square estimate imply the nonprincipal character square estimate.
CONDITIONAL ON grh_mellin_transfer519 and lemma2_square519. -/

name: principal_arithmetic519
header:
theorem principal_arithmetic519 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hlog : 1 ≤ Real.log N)
    (hq : (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) ≤ q) (hqN : (q : ℝ) ≤ N) :
    (N : ℝ) / q.totient ≤ 4 * (N : ℝ) ^ (9 / 10 : ℝ) * Real.log N
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 passage from equation 9.1 to 9.3. The logarithmic
totient ratio keeps the full q saving on the specified minor denominator range. -/

name: system_character_bound519
header:
theorem system_character_bound519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) < q →
        (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∫ α in arcSystem519 q ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ∩ Set.Icc 0 1,
          ‖primeFourier111_up111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) ^ (9 / 10 : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.1. The finite character expansion and the
nonprincipal square estimate give the system bound before power absorption.
CONDITIONAL ON grh_mellin_transfer519 and lemma2_square519. -/

name: system_mass519
header:
theorem system_mass519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∫ α in arcSystem519 q ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ∩ Set.Icc 0 1,
          ‖primeFourier111_up111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤ C * (N : ℝ) ^ (93 / 100 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equations 9.1 and 9.3. Logarithmic absorption of
the character system estimate on the minor denominator range.
CONDITIONAL ON grh_mellin_transfer519 and lemma2_square519. -/

name: denominator_range519
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equations 9.1 and 9.3. The denominator range is
nonempty at arbitrarily large integral scales: N is k to seventy and q
is k to nine for any integer k at least two. -/

name: square_root_totient_loss519
header:
theorem square_root_totient_loss519 (C : ℝ) : ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
    C * (N : ℝ) ^ (93 / 100 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) ^ (19 / 20 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 passage from equation 9.1 to 9.3. Arithmetic audit
of the earlier square root totient route. A bound at exponent nineteen
twentieths cannot imply any fixed constant bound at ninety three hundredths.
This compares candidate bounds and asserts no failure of the paper. -/

name: nonprincipal_mod_three519
header: theorem nonprincipal_mod_three519 : ∃ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 3, χ ≠ 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.2. The nonprincipal character domain
has a concrete inhabitant modulo three. This instance assumes no GRH. -/

name: rational_separation520
header:
theorem rational_separation520 (a b : ℤ) (q r : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hne : a * (r : ℤ) - b * (q : ℤ) ≠ 0) :
    1 / ((q : ℝ) * r) ≤ |(a : ℝ) / q - (b : ℝ) / r|
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 before equation 8.1. Distinct rational centres are
separated by the reciprocal product of their denominators. -/

name: rational_arcs_disjoint520
header:
theorem rational_arcs_disjoint520 (a b : ℤ) (q r : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hne : a * (r : ℤ) - b * (q : ℤ) ≠ 0) (τ : ℝ)
    (hτsum : (q : ℝ) + r < τ) :
    Disjoint
      (Set.Icc ((a : ℝ) / q - 1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))
        ((a : ℝ) / q + 1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)))
      (Set.Icc ((b : ℝ) / r - 1 / ((r : ℝ) * τ))
        ((b : ℝ) / r + 1 / ((r : ℝ) * τ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 before equation 8.1. Two rational major arcs are
disjoint when their denominator sum is strictly smaller than tau. -/

name: arcIndices520
header: noncomputable def arcIndices520 (Q : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)
doc: /-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The finite reduced rational centres, including both endpoint representatives at modulus one. -/

name: rationalArc520
header: noncomputable def rationalArc520 (q a : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) : Set ℝ
doc: /-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The full closed rational arc of radius one over q tau. -/

name: rationalMajor520
header: noncomputable def rationalMajor520 (Q : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) : Set ℝ
doc: /-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The rational major arcs with natural denominator cutoff, clipped to the unit interval. -/

name: arcIndices_mem520
header:
theorem arcIndices_mem520 (Q : ℕ) (p : ℕ × ℕ) :
    p ∈ arcIndices520 Q ↔ 1 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 ≤ Q ∧ p.2 ≤ p.1 ∧ Nat.Coprime p.2 p.1
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. Membership in the finite rational centre index set. -/

name: rational_major_cover520
header:
theorem rational_major_cover520 (Q : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 1 < τ) :
    rationalMajor520 Q τ =
      ⋃ p ∈ arcIndices520 Q, Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ rationalArc520 p.1 p.2 τ
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The rational definition equals the explicit finite union of clipped arcs. -/

name: arcIndices_cross_ne520
header:
theorem arcIndices_cross_ne520 (Q : ℕ) (p t : ℕ × ℕ)
    (hp : p ∈ arcIndices520 Q) (ht : t ∈ arcIndices520 Q) (hne : p ≠ t) :
    (p.2 : ℤ) * t.1 - (t.2 : ℤ) * p.1 ≠ 0
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. Distinct reduced rational representatives have nonzero cross difference. -/

name: rational_clipped_integral520
header:
theorem rational_clipped_integral520 (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) (τ : ℝ)
    (hτ : 2 * (Q : ℝ) < τ) (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : Continuous f) :
    (∫ α in rationalMajor520 Q τ, f α) =
      ∑ p ∈ arcIndices520 Q,
        ∫ α in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ rationalArc520 p.1 p.2 τ, f α
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The integral over the major arcs is the sum of the clipped arc integrals. -/

name: rational_arc_integral520
header:
theorem rational_arc_integral520 (q a : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 0 < τ)
    (f : ℝ → ℂ) :
    (∫ α in rationalArc520 q a τ, f α) =
      ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))..(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)), f ((a : ℝ) / q + z)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. Translation converts a full rational arc integral to its symmetric local coordinate integral. -/

name: interior_arc_subset520
header:
theorem interior_arc_subset520 (q a : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (ha : a < q)
    (hc : Nat.Coprime a q) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 1 ≤ τ) :
    rationalArc520 q a τ ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. For denominator at least two, every reduced representative arc lies inside the unit interval. -/

name: unit_arc_join520
header:
theorem unit_arc_join520 (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 2 < τ) (f : ℝ → ℂ)
    (hf : Continuous f) (hp : Function.Periodic f 1) :
    (∫ α in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ rationalArc520 1 0 τ, f α) +
      (∫ α in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ rationalArc520 1 1 τ, f α) =
      ∫ z in -(1 / τ)..(1 / τ), f z
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The clipped endpoint arcs join into the symmetric unit modulus arc by period one. -/

name: denominator_arc_sum520
header:
theorem denominator_arc_sum520 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 2 < τ)
    (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : Continuous f) (hp : Function.Periodic f 1) :
    (∑ a ∈ (Icc 0 q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
      ∫ α in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ rationalArc520 q a τ, f α) =
    ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
      ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))..(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)), f ((a : ℝ) / q + z)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. At each denominator the clipped representatives give the required full local arc sum. -/

name: arcIndices_sum520
header:
theorem arcIndices_sum520 (Q : ℕ) (H : ℕ × ℕ → ℂ) :
    (∑ p ∈ arcIndices520 Q, H p) =
      ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 Q, ∑ a ∈ (Icc 0 q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), H (q, a)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The pair index sum equals the iterated denominator and reduced numerator sum. -/

name: rational_partition520
header:
theorem rational_partition520 (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) (τ : ℝ)
    (hτ : 2 * (Q : ℝ) < τ) (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : Continuous f) (hp : Function.Periodic f 1) :
    (∫ α in rationalMajor520 Q τ, f α) =
      ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 Q, ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))..(1 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)), f ((a : ℝ) / q + z)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. A continuous periodic function has the exact rational arc partition when tau exceeds twice Q. -/

name: major_parameters_separated520
header:
theorem major_parameters_separated520 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ^ 70 < N) :
    1 ≤ ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ ∧
      2 * (⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. Above two to power seventy the chosen tau exceeds twice the integer Q. -/

name: major_arc_partition_proved520
header:
theorem major_arc_partition_proved520 :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ f : ℝ → ℂ,
      Continuous f → Function.Periodic f 1 →
      (∫ α in majorArcs280_up111 N, f α) =
        ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊,
          ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
            ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))..
                (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))),
              f ((a : ℝ) / q + z)
doc: /-- LEAF. P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 166 equation 8.2. The exact major arc partition at the parameters used by the sealed target. -/

name: principalPrime520
header: noncomputable def principalPrime520 (N q : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 before equation 5.1. The principal character prime series
is the prime series with the prime divisors of the modulus removed. -/

name: principalCoefficient520
header: noncomputable def principalCoefficient520 (q : ℕ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The principal rational coefficient. -/

name: residueError520
header: noncomputable def residueError520 (N q a : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The residue error retains the omitted
prime divisor terms after removing the principal character contribution. -/

name: localArc520
header: noncomputable def localArc520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 pages 155 and 156 equations 3.1 and 3.4. The local prime square integral. -/

name: mixedIntegral520
header: noncomputable def mixedIntegral520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 pages 155 and 156 equations 3.1 and 3.4. The mixed local contribution. -/

name: errorIntegral520
header: noncomputable def errorIntegral520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 pages 155 and 156 equations 3.1 and 3.4. The square of the residue error. -/

name: principalIntegral520
header: noncomputable def principalIntegral520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 page 160 equation 6.1. The principal square on one centred arc. -/

name: signedRamanujan520
header: noncomputable def signedRamanujan520 (q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The Ramanujan phase at a signed residual. -/

name: logConvolution520
header: noncomputable def logConvolution520 (n : ℕ) : ℝ
doc: /-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The exact logarithmic convolution. -/

name: localMain520
header: noncomputable def localMain520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4. The exact damped local main term. -/

name: continuous_principal520
header:
theorem continuous_principal520 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Continuous (principalPrime520 N q)
doc: /-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1. The principal series is continuous. -/

name: continuous_residue520
header:
theorem continuous_residue520 (N q a : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Continuous (residueError520 N q a)
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. Every residue error is continuous. -/

name: residue_square520
header:
theorem residue_square520 (N q a : ℕ) (z : ℝ) :
    primeFourier111_up111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z) ^ 2 =
      principalCoefficient520 q ^ 2 * principalPrime520 N q z ^ 2 +
        2 * principalCoefficient520 q * principalPrime520 N q z * residueError520 N q a z +
        residueError520 N q a z ^ 2
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. Exact square expansion at one residue. -/

name: centred_phase520
header:
theorem centred_phase520 (q a : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (z : ℝ) :
    Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The centred phase factors exactly. -/

name: local_decomposition520
header:
theorem local_decomposition520 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (n : ℤ) :
    localArc520 N q n =
      principalCoefficient520 q ^ 2 * signedRamanujan520 q n * principalIntegral520 N q n +
        mixedIntegral520 N q n + errorIntegral520 N q n
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. Exact principal, mixed and error square split. -/

name: residue_square_mean520
header:
theorem residue_square_mean520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
      (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))..(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))), ‖residueError520 N q a z‖ ^ 2) ≤
        C * (N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 pages 159 and 160 equations 3.4, 5.2 and 5.4.
The residue error square means summed over the reduced residues are bounded.
The error retains the omitted prime divisor terms of equation 3.4.
GRH Mellin square estimates and character orthogonality supply this bound. -/

name: mixed_bound520
header:
theorem mixed_bound520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖mixedIntegral520 N q n‖ ≤ C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 6 /
        Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 160 equations 5.3 and 5.5 with equation 3.4.
The mixed contribution has square root of q tau in its denominator.
The residue error retains the omitted prime divisors of the modulus. -/

name: logCoefficient520
header: noncomputable def logCoefficient520 (N m : ℕ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The damped reciprocal logarithm coefficient,
extended by zero at frequencies zero and one. -/

name: logFourier520
header: noncomputable def logFourier520 (N : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : ℂ
doc: /-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The model series S one. -/

name: logCoefficient_summable520
header:
theorem logCoefficient_summable520 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Summable (logCoefficient520 N)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The logarithmic coefficients are absolutely
summable by comparison with the geometric damping series. -/

name: fourier_square_group520
header:
theorem fourier_square_group520 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, a m * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) ^ 2 =
      ∑' m : ℕ, (∑ j ∈ range (m + 1), a j * a (m - j)) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. Mathlib Cauchy multiplication groups the
square of an absolutely convergent Fourier series by its total frequency. -/

name: fourier_square_integral520
header:
theorem fourier_square_integral520 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (n : ℤ) :
    (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1,
      (∑' m : ℕ, a m * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * z * (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      if 0 ≤ n then ∑ j ∈ range (n.toNat + 1), a j * a (n.toNat - j) else 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The full period coefficient of the square
is its Cauchy convolution at nonnegative residuals and zero at negative residuals. -/

name: logCoefficient_convolution520
header:
theorem logCoefficient_convolution520 (N m : ℕ) :
    (∑ j ∈ range (m + 1), logCoefficient520 N j * logCoefficient520 N (m - j)) =
      ((Real.exp (-(m : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution520 m : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The Cauchy coefficient of S one
squared is exactly the exponentially damped finite logarithmic convolution. -/

name: logFourier_square_integral520
header:
theorem logFourier_square_integral520 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (n : ℤ) :
    (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1, logFourier520 N z ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * z * (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution520 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The exact signed full period
model integral is the damped convolution, including every negative residual. -/

name: principal_model520
header:
theorem principal_model520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖principalIntegral520 N q n -
        (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1, logFourier520 N z ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * z * (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))‖ ≤
        C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
          (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
            1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 pages 160 and 161 equations 6.1 through 6.3.
Replace the principal square by the full period S one square model.
This is the analytic contour comparison. Fourier extraction is proved separately. -/

name: principal_convolution520
header:
theorem principal_convolution520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖principalIntegral520 N q n -
        ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution520 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
        C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
          (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
            1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 160 and 161 equations 6.1 through 6.3.
CONDITIONAL on principal_model520. Extend the principal square to a full period and read its exact convolution.
No fixed one over N shoulder is removed. -/

name: error_integral_le520
header:
theorem error_integral_le520 (N q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) :
    ‖errorIntegral520 N q n‖ ≤
      ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ∫ z in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))..
          (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))),
          ‖residueError520 N q a z‖ ^ 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 160 equation 5.4. The phase has unit norm, so the error
square integral is bounded by its square mean at every signed residual. -/

name: logConvolution_vanish520
header:
theorem logConvolution_vanish520 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 3) :
    logConvolution520 n = 0
doc: /-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The convolution vanishes below four. -/

name: logConvolution_four520
header:
theorem logConvolution_four520 :
    logConvolution520 4 = 1 / (Real.log 2 * Real.log 2)
doc: /-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The first nonzero convolution. -/

name: signedRamanujan_toNat520
header:
theorem signedRamanujan_toNat520 (q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    signedRamanujan520 q n = LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n.toNat
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. Nonnegative signed phases equal the
natural Ramanujan sum already formalized in Ramanujan103. -/

name: ramanujan_im_zero520
header:
theorem ramanujan_im_zero520 (q m : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q m).im = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4. The Ramanujan sum is real by its
integer Mobius divisor expansion. -/

name: ramanujan_cos520
header:
theorem ramanujan_cos520 (q m : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q m =
      ((∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (m : ℝ) * (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4. The complex Ramanujan sum is exactly
the cast of the finite real cosine sum used in the sealed target. -/

name: principal_coefficient_norm_real520
header:
theorem principal_coefficient_norm_real520 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (n : ℤ) :
    ‖(((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
      signedRamanujan520 q n‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The principal arithmetic coefficient
has norm at most one for every positive modulus and every signed frequency. -/

name: principal_coefficient_norm520
header:
theorem principal_coefficient_norm520 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (n : ℤ) :
    ‖principalCoefficient520 q ^ 2 * signedRamanujan520 q n‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. The coefficient in the square expansion
has the same norm bound as its real fraction form. -/

name: local_expansion520
header:
theorem local_expansion520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖localArc520 N q n - localMain520 N q n‖ ≤
        B * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
          (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
            1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 160 and 161 equations 5.4, 5.5 and 6.3.
CONDITIONAL on the three explicit local analytic leaves. The elementary
assembly retains the exact Ramanujan coefficient and damped convolution. -/

name: residual_periodic520
header:
theorem residual_periodic520 (N : ℕ) (n : ℤ) :
    Function.Periodic (fun α : ℝ => primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1. The signed residual integrand has period
one. The proof also covers every negative integer residual. -/

name: major_integral_partition520
header:
theorem major_integral_partition520 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ^ 70 < N) (n : ℤ) :
    (∫ α in majorArcs280_up111 N, primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊, localArc520 N q n
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1. Join the clipped endpoints and sum the
local prime square integrals over disjoint rational arcs. -/

name: local_main_cos520
header:
theorem local_main_cos520 (N q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (n : ℤ) :
    localMain520 N q n =
      ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) *
        (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
          ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
            Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (n.toNat : ℝ) * (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) *
        logConvolution520 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4. A local main term is the real cosine
coefficient times the exact damped convolution, even for negative residuals. -/

name: major_expansion520
header:
theorem major_expansion520 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖(∫ α in majorArcs280_up111 N, primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * (n : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) -
        ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) *
          (∑ q ∈ Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊,
            ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ) ^ 2 *
              ∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
                Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (n.toNat : ℝ) * (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) *
          logConvolution520 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
        B * N * Real.log N ^ 13 * ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊,
          (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
            1 / Real.sqrt (q * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 161 and 165 equations 6.4 and 8.1. The per modulus
expansion and the exact disjoint arc partition give the summed expansion.
CONDITIONAL on residue_square_mean520, mixed_bound520 and principal_model520. -/

name: principal_unit520
header:
theorem principal_unit520 (N : ℕ) (z : ℝ) :
    principalPrime520 N 1 z = primeFourier111_up111 N z
doc: /-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. At modulus one no prime divisor is removed. -/

name: residue_unit520
header: theorem residue_unit520 (N : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : residueError520 N 1 0 z = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. At the unit modulus residue zero
is exactly principal, so its residue error vanishes pointwise. -/

name: error_unit520
header: theorem error_unit520 (N : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : errorIntegral520 N 1 n = 0
doc: /-- P0093 page 160 equation 5.4. The unit modulus error square is zero. -/

name: mixed_unit520
header: theorem mixed_unit520 (N : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : mixedIntegral520 N 1 n = 0
doc: /-- P0093 page 160 equation 5.5. The unit modulus mixed term is zero. -/

name: local_main_four_unit520
header:
theorem local_main_four_unit520 (N : ℕ) :
    localMain520 N 1 4 =
      ((Real.exp (-(4 : ℝ) / N) / (Real.log 2 * Real.log 2) : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4. At modulus one and residual four
the main term is positive and has the exact first convolution value. -/

name: local_parameters_instance520
header:
theorem local_parameters_instance520 (N0 : ℕ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, N0 < N ∧ 2 ^ 70 < N ∧ 1 ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) ∧
      (4 : ℤ) ≤ N ∧ 0 < (Real.exp (-(4 : ℝ) / N) / (Real.log 2 * Real.log 2))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 161 and 165 equations 6.4 and 8.1. There are arbitrarily
large admissible parameters with modulus one and a nonzero convolution. -/

name: rational_phase521
header:
theorem rational_phase521 (q a : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (z : ℝ) :
    Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4. Split the residual phase at a rational centre.
This is an exact identity and does not approximate the prime series. -/

name: rational_model_sum521
header:
theorem rational_model_sum521 (q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n)
    (c : ℂ) (F : ℝ → ℂ) (l r : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
      ∫ z in l..r, (c * F z) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      c ^ 2 * LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n.toNat *
        (∫ z in l..r, F z ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4 and page 161 equation 6.4.
A residue independent model square factors into its arithmetic coefficient,
the Ramanujan sum and its remaining integral. Both endpoints remain arbitrary. -/

name: rational_model_error521
header:
theorem rational_model_error521 (q : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n)
    (c : ℂ) (P F : ℝ → ℂ) (l r : ℝ) (D : ℂ) :
    ‖(∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ∫ z in l..r, P ((a : ℝ) / q + z) ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) -
      c ^ 2 * LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n.toNat * D‖ ≤
      ‖(∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
          ∫ z in l..r, P ((a : ℝ) / q + z) ^ 2 *
            Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) -
        (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
          ∫ z in l..r, (c * F z) ^ 2 *
            Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))‖ +
      ‖c ^ 2 * LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n.toNat‖ *
        ‖(∫ z in l..r, F z ^ 2 *
            Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) - D‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 3.4 and page 161 equations 6.2 and 6.3.
Auxiliary exact error decomposition. The first error compares a shifted
square with the rational model. The second keeps the model integral
minus its proposed coefficient D. No bound on either error is assumed. -/

name: square_series521
header:
theorem square_series521 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, a m * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) ^ 2 =
      ∑' n : ℕ, (∑ m ∈ range (n + 1), a m * a (n - m)) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * n) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The square of an absolutely summable
negative Fourier series has the Cauchy product coefficients. -/

name: square_series_integral521
header:
theorem square_series_integral521 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1,
      (∑' m : ℕ, a m * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ∑ m ∈ range (n + 1), a m * a (n - m)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. Full period extraction of the coefficient
of a squared absolutely summable negative Fourier series. -/

name: logCoefficient521
header: noncomputable def logCoefficient521 (N m : ℕ) : ℝ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 definition of S one after equation 6.3.
Its real coefficients vanish below two and otherwise carry reciprocal logarithms. -/

name: log_coefficients_summable521
header:
theorem log_coefficients_summable521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Summable (fun m : ℕ => (logCoefficient521 N m : ℂ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The logarithmic model has absolutely
summable coefficients at each positive damping scale. -/

name: log_coefficient_convolution521
header:
theorem log_coefficient_convolution521 (N n : ℕ) :
    (∑ m ∈ range (n + 1),
      (logCoefficient521 N m : ℂ) * (logCoefficient521 N (n - m) : ℂ)) =
      ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. Multiplying the logarithmic
coefficients gives the exact convolution with damping at the residual. -/

name: square_series_integral_shift521
header:
theorem square_series_integral_shift521 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (n : ℕ) (b : ℝ) :
    (∫ z in b..b + 1,
      (∑' m : ℕ, a m * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ∑ m ∈ range (n + 1), a m * a (n - m)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equations 6.2 and 6.3. Extraction on any full period
has the same coefficient. The starting point is arbitrary. -/

name: logarithmicModel521
header: noncomputable def logarithmicModel521 (N : ℕ) (z : ℝ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 definition of S one after equation 6.3.
The damped reciprocal logarithm series is indexed by all natural numbers
with its first two coefficients set to zero. -/

name: logarithmic_model_full_period521
header:
theorem logarithmic_model_full_period521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ z in (-1 / 2 : ℝ)..(1 / 2 : ℝ), logarithmicModel521 N z ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
        ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3 and its following display.
The full period model square gives the exact damped convolution.
This theorem states no estimate for a truncated core interval. -/

name: logarithmic_model_residue521
header:
theorem logarithmic_model_residue521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (q n : ℕ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
      ∫ z in (-1 / 2 : ℝ)..(1 / 2 : ℝ),
        ((((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) / (q.totient : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          logarithmicModel521 N z) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ((((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n *
        ((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n : ℝ) : ℂ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.4 before the convolution asymptotic.
The full period logarithmic model with the principal rational coefficient
has exactly the singular coefficient times the Ramanujan sum times the
damped convolution. No approximation of the prime square is asserted. -/

name: core_diagonal_integral521
header:
theorem core_diagonal_integral521 (N : ℕ) :
    (∫ z in -(1 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / (N : ℝ)),
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * (2 : ℕ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (4 : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ((2 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. Auxiliary interval diagnostic.
A single negative mode at two paired with residual four has constant
integrand one. Its core integral is two over N rather than a full period. -/

name: core_diagonal_not_full_period521
header:
theorem core_diagonal_not_full_period521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    (∫ z in -(1 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / (N : ℝ)),
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * (2 : ℕ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (4 : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) ≠ 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. Auxiliary interval diagnostic.
For N at least three the core diagonal is not the full period coefficient.
This refutes an exact truncated orthogonality substitution only. -/

name: logarithmic_model_nonpositive521
header:
theorem logarithmic_model_nonpositive521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≤ 0) :
    (∫ z in (-1 / 2 : ℝ)..(1 / 2 : ℝ), logarithmicModel521 N z ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 sentence after equation 6.3. The full period logarithmic
model coefficient vanishes at every nonpositive signed residual.
The model itself has positive coefficients starting at frequency two. -/

name: logarithmic_model_signed_full_period521
header:
theorem logarithmic_model_signed_full_period521 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (n : ℤ) :
    (∫ z in (-1 / 2 : ℝ)..(1 / 2 : ℝ), logarithmicModel521 N z ^ 2 *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
        ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3 and its nonpositive residual case.
The exact full period model coefficient uses the natural part of a signed
residual. At a negative residual the convolution is empty and both sides vanish. -/

name: principal_error_small549
header:
theorem principal_error_small549 (C ε : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      C * Real.log N ^ 15 *
        (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
          1 / Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) ≤ ε
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. The displayed error at modulus one, multiplied
by log squared N and divided by N, tends to zero. This uses the existing
logarithmic power absorption theorem. -/

name: principal_main_dominates_error549
header:
theorem principal_main_dominates_error549 (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
        (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
          1 / Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) <
        Real.exp (-1) * logConvolution1622 N
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. At residual N the damped convolution
exceeds every fixed multiple of the displayed unit modulus error for large N.
The lower bound is the existing clean logarithmic convolution theorem. -/

name: principal_amplitude_incompatible_with_unit549
header:
theorem principal_amplitude_incompatible_with_unit549
    (hunit : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → q = 1 →
        ∀ n : ℤ, 4 ≤ n → n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n -
          ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))) :
    ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 equation 6.3. QUESTION about the sealed split.
If the unit modulus approximation holds, the error only amplitude statement
is false. The witness is modulus one and residual N for large N.
No GRH, Mellin bound or admitted theorem is used in this implication. -/

name: small_power_divisors376
header:
theorem small_power_divisors376 :
    ∃ D : ℝ, 0 < D ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ D * (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 100 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 168 last inequality in equation 10.5. The standard
small power bound for the divisor count used there, with exponent three
hundredths. This is independent of the singular series and its cutoff. -/

name: combine_tail_powers376
header:
theorem combine_tail_powers376 (x : ℝ) (hx : 1 ≤ x) :
    x ^ (3 / 100 : ℝ) * x ^ (-(1 / 20 : ℝ)) ≤ x ^ (-(1 / 100 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.5. Multiplying the divisor loss with the
tail saving gives exponent negative two hundredths, which is stronger than
the negative one hundredth requested by singular_tail357. -/

name: integral_exp_two_pi_mul_int_proved439
header:
theorem integral_exp_two_pi_mul_int_proved439 (m : ℤ) :
    (∫ α in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * (m : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) =
      if m = 0 then 1 else 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 154 equation 2.2, elementary integer phase integral.
Exact integral_exp_two_pi_mul_int357 statement, using the proved lab
phase integral already used for the page 162 Fourier coefficient identity. -/

name: log_power_absorption_proved439
header:
theorem log_power_absorption_proved439 :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ 13 ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 40 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.3, absorption of the logarithm by a
positive power saving. Exact log_power_absorption357 statement. -/

name: entropy_fraction435
header:
theorem entropy_fraction435 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧
      ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 equation 7.18 and page 165 equation 7.19.
The entropy cost tends to zero with the exceptional fraction.
This is the parameter choice after the binary word count. -/

name: entropy_unit_bound435
header:
theorem entropy_unit_bound435 (M r : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (hr : 4 ≤ r)
    (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2)
    (hcost : ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1)))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 after equation 7.19. The explicit finite word
bound is at most four times the prescribed dyadic measure scale once
the entropy cost is below delta log two. -/

name: entropy_three_periods435
header:
theorem entropy_three_periods435 (M r : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
      3 * volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
        (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card}
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 measure conclusion after equation 7.19.
Three consecutive periods cost at most three unit period measures.
Integer translation preserves the concentration predicate. -/

name: binary_entropy_measure_proved435
header:
theorem binary_entropy_measure_proved435 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, 4 ≤ r ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ M0 : ℕ, ∀ M : ℕ, M0 < M →
        volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
          (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
            C * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 164 and 165 binary word count and measure conclusion.
The exact binary_entropy_measure412 statement has a clean proof from
the proved Gallagher word count. No cited entropy input is used. -/

name: binary_three_period_measure439
header:
theorem binary_three_period_measure439 (M r : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
        3 * volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
          (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card}
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 after equation 7.19. Periodicity extends the unit
period binary concentration measure to three periods, with no loss except
the factor three. The remaining endpoint is a singleton of measure zero. -/

name: binary_unit_entropy_bound439
header:
theorem binary_unit_entropy_bound439 (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (ε δ : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2)
    (hentropy : ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M 4 α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1)))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 164 and 165 equations 7.15 through 7.19. The explicit
binomial expression has the desired exponential rate once its entropy
coefficient is small. This step contains no binary word counting. -/

name: binary_entropy_measure_proved439
header:
theorem binary_entropy_measure_proved439 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, 4 ≤ r ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ M0 : ℕ, ∀ M : ℕ, M0 < M →
        volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
          (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
            C * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 163 through 165 binary expansion 7.12 through 7.19.
Exact binary_entropy_measure412 statement, supplied by the existing finite
word count, continuity of x log x and the three period measure extension. -/

name: near_phase_digit_equal412
header:
theorem near_phase_digit_equal412 (M r m : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α : ℝ)
    (hm : m ∈ nearIntegerIndices412 M r α) :
    LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.digit α (m + 2) =
      LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.digit α (m + 3)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 after equation 7.12. A near integer doubling at
binary radius at most one sixteenth forces two adjacent binary digits
 to agree. Reuse the proved lab cosine to digit implication from P0094
page 132 Lemma 1. -/

name: changes_le_bad_indices412
header:
theorem changes_le_bad_indices412 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α : ℝ) :
    (LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.changes α M).card ≤
      M - (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 binary run count leading to 7.13. Every change
in the interior digit string corresponds injectively to an index outside
the near integer set. This supplies the exact exceptional set needed
by the existing Gallagher finite word counting proof. -/

name: changes_fraction_bound412
header:
theorem changes_fraction_bound412 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α ε : ℝ)
    (hgood : (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card) :
    ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.changes α M).card : ℝ) ≤ ε * M
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 equations 7.13 through 7.15. The concentration
fraction implies the corresponding real upper bound for digit changes.
The existing Gallagher count and binomial estimate can now be reused. -/

name: concentrated_word_mem412
header:
theorem concentrated_word_mem412 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α ε : ℝ)
    (hα : α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1)
    (hgood : (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card) :
    ⌊(2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1) * α⌋₊ ∈ LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 equation 7.13 and page 165 equation 7.19.
The binary word of a concentrated phase belongs to the exact finite
word set already counted in the proved Gallagher module. -/

name: binary_cells_measure412
header:
theorem binary_cells_measure412 (M : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      ⌊(2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1) * α⌋₊ ∈ S} ≤
        (S.card : ENNReal) * ENNReal.ofReal (1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 after equation 7.19. A finite collection of binary
words covers its phases by equal dyadic cells. Its measure is at most
the word count times their common length. -/

name: binary_unit_measure_le_words412
header:
theorem binary_unit_measure_le_words412 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (ε : ℝ) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
        ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)).card : ENNReal) *
          ENNReal.ofReal (1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 word count and page 165 conversion to measure.
The actual near integer phase set in one period is bounded by the
proved Gallagher word count at parameter epsilon over four. -/

name: near_indices_int_shift412
header:
theorem near_indices_int_shift412 (M r : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (z : ℤ) :
    nearIntegerIndices412 M r (α + z) = nearIntegerIndices412 M r α
doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 binary expansion and page 165 measure bound.
Integer translation preserves the exact near integer index set.
Thus the binary concentration condition is periodic with period one. -/

name: binary_word_card_bound412
header:
theorem binary_word_card_bound412 (M : ℕ) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε * M) (hM : ε * M ≤ (M - 1 : ℕ)) :
    ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)).card : ℝ) ≤
      4 * (Real.exp 1 * (M - 1 : ℕ) / (ε * M)) ^ (ε * M)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 164 binomial estimate 7.15 and Gallagher page 133
counting proof. Reuse the proved finite word injection and small subset
bound to retain the explicit entropy expression before choosing epsilon. -/

name: binary_unit_measure_explicit412
header:
theorem binary_unit_measure_explicit412 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε * M) (hM : ε * M ≤ (M - 1 : ℕ)) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (Real.exp 1 * (M - 1 : ℕ) / (ε * M)) ^ (ε * M) /
          (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 conversion of word count to measure after 7.19.
The actual binary concentration set in one period satisfies the explicit
binomial entropy bound already proved in the Gallagher counting library.
Only the small fraction choice and bounded period extension remain. -/

name: entropy_fraction439
header:
theorem entropy_fraction439 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧
      ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 164 and 165 equations 7.15 through 7.19. Choose a
positive exceptional fraction below one half with arbitrarily small
binomial entropy exponent. This is independent of the binary phase set. -/

name: singular_eq_heath_brown_all435
header:
theorem singular_eq_heath_brown_all435 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    singularSeries111 n = LeanLab.HeathBrown1985.singular n
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6. At an odd positive residual,
the prime two local factor vanishes, so the full product is zero.
Together with the proved even bridge this identifies the product
with the existing general Heath Brown singular series. -/

name: ramanujan_real_eq_gm435
header:
theorem ramanujan_real_eq_gm435 (n q : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :

Adding the series at phases alpha and alpha plus one half leaves exactly
 twice the damped term of the prime two. This separates the full prime series term
from the exceptional prime two correction. -/

name: prime_half_value453
header:
theorem prime_half_value453 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    primeFourier111 N (1 / 2) + primeFourier111 N 0 =
      2 * (Real.exp (-(2 : ℝ) / N) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 155 equation 2.3 at denominator two and zero local shift.
The values at zero and one half differ by the exact prime two correction. -/

name: prime_power_five357
header: theorem prime_power_five357 : primePowerCount111 5 = 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 definition before equation 7.4. The fiber at five is
nonempty and has exactly the representation three plus two to the first. -/
