doc:
/-- P0093 page 154 equation 2.1. The representation count has a positive
instance at eight from the two primes three and the positive power two. -/

name: truncated_singular_one357
header: theorem truncated_singular_one357 (n : ℕ) : truncatedSingular357 1 n = 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6. At cutoff one the finite singular
series contains only its normalized modulus one term. -/

name: phase_five357
header:
theorem phase_five357 :
    fourierCoeffOn (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)
      (fun α => Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (5 : ℕ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) (-5) = 1 ∧
    fourierCoeffOn (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)
      (fun α => Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (5 : ℕ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) 5 = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.4. A single phase at negative five has
coefficient one there and zero at the positive frequency five. -/

name: power_zero_norm_pos376
header:
theorem power_zero_norm_pos376 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    0 < ‖powerFourier111 N 0‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 154 definition of T. At phase zero the damped power
series has strictly positive norm for every positive N. -/

name: large_value_zero376
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 Lemma 5. For positive eta and positive N, zero
belongs to the actual large T set. The interval cover cannot be justified
by treating its covered set as empty. -/

name: power_trunc_two412
header: theorem power_trunc_two412 : powerTrunc412 2 0 = (Real.exp (-1) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. At N equal to two the finite
polynomial at zero has its single positive term exp of negative one. -/

name: near_indices_interval412
header:
theorem near_indices_interval412 (M r : ℕ) (α : ℝ)
    (hα : |α| ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (M + r)) :
    (nearIntegerIndices412 M r α).card = M
doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 equation 7.11. A whole interval around zero, of
radius two to the negative sum of M and r, has all M dyadic phases in range.
This is a positive length instance of the binary concentration set. -/

name: binary_set_positive_measure412
doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 equation 7.11 and page 165 entropy measure bound.
For every nonnegative exceptional fraction the actual binary phase
set in three periods has strictly positive measure at each finite M.
This excludes an empty set justification of the entropy supply leaf. -/

name: finite_large_value_zero412
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. For every N at least two and every
positive eta, phase zero lies in the actual finite polynomial large
value set. The eventual concentration hypothesis is therefore nonempty. -/

name: weighted_alignment_instance435
header:
theorem weighted_alignment_instance435 (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    (1 - η) * (∑ _m ∈ Finset.range 1, (1 : ℝ)) <
      ‖∑ _m ∈ Finset.range 1, (1 : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (0 : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.8. The weighted alignment hypothesis
holds for a one term unit weight and zero phase at every positive eta.
This is an actual nonzero norm instance. -/

name: dyadic_system_range435
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 denominator range in equation 9.3. Explicit
 dyadic points have denominator two to eight m between N to one tenth
and N to one seventh when N is two to seventy m. -/

name: system_range_unbounded435
header:
theorem system_range_unbounded435 (N0 : ℕ) :
    ∃ N q : ℕ, N0 < N ∧ 1 ≤ q ∧
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) ≤ q ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 denominator range in equations 9.1 and 9.3.
For every proposed threshold there are larger N and a positive natural
q in the required denominator interval. This witnesses the numerical
hypotheses only. It does not assume or witness GRH. -/

name: mellin_kernel_norm_pos442
header:
theorem mellin_kernel_norm_pos442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 < N) (α t : ℝ) :
    0 < ‖mellinKernel442 N α t‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 4.1. For N greater than one the Mellin
kernel has positive norm at every real phase and frequency. Its base
has positive real part and its Gamma argument has positive real part. -/

name: lineBound_one_large442
header:
theorem lineBound_one_large442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    LineBound1622 N 1 (fun _ => 1)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 156 equation 4.1. The constant one coefficient
satisfies the line bound at every N at least three. This supplies a
nonzero witness arbitrarily far beyond any threshold. -/

name: symmetric_integral376
header:
theorem symmetric_integral376 (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f)
    (heven : ∀ x, f (-x) = f x) (A : ℝ) :
    (∫ x in -A..A, f x) = 2 * (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..A, f x)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 symmetric frequency box. Integrating an even
continuous function on a symmetric interval doubles its positive half. -/

name: kernel_box_bound376
header:
theorem kernel_box_bound376 (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f)
    (hpos : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    (∫ t in -T..T, ∫ u in -T..T, f (t + u)) ≤
      2 * T * (∫ v in -(2 * T)..(2 * T), f v)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 integration of a frequency kernel on a square box.
Each translated inner interval lies in the symmetric interval of twice
the radius. Nonnegativity permits that enlargement. -/

name: reciprocal_abs_integral376
header:
theorem reciprocal_abs_integral376 (A : ℝ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    (∫ x in -A..A, 1 / (1 + |x|)) = 2 * Real.log (A + 1)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 reciprocal difference kernel. The symmetric
one dimensional integral has the exact elementary logarithmic value. -/

name: exp_abs_integral_le376
header:
theorem exp_abs_integral_le376 (c A : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    (∫ x in -A..A, Real.exp (-c * |x|)) ≤ 2 / c
doc:
/-- P0093 page 158 decaying sum kernel. Its symmetric one dimensional
integral is at most twice the inverse decay rate. -/

name: weighted_power_summable412_l4p111
header:
theorem weighted_power_summable412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Summable (fun m : ℕ => ((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) *
      Real.exp (-((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N))
doc:
/-- PORT of weighted_power_summable412 from Stability412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, differentiation of the damped
series. The first frequency moment converges absolutely for positive N. -/

name: weighted_power_bound412_l4p111
header:
theorem weighted_power_bound412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, ((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) *
      Real.exp (-((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) ≤ 10 * N
doc:
/-- PORT of weighted_power_bound412 from Stability412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, the uniform derivative majorant.
Split the dyadic first moment at the integer logarithm of N. The initial
geometric sum is at most two N and the tail is at most eight N. -/

name: powerTrunc412_l4p111
header: noncomputable def powerTrunc412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- PORT of powerTrunc412 from Truncation412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. The finite damped polynomial contains
exactly the positive powers of two at most N. -/

name: power_trunc_error412_l4p111
header:
theorem power_trunc_error412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (α : ℝ) :
    ‖powerFourier111_up111 N α - powerTrunc412_l4p111 N α‖ ≤ 10
doc:
/-- PORT of power_trunc_error412 from Truncation412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 passage from equation 7.5 to 7.7 and page 161
7.2. The discarded dyadic tail has uniformly bounded norm. Ten is a
conservative constant from the proved first moment bound. -/

name: power_trunc_zero_lower412_l4p111
header:
theorem power_trunc_zero_lower412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Real.exp (-1) * Nat.log 2 N ≤ ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N 0‖
doc:
/-- PORT of power_trunc_zero_lower412 from Truncation412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. At zero every retained damping
weight is at least exp of negative one. Thus the finite polynomial grows
at least linearly in the integer base two logarithm of N. -/

name: large_value_to_trunc412_l4p111
header:
theorem large_value_to_trunc412_l4p111 (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ α : ℝ,
      (1 - η / 2) * ‖powerFourier111_up111 N 0‖ < ‖powerFourier111_up111 N α‖ →
      (1 - η) * ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N 0‖ < ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N α‖
doc:
/-- PORT of large_value_to_trunc412 from Truncation412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. A fixed large value margin absorbs
the bounded discarded tail once the finite polynomial at zero is large.
Only the finite polynomial remains on the right side. -/

name: nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111
header: noncomputable def nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : Finset ℕ
doc:
/-- PORT of nearIntegerIndices412 from Decomp412c, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 equation 7.11. Indices of the first M positive
powers whose phase lies within two to negative r of an integer. -/

name: dyadic_measure_scale412_l4p111
header:
theorem dyadic_measure_scale412_l4p111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (a : ℝ)
    (ha : -1 ≤ a) (ha0 : a ≤ 0) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ ((Nat.log 2 N : ℝ) * a) ≤ 2 * (N : ℝ) ^ a
doc:
/-- PORT of dyadic_measure_scale412 from Decomp412c, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 conversion from binary length to N after 7.19.
For a negative exponent a between negative one and zero, using the
integer logarithm costs at most a factor two. -/

name: adjacent_pair435_l4p111
header:
theorem adjacent_pair435_l4p111 (M : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : S ⊆ range M)
    (hcard : M + 1 < 2 * S.card) : ∃ n : ℕ, n ∈ S ∧ n + 1 ∈ S
doc:
/-- PORT of adjacent_pair435 from Phase435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 after equation 7.10. More than half of a finite
interval, with its endpoint allowance, contains an adjacent pair. -/

name: rotation_removal435_l4p111
header:
theorem rotation_removal435_l4p111 (α φ ρ : ℝ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hcluster : ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ, |α * (2 : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) - φ - z| ≤ ρ)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ S) (hn1 : n + 1 ∈ S) :
    ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ, |α * (2 : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) - z| ≤ 4 * ρ
doc:
/-- PORT of rotation_removal435 from Phase435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 the two displays after equation 7.10 and equation
7.11. If a set of dyadic phases clusters within rho of a common
rotation and contains an adjacent pair, all its phases lie within
four rho of integers. This uses no Fourier or measure estimate. -/

name: cluster_to_near_indices435_l4p111
header:
theorem cluster_to_near_indices435_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hM : 4 ≤ M) (α φ ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hS : S ⊆ range M) (hc : (1 - ε / 2) * (M : ℝ) ≤ S.card)
    (hp : ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ,
      |α * (2 : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) - φ - z| ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ r / 4) :
    (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card
doc:
/-- PORT of cluster_to_near_indices435 from Phase435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 equation 7.11. A common rotation cluster of
fraction at least one minus epsilon over two gives the required
near integer index count, once epsilon is below one half and M is
at least four. The radius is one quarter of the desired radius. -/

name: near_phase_digit_equal412_l4p111
header:
theorem near_phase_digit_equal412_l4p111 (M r m : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α : ℝ)
    (hm : m ∈ nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α) :
    LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.digit α (m + 2) =
      LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.digit α (m + 3)
doc:
/-- PORT of near_phase_digit_equal412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 after equation 7.12. A near integer doubling at
binary radius at most one sixteenth forces two adjacent binary digits
 to agree. Reuse the proved lab cosine to digit implication from P0094
page 132 Lemma 1. -/

name: changes_le_bad_indices412_l4p111
header:
theorem changes_le_bad_indices412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α : ℝ) :
    (LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.changes α M).card ≤
      M - (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card
doc:
/-- PORT of changes_le_bad_indices412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 binary run count leading to 7.13. Every change
in the interior digit string corresponds injectively to an index outside
the near integer set. This supplies the exact exceptional set needed
by the existing Gallagher finite word counting proof. -/

name: changes_fraction_bound412_l4p111
header:
theorem changes_fraction_bound412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α ε : ℝ)
    (hgood : (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card) :
    ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.changes α M).card : ℝ) ≤ ε * M
doc:
/-- PORT of changes_fraction_bound412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 equations 7.13 through 7.15. The concentration
fraction implies the corresponding real upper bound for digit changes.
The existing Gallagher count and binomial estimate can now be reused. -/

name: concentrated_word_mem412_l4p111
header:
theorem concentrated_word_mem412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (α ε : ℝ)
    (hα : α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1)
    (hgood : (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card) :
    ⌊(2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1) * α⌋₊ ∈ LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)
doc:
/-- PORT of concentrated_word_mem412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 equation 7.13 and page 165 equation 7.19.
The binary word of a concentrated phase belongs to the exact finite
word set already counted in the proved Gallagher module. -/

name: binary_cells_measure412_l4p111
header:
theorem binary_cells_measure412_l4p111 (M : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      ⌊(2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1) * α⌋₊ ∈ S} ≤
        (S.card : ENNReal) * ENNReal.ofReal (1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- PORT of binary_cells_measure412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 after equation 7.19. A finite collection of binary
words covers its phases by equal dyadic cells. Its measure is at most
the word count times their common length. -/

name: binary_unit_measure_le_words412_l4p111
header:
theorem binary_unit_measure_le_words412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (ε : ℝ) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card} ≤
        ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)).card : ENNReal) *
          ENNReal.ofReal (1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- PORT of binary_unit_measure_le_words412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 word count and page 165 conversion to measure.
The actual near integer phase set in one period is bounded by the
proved Gallagher word count at parameter epsilon over four. -/

name: near_indices_int_shift412_l4p111
header:
theorem near_indices_int_shift412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (z : ℤ) :
    nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r (α + z) = nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α
doc:
/-- PORT of near_indices_int_shift412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 binary expansion and page 165 measure bound.
Integer translation preserves the exact near integer index set.
Thus the binary concentration condition is periodic with period one. -/

name: binary_word_card_bound412_l4p111
header:
theorem binary_word_card_bound412_l4p111 (M : ℕ) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε * M) (hM : ε * M ≤ (M - 1 : ℕ)) :
    ((LeanLab.Linnik.Gallagher1975Lemma1.T M (ε / 4)).card : ℝ) ≤
      4 * (Real.exp 1 * (M - 1 : ℕ) / (ε * M)) ^ (ε * M)
doc:
/-- PORT of binary_word_card_bound412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 binomial estimate 7.15 and Gallagher page 133
counting proof. Reuse the proved finite word injection and small subset
bound to retain the explicit entropy expression before choosing epsilon. -/

name: binary_unit_measure_explicit412_l4p111
header:
theorem binary_unit_measure_explicit412_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε * M) (hM : ε * M ≤ (M - 1 : ℕ)) :
    MeasureTheory.volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (Real.exp 1 * (M - 1 : ℕ) / (ε * M)) ^ (ε * M) /
          (2 : ℝ) ^ (M + 1))
doc:
/-- PORT of binary_unit_measure_explicit412 from EntropyBridge412, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 conversion of word count to measure after 7.19.
The actual binary concentration set in one period satisfies the explicit
binomial entropy bound already proved in the Gallagher counting library.
Only the small fraction choice and bounded period extension remain. -/

name: cosine_deficit_radius435_l4p111
header:
theorem cosine_deficit_radius435_l4p111 (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ d : ℝ, 0 < d ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, 1 - Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * x) < d →
      ∃ z : ℤ, |x - z| ≤ ρ
doc:
/-- PORT of cosine_deficit_radius435 from Alignment435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 equation 7.10. For every positive radius there
is a positive cosine deficit threshold that forces distance to an
integer within that radius. Round supplies the nearest integer. -/

name: rotation_cosine435_l4p111
header:
theorem rotation_cosine435_l4p111 (u : ℂ) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (x : ℝ) :
    (u * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * x) : ℝ) * Complex.I)).re =
      Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (x - u.arg / (2 * Real.pi)))
doc:
/-- PORT of rotation_cosine435 from Alignment435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equation 7.8. A unit complex rotation is an
exponential of its argument. Multiplying a negative Fourier phase by
that rotation subtracts one common real phase inside the cosine. -/

name: weighted_deficit435_l4p111
header:
theorem weighted_deficit435_l4p111 (M : ℕ) (w θ : ℕ → ℝ) (η : ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ m ∈ range M, 0 ≤ w m ∧ w m ≤ 1)
    (hη : 0 ≤ η)
    (hlarge : (1 - η) * (∑ m ∈ range M, w m) <
      ‖∑ m ∈ range M, (w m : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * θ m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖) :
    ∃ φ : ℝ, ∑ m ∈ range M, w m *
      (1 - Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (θ m - φ))) < η * M
doc:
/-- PORT of weighted_deficit435 from Alignment435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equations 7.8 and 7.9. The weighted cosine
deficit is small when the norm of the weighted phase sum is almost
its total weight. This is the finite scalar identity before counting
exceptional indices. -/

name: weighted_bad_count435_l4p111
header:
theorem weighted_bad_count435_l4p111 (M : ℕ) (w D : ℕ → ℝ) (ε d : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hw : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range M, Real.exp (-1) ≤ w m)
    (hD : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range M, 0 ≤ D m)
    (hs : ∑ m ∈ Finset.range M, w m * D m <
      ε * d * Real.exp (-1) * M) :
    ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => d ≤ D m)).card ≤ ε * (M : ℝ)
doc:
/-- PORT of weighted_bad_count435 from Alignment435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 the exceptional index count between equations
7.8 and 7.9. Positive lower damping weights turn a small total
weighted deficit into a small number of indices above a fixed deficit.
Only finite sums and real inequalities occur here. -/

name: weighted_phase_alignment_proved435_l4p111
header:
theorem weighted_phase_alignment_proved435_l4p111 (ε ρ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 / 2 ∧ ∀ M : ℕ,
      ∀ w θ : ℕ → ℝ,
        (∀ m ∈ Finset.range M, Real.exp (-1) ≤ w m ∧ w m ≤ 1) →
        (1 - η) * (∑ m ∈ Finset.range M, w m) <
          ‖∑ m ∈ Finset.range M, (w m : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * θ m) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ →
        ∃ φ : ℝ, ∃ S : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ Finset.range M ∧
          (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ S.card ∧
          ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ, |θ m - φ - z| ≤ ρ
doc:
/-- PORT of weighted_phase_alignment_proved435 from Alignment435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 162 equations 7.8 and 7.9 through page 163 equation
7.10. The exact generic weighted alignment input follows from the
rotation identity, weighted deficit count and cosine radius bound. -/

name: finite_phase_concentration_decomposed435_l4p111
header:
theorem finite_phase_concentration_decomposed435_l4p111 (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2)
    (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ α : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 →
        (1 - η) * ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N 0‖ < ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N α‖ →
          (1 - ε) * (Nat.log 2 N : ℝ) ≤
            (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 (Nat.log 2 N) r α).card
doc:
/-- PORT of finite_phase_concentration_decomposed435 from Decomp435a, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 163 equation 7.11. Exact finite_phase_concentration412
statement, assembled from weighted alignment and the proved adjacent
pair rotation removal. Both components now have clean proofs. -/

name: entropy_fraction435_l4p111
header:
theorem entropy_fraction435_l4p111 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧
      ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2
doc:
/-- PORT of entropy_fraction435 from Entropy435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 164 equation 7.18 and page 165 equation 7.19.
The entropy cost tends to zero with the exceptional fraction.
This is the parameter choice after the binary word count. -/

name: entropy_unit_bound435_l4p111
header:
theorem entropy_unit_bound435_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) (hr : 4 ≤ r)
    (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2)
    (hcost : ε * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / ε) ≤ δ * Real.log 2) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1)))
doc:
/-- PORT of entropy_unit_bound435 from Entropy435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 after equation 7.19. The explicit finite word
bound is at most four times the prescribed dyadic measure scale once
the entropy cost is below delta log two. -/

name: entropy_three_periods435_l4p111
header:
theorem entropy_three_periods435_l4p111 (M r : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
      (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card} ≤
      3 * volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
        (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card}
doc:
/-- PORT of entropy_three_periods435 from Entropy435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 page 165 measure conclusion after equation 7.19.
Three consecutive periods cost at most three unit period measures.
Integer translation preserves the concentration predicate. -/

name: binary_entropy_measure_proved435_l4p111
header:
theorem binary_entropy_measure_proved435_l4p111 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, 4 ≤ r ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ M0 : ℕ, ∀ M : ℕ, M0 < M →
        volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
          (1 - ε) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412_l4p111 M r α).card} ≤
            C * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * (δ - 1))
doc:
/-- PORT of binary_entropy_measure_proved435 from Entropy435, same proof, renamed so that Decomp111 can use it.
 P0093 pages 164 and 165 binary word count and measure conclusion.
The exact binary_entropy_measure412 statement has a clean proof from
the proved Gallagher word count. No cited entropy input is used. -/

name: finite_large_value_measure_general_l4p111
header:
theorem finite_large_value_measure_general_l4p111 (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hκ1 : κ ≤ 1) :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ,
      ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
        volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
          (1 - η) * ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N 0‖ < ‖powerTrunc412_l4p111 N α‖} ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) ^ (κ - 1)
doc:
/-- P0093 pages 162 to 165, Lemma 4 for the finite polynomial 7.7, with the exponent
kappa of 7.6 free. Same assembly as finite_large_value_measure435 in Measure435, which is
the case kappa equal to one two hundredth: the phase concentration 7.8 to 7.11, the binary
digit and entropy count 7.12 to 7.18, and the passage from M to N after 7.18. -/

name: large_value_measure_general_l4p111
header:
theorem large_value_measure_general_l4p111 (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hκ1 : κ ≤ 1) :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ,
      ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
        volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
          (1 - 2 * η) * ‖powerFourier111_up111 N 0‖ < ‖powerFourier111_up111 N α‖} ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) ^ (κ - 1)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.6, Lemma 4, read at 2 eta as in the proof of Lemma 5 on
page 165, with the exponent kappa free. Same passage from the full series to the finite
polynomial 7.7 as large_value_measure435 in Measure435, which is the case kappa equal to
one two hundredth. -/

name: arcSystemSplit111
header: def arcSystemSplit111 (q : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) : Set ℝ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166, the system F_q of the phi of q segments of half width 2 over q tau
around the reduced fractions a over q. Rationals carry reduced numerators, so r.den
equal to q means a coprime to q. Local copy of arcSystem111 of Decomp111b, which sits
downstream of Decomp111. -/

name: system_mass_split111
header:
theorem system_mass_split111 (hG : GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∫ α in arcSystemSplit111 q ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ∩ Set.Icc 0 1,
          ‖primeFourier111_up111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤ C * (N : ℝ) ^ (93 / 100 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF under GRH. P0093 page 166 equation 9.1, obtained in the paper by a trivial
modification of the derivation of 6.4 from 3.4, so through Lemma 1, Lemma 2 and
Sections 3 to 6. For one system F_q with Q equal to N to the one tenth below q and q
at most tau equal to N to the one seventh, the integral of the squared prime series over
F_q in the unit interval is at most C times N to the 93 hundredths. Equation 9.1 gives
mu squared of q over phi of q times N over ln N plus B N ln to the 13 of N times
1 over tau plus 2 over the square root of q tau, which is N to the 0.9 plus o of 1 for
such q, so the exponent 93 hundredths leaves room for every logarithm. No cover and no
count is left in this leaf. -/

name: finite_cover_integral_split111
header:
theorem finite_cover_integral_split111 {ι : Type*} (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x)
    (s : Set ℝ) (S : Finset ι) (t : ι → Set ℝ)
    (hi : ∀ q ∈ S, IntegrableOn f (t q))
    (hcover : s ⊆ ⋃ q ∈ S, t q) :
    (∫ x in s, f x) ≤ ∑ q ∈ S, ∫ x in t q, f x
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 proof of Lemma 7, equation 9.3: a finite cover bounds the integral of
a nonnegative function by the sum of its integrals over the covering sets, which need
not be disjoint. Same proof as finite_cover_integral376 of Decomp376c, with any index
type. Proved. -/

name: dirichlet_minor_split111
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 Section 8 and page 166 Section 9: every point theta of the unit
interval has the Dirichlet form a over q plus alpha with q at most tau and alpha at most
1 over q tau. If theta is not on a major arc, then q is above Q. Proved from Mathlib
Real.exists_rat_abs_sub_le_and_den_le. -/

name: lemma6_split111
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166, Lemma 6: a segment of length N to the minus 0.99 that meets a minor
point theta lies in the single system F_q, where a over q is the Dirichlet fraction of
theta, because N to the minus 0.99 is at most 1 over q tau, as q tau is at most tau
squared, N to the two sevenths. Proved. -/

name: logConvolution1622_lc111
header: noncomputable def logConvolution1622_lc111 (n : ℕ) : ℝ
doc:
/-- PORT of logConvolution1622 from SPLIT1622_major, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. The sum of 1 over ln m ln m' over m + m' = n
with both at least 2. It is empty for n below 4. -/

name: logConvolution_four1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConvolution_four1622_lc111 :
    logConvolution1622_lc111 4 = 1 / (Real.log 2 * Real.log 2)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConvolution_four1622 from SPLIT1622_major, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 Vacuity instance: at n equal to 4 the convolution is the single term at m equal to 2. -/

name: log_two_pos1622_lc111
header: private lemma log_two_pos1622_lc111 : 0 < Real.log 2
doc: /-- PORT of log_two_pos1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof. -/

name: log_four_eq1622_lc111
header: private lemma log_four_eq1622_lc111 : Real.log 4 = 2 * Real.log 2
doc: /-- PORT of log_four_eq1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof. -/

name: log_three_le1622_lc111
header: private lemma log_three_le1622_lc111 : Real.log 3 ≤ 2 * Real.log 2 - 1 / 4
doc:
/-- PORT of log_three_le1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 `log 3` is at most `2 log 2 - 1/4`, from `log (3/4) ≤ 3/4 - 1`. -/

name: log_five_ge1622_lc111
header: private lemma log_five_ge1622_lc111 : 2 * Real.log 2 + 1 / 5 ≤ Real.log 5
doc:
/-- PORT of log_five_ge1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 `log 5` is at least `2 log 2 + 1/5`, from `1 - 1/x ≤ log x` at `x = 5/4`. -/

name: log_six_ge1622_lc111
header: private lemma log_six_ge1622_lc111 : 5 / 2 * Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log 6
doc:
/-- PORT of log_six_ge1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 `log 6` is at least `(5/2) log 2`, because `4 * sqrt 2 ≤ 6`. -/

name: exp_seven_ge1622_lc111
header: private lemma exp_seven_ge1622_lc111 : (1000 : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp 7
doc:
/-- PORT of exp_seven_ge1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 `1000 ≤ exp 7`. -/

name: logConv_main_le1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_main_le1622_lc111 (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) :
    (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ logConvolution1622_lc111 n
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_main_le1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. Scale control, main term is dominated: from n equal to 4 upwards the
convolution sum is at least n / (log n)^2. The sum has about n terms each of size
about 1 / (log n)^2, and this leaf asserts only the one-sided floor, with no error
term. It is the step that removes the absolute value in the large range. -/

name: logConv_small_range1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_small_range1622_lc111 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ 1000 →
      |logConvolution1622_lc111 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
        B * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_small_range1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. The finite range: for 2 <= n <= 10^3 the whole claim of the target holds
with one constant, in absolute value and with the relative weight 1/sqrt(log n).
Finitely many cases and no asymptotic content. -/

name: logConv_log_cube_split1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_log_cube_split1622_lc111 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 3 = ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.log n)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_log_cube_split1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. The power identity that turns the excess into the relative weight:
n / (log n)^3 is n / (log n)^2 times 1 / log n, for every n at least 2, where the
logarithm does not vanish. -/

name: logConv_recip_log_le_sqrt1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_recip_log_le_sqrt1622_lc111 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1000 ≤ n) :
    1 / Real.log n ≤ 1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_recip_log_le_sqrt1622 from SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. The logarithmic weight comparison: for n at least 10^3 the logarithm is at
least one, so 1 / log n is at most 1 / sqrt(log n). This is what converts the
second order excess into the exact weight of the target. -/

name: logConv_shift_nonneg1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_shift_nonneg1622_lc111 (n m : ℕ) (hm : m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)) :
    0 ≤ 2 * Real.log (n : ℝ) - (Real.log m + Real.log (n - m : ℕ))
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_shift_nonneg1622 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. Positivity of the shift: for every index of the convolution the logarithm
of m (n - m) is at most twice the logarithm of n, that is the shift 2 log n minus
log m minus log (n - m) is nonnegative. This is the step that lets the shift be
weight summed over the range without a sign condition. -/

name: logConv_shift_sum1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_shift_sum1622_lc111 :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1000 ≤ n →
      (∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2),
          (2 * Real.log (n : ℝ) - (Real.log m + Real.log (n - m : ℕ))))
        ≤ K * (n : ℝ)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_shift_sum1622 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. Total of the shift: summed over the whole range 2 <= m <= n - 2 the shift
2 log n - log m - log (n - m) is at most a constant times n. The shift is the
logarithm of n^2 / (m (n - m)), and the sum of the logarithms is read off a lower
bound for the logarithm of the factorial (n - 2)!, so the constant is absolute. -/

name: logConv_middle_shift1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_middle_shift1622_lc111 (n m : ℕ) (hn : 1000 ≤ n)
    (hm1 : 2 * Nat.sqrt n ≤ m) (hm2 : m ≤ n - 2 * Nat.sqrt n) :
    2 * Real.log (n : ℝ) - (Real.log m + Real.log (n - m : ℕ)) ≤ Real.log (n : ℝ) / 2
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_middle_shift1622 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. Small shift in the middle of the range: for n at least 10^3 and for an
index m with 2 sqrt n <= m <= n - 2 sqrt n the product m (n - m) is at least
n^(3/2), so the shift 2 log n - log m - log (n - m) is at most half of log n. This
is the step that makes the termwise majorant applicable away from the two ends. -/

name: logConv_end_mass1622_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_end_mass1622_lc111 :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1000 ≤ n →
      (∑ m ∈ (Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)).filter
          (fun m => ¬ (2 * Nat.sqrt n ≤ m ∧ m ≤ n - 2 * Nat.sqrt n)),
          1 / (Real.log m * Real.log (n - m : ℕ)))
        ≤ K * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ 3)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_end_mass1622 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 LEAF. Mass of the two ends: summed over the indices m of the range which fail
2 sqrt n <= m <= n - 2 sqrt n, that is over the two ends of the range, the summand
1 / (log m log (n - m)) is at most a constant times n / (log n)^3. Each such index
has both logarithms at least half of log n, and there are at most 4 sqrt n of them. -/

name: logConv_term_majorant_bounded474_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_term_majorant_bounded474_lc111 (u v L : ℝ) (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v)
    (hL : 0 < L) (huL : u ≤ L) (hvL : v ≤ L)
    (hshift : 2 * L - (u + v) ≤ L / 2) :
    1 / (u * v) ≤ 1 / L ^ 2 + (2 / L ^ 3) * (2 * L - (u + v))
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_term_majorant_bounded474 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 The valid termwise estimate includes the upper bounds on both logarithms.
These hold for convolution indices on page 161 after equation 6.3. -/

name: logConv_excess_corrected474_lc111
header:
theorem logConv_excess_corrected474_lc111 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1000 ≤ n →
      logConvolution1622_lc111 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ C * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 3)
doc:
/-- PORT of logConv_excess_corrected474 from SPLIT_logConv_excess1622, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 The convolution excess estimate from the bounded majorant. This proof
uses the two logarithm upper bounds and avoids the false sealed annotation. -/

name: log_convolution_estimate487_lc111
header:
theorem log_convolution_estimate487_lc111 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → |logConvolution1622_lc111 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤ B * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- PORT of log_convolution_estimate487 from Decomp487c, same proof, renamed so that Major81Split111 can use it.
 P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3. Exact relative convolution estimate from the corrected bounded majorant. No use of the refuted unbounded majorant. -/

name: tuple_cons_prod_split111
header:
theorem tuple_cons_prod_split111 {R : Type*} [CommMonoid R] (f : ℕ → R) (k : ℕ)
    (x : ℕ × (Fin k → ℕ)) :
    (fun ν : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ => ∏ i, f (ν i)) (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (k + 1) => ℕ) x) =
      f x.1 * ∏ i, f (x.2 i)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1, the expansion of T to the k: splitting the first exponent
off a tuple of k plus 1 exponents. Proved. -/

name: summable_tuple_prod_real_split111
header:
theorem summable_tuple_prod_real_split111 (g : ℕ → ℝ) (hg0 : ∀ m, 0 ≤ g m)
    (hg : Summable g) (k : ℕ) : Summable (fun ν : Fin k → ℕ => ∏ i, g (ν i))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1: for a summable nonnegative family, the products over
tuples of k exponents are summable. Proved by induction on k. -/

name: hasSum_tuple_prod_split111
header:
theorem hasSum_tuple_prod_split111 (f : ℕ → ℂ) (hf : Summable (fun m => ‖f m‖)) (k : ℕ) :
    HasSum (fun ν : Fin k → ℕ => ∏ i, f (ν i)) ((∑' m, f m) ^ k)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1: an absolutely summable series raised to the k is the sum
over all tuples x_1 to x_k of the products of its terms. Proved by induction on k with
Mathlib HasSum.mul. -/

name: arc_tuple_expand_split111
header:
theorem arc_tuple_expand_split111 (k N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (s : Set ℝ) (hs : s ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1) :
    HasSum (fun ν : Fin k → ℕ =>
      (((∏ i, Real.exp (-((2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ α in s, primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * ((N : ℝ) - ∑ i, ((2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
            Complex.I))
      (∫ α in s, primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 * powerFourier111_up111 N α ^ k *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * N) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1, first step: on any part s of the unit interval, the
integral of S squared times T to the k times e of N alpha is the sum over all tuples of
exponents of the tuple weight, the product of the e to the minus 2 to the x_i over N,
times the integral of S squared times e of N_1 alpha, with N_1 equal to N minus the sum of
the 2 to the x_i, here x_i equal to nu i plus 1. Exchange of sum and integral by dominated
convergence, with dominating function S squared times the tuple weight. Proved. -/

name: polylog_small_m111
header:
theorem polylog_small_m111 (j : ℕ) {c A ε : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → A * Real.log N ^ j ≤ ε * (N : ℝ) ^ c
doc:
/-- Copy of polylog_small_split111 of Decomp111, same proof, for use upstream of it.
P0093 pages 166 and 168: a constant times a fixed power of ln N is eventually below
epsilon times a fixed positive power of N. Proved. -/

name: inv_sqrt_sum_le_split111
header:
theorem inv_sqrt_sum_le_split111 (Q : ℕ) :
    ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 Q, 1 / Real.sqrt q ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt Q
doc:
/-- Helper for P0093 page 166 equation 8.2: the sum of 1 over the square root of q for q
from 1 to Q is at most 2 times the square root of Q. Proved by induction. -/

name: error_sum_82_split111
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 8.2 with the parameters of page 165, tau equal to N to the one
seventh and Q equal to N to the one tenth: the sum over q at most Q of the error factor
1 over tau plus 1 over the square root of q tau from 6.4 is at most 3 times N to the minus
3 over 140, the printed N to the minus 1 over 68 up to the exponent. Proved. This is the
computation behind the resolution of the burst 9 QUESTION in the p3 note. -/

name: system_bound_91_split111
header:
theorem system_bound_91_split111 (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ,
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ) *
            ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N) +
          B * N * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) + 2 / Real.sqrt (q * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) ≤
          5 * (N : ℝ) ^ (93 / 100 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.1, read for one system F_q with q between Q equal to N to the
one tenth and tau equal to N to the one seventh: the right side of 9.1, mu squared of q
over phi of q times N over ln N plus B N ln to the 13 of N times 1 over tau plus 2 over the
square root of q tau, is at most 5 times N to the 93 hundredths for large N. So the leaf
system_mass_split111 of Lemma6Split111 is a consequence of 9.1. Proved, with the lab bound
q over phi of q at most 2 times 1 plus ln q of Perelli1996 TotientRatio320. -/

name: r1_absorb_split111
header:
theorem r1_absorb_split111 (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B) (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      B * (Real.log N / Real.log 2 + 2) ^ k * N * Real.log N ^ 13 *
          (3 * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(3 / 140 : ℝ))) ≤ ε * scale111_up111 k N
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 8.2 and page 168, the absorption of R_1 into the scale of
Section 11: with at most ln N over ln 2 plus 2 to the k in tuple weight, as in the count
of the N_1 on page 166, and the summed error N ln to the 13 of N times 3 N to the minus
3 over 140 of error_sum_82_split111, the total is eventually below any epsilon times
scale111 for every k at least 3. Proved. With the paper's parameters, so the lab tau, the
error accounting of 8.1 and 8.2 therefore fits inside major_truncated_split111. -/

name: truncSingular_m111
header: noncomputable def truncSingular_m111 (Q n : ℕ) : ℝ
doc: /-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6 left side. Local copy of truncSingular111 of Decomp111. -/

name: logConv_m111
header: noncomputable def logConv_m111 (n : ℕ) : ℝ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3: the sum of 1 over ln m ln m prime over m plus m
prime equal to n with both at least 2, empty for n below 4. Local copy of
logConvolution1622 of SPLIT1622_major. -/

name: major_local_expansion_m111
header:
theorem major_local_expansion_m111 (hG : GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
      ‖(∫ α in majorArcs280_up111 N, primeFourier111_up111 N α ^ 2 *
            Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * α * (n : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) -
          (((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * truncSingular_m111 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ n.toNat *
            logConv_m111 n.toNat) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
        B * N * Real.log N ^ 13 * ∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊,
          (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) + 1 / Real.sqrt (q * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- CONDITIONAL under GRH on the three local analytic leaves of Decomp520a.
P0093 page 161 equation 6.4, from 3.4, 5.4, 5.5 and
6.3 on pages 156 and 159 to 161, for each q at most Q equal to N to the one tenth, summed over the
disjoint arcs of the major arcs as in 8.1 on page 165, at one residual n, uniformly in n.
The main term keeps the exact convolution of 6.3 and the damping e to the minus n over N,
which the printed e to the minus 1 absorbs together with the tuple weight; it is zero for
n below 4. The error is B N ln to the 13 of N times the sum over q at most Q of 1 over
tau plus 1 over the square root of q tau, as on the original scan pages 161 and 165, with
tau equal to N to the one seventh. -/

name: tuple_sum_even_m111
header: theorem tuple_sum_even_m111 {k : ℕ} (ν : Fin k → ℕ) : Even (∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165, the N_1 of 8.1 are even: a sum of powers 2 to the x with x at least 1
is even. Proved. -/

name: mainTermTrunc_reindex_m111
header:
theorem mainTermTrunc_reindex_m111 (k N Q : ℕ) (hN : Even N) (hN1 : 1 ≤ N) :
    mainTermTrunc_m111 k N Q =
      ∑ ν ∈ (Fintype.piFinset fun _ : Fin k => Finset.range N).filter
          (fun ν => 2 + ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1) ≤ N),
        truncSingular_m111 Q (N - ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1)) *
          ((N - ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / Real.log ((N - ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1 and page 168 equation 10.7: the main term of Decomp111,
indexed by tuples in Fin of N plus 1 with exponents at least 1, rewritten over tuples of
naturals nu with x_i equal to nu i plus 1 and N_1 at least 2; evenness of N_1 is automatic
for even N. Proved. -/

name: truncSingular_small_m111
header:
theorem truncSingular_small_m111 (ε0 : ℝ) (hε0 : 0 < ε0) :
    ∃ C0 : ℝ, 0 < C0 ∧ ∀ Q n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      |truncSingular_m111 Q n| ≤ ε0 * Real.log n + C0
doc:
/-- PROVED in burst 8 p3, formerly a leaf. P0093 page 168, after equation 10.6, the size of the truncated
singular series, in the form 10.7 needs: for every epsilon_0 there is C_0 with the
truncated series at any level Q and any n at least 1 at most epsilon_0 ln n plus C_0. It
follows from the classical bound: the Ramanujan sum at a squarefree q is at most the gcd
of q and n in size, so the series is at most the product over p of 1 plus gcd of p and n
over p minus 1 squared, a constant times n over phi of n, which is at most a constant
times ln ln n by Landau. The paper uses instead an absolute upper bound c_1 for the
singular series at even N_1, which fails; see the QUESTION in the p3 note. -/

name: logConv_dev_m111
header:
theorem logConv_dev_m111 :
    ∃ K0 C1 : ℝ, 0 < K0 ∧ 0 < C1 ∧ ∀ N m : ℕ, 4 ≤ m → m ≤ N →
      |logConv_m111 m - (m : ℝ) / Real.log m ^ 2| ≤
        K0 + C1 * (Real.sqrt N + 8 * (N : ℝ) / Real.log N ^ 3)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 161 after equation 6.3: for 4 at most m at most N, the convolution
differs from m over ln squared m by at most K_0 plus C_1 times the square root of N plus
8 N over ln cubed N. From the ported clean lab estimates, the finite range bound for m
below 1000 and the excess bound C m over ln cubed m above. Proved. -/

name: major_main_sum_m111
header:
theorem major_main_sum_m111 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N0 < N →
      |∑ ν ∈ (Fintype.piFinset fun _ : Fin k => Finset.range N).filter
            (fun ν => 4 + ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1) ≤ N),
          truncSingular_m111 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ (N - ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1)) *
            logConv_m111 (N - ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i + 1)) -
        mainTermTrunc_m111 k N ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊| ≤ ε * scale111_up111 k N
doc:
/-- SPLIT burst 8 p3, PROVED, through truncSingular_small_m111. P0093 page 165
equation 8.1 and page 168 equations 10.6 and 10.7, the arithmetic left of the bookkeeping
once the GRH errors are summed: over the tuples of exponents x_i equal to nu i plus 1 with
N_1, N minus the sum of the 2 to the x_i, at least 4, the sum of the truncated singular
series at N_1 times the exact convolution of 6.3 at N_1 is the main term with N_1 over
ln squared N_1 up to epsilon times the scale. The proof reindexes the main term by
mainTermTrunc_reindex_m111, bounds the convolution error by logConv_dev_m111 from the
ported clean lab estimates of LogConvPort111, bounds the tuples with N_1 equal to 2 or 3
directly, and counts at most ln N over ln 2 to the k tuples. -/

name: major_bookkeeping_m111
header:
theorem major_bookkeeping_m111 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N0 < N → ∀ J : ℝ → ℂ,
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
        ‖J n - (((Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / N) * truncSingular_m111 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ n.toNat *
            logConv_m111 n.toNat) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          B * N * Real.log N ^ 13 * ∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊,
            (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) + 1 / Real.sqrt (q * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))) →
      |Real.exp 1 * (∑' ν : Fin k → ℕ,
          (((∏ i, Real.exp (-((2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
            J ((N : ℝ) - ∑ i, ((2 ^ (ν i + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ))).re -
        mainTermTrunc_m111 k N ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊| ≤ ε * scale111_up111 k N
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 equation 8.1, page 166 equation 8.2 and page 168 equation 10.7. Given
any function J of the residual that satisfies the local expansion of
major_local_expansion_m111 at every integer residual at most N, the tuple sum of 8.1,
e times the real part of the sum over tuples of the tuple weight times J at N_1, is the
main term with the truncated singular series at Q equal to N to the one tenth up to
epsilon times the scale. Proved, through major_main_sum_m111: e times the tuple
weight times e to the minus N_1 over N is 1, the main terms vanish for N_1 below 4, and
the errors sum to at most the tuple weight sum, at most ln N over ln 2 plus 2 to the k,
times the 8.2 error, which r1_absorb_split111 absorbs. -/

name: reciprocal_totient435
header:
theorem reciprocal_totient435 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    1 / (q.totient : ℝ) ≤ 2 / Real.sqrt q
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 after equation 9.3. The elementary square root
lower bound for the totient gives a reciprocal denominator bound.
Reuse the proved lab bound from P0083 page 484 equation 17. -/

name: system_principal_bound435
header:
theorem system_principal_bound435 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hlog : 1 ≤ Real.log N) (hq : (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) ≤ q) :
    (N : ℝ) / q.totient / Real.log N ≤ 2 * (N : ℝ) ^ (19 / 20 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.1 and its use in 9.3. For q at least
N to one tenth the principal term is at most twice N to nineteen
twentieths, once log N is at least one. -/

name: system_reciprocal_bound435
header:
theorem system_reciprocal_bound435 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
      2 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ≤
        3 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 14 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.1. Dropping q from the square root
error denominator costs only a weaker power saving. Both reciprocal
terms are bounded by three times N to negative one fourteenth. -/

name: log_power_small435
header:
theorem log_power_small435 (k : ℕ) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → Real.log N ^ k ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ a
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.3. An arbitrary fixed logarithmic
power is eventually below any prescribed positive power of N.
This packages the real logarithmic absorption already used in the lab. -/

name: system_expression_bound435
header:
theorem system_expression_bound435 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hlog : 1 ≤ Real.log N) (hq : (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) ≤ q) :
    (N : ℝ) / q.totient / Real.log N +
      (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
        (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
          2 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) ≤
      5 * (N : ℝ) ^ (19 / 20 : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13
doc:
/-- P0093 page 166 equation 9.1 through 9.3. The explicit local
main term and error are bounded by five times N to nineteen twentieths
 times the thirteenth power of log N. The square root totient bound
suffices for this weaker saving. -/

name: finite_large_value_measure435
header:
theorem finite_large_value_measure435 :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 / 2 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ,
      ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →

name: large_value_measure435
header:
theorem large_value_measure435 :

name: large_value_intervals435
header:
theorem large_value_intervals435 :

name: exp_decay_cubic_integrable473

theorem exp_decay_cubic_integrable473 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :

makes the cubic absolute value weight integrable on the whole real line. -/

name: gamma_vertical_integrable473
header:
theorem gamma_vertical_integrable473 (σ : ℝ) (hlo : 1 / 2 ≤ σ) (hhi : σ ≤ 3 / 2) :

doc:
/-- P0093 page 157 Gamma decay. Gamma is integrable on every vertical line
in the closed strip from one half to three halves. -/

name: inverse_mellin_gamma_of_vertical473

    (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    mellinInv σ Complex.Gamma x = (Real.exp (-x) : ℂ)

is the exponential whenever the vertical Gamma integral is integrable. -/

name: inverse_mellin_gamma473
header:
theorem inverse_mellin_gamma473 (σ : ℝ) (hlo : 1 / 2 ≤ σ) (hhi : σ ≤ 3 / 2)
    (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    mellinInv σ Complex.Gamma x = (Real.exp (-x) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 scalar supply. Mellin inversion of Gamma
is the exponential throughout the strip used by the shifted contour. -/

name: mellin_single_exponential473
header:
theorem mellin_single_exponential473 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    mellinU1622 N (fun t => (a : ℂ) ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t))) 0 =
      (Real.exp (-a / N) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 scalar supply. At phase zero the Mellin
kernel applied to one positive exponential frequency gives its damping factor. -/

name: gamma_real_kernel_integrable473
header:
theorem gamma_real_kernel_integrable473 (σ : ℝ) (hV : Complex.VerticalIntegrable Complex.Gamma σ)
    (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => (x : ℂ) ^ (-((σ : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) *
      Complex.Gamma ((σ : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 scalar supply. The real positive Mellin
kernel is integrable whenever Gamma is vertically integrable. -/

name: inverse_mellin_finite_gamma473
header:
theorem inverse_mellin_finite_gamma473 {ι : Type*} (σ : ℝ)
    (hlo : 1 / 2 ≤ σ) (hhi : σ ≤ 3 / 2) (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → ℝ) (c : ι → ℂ)
    (ha : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < a i) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    mellinInv σ (fun z => Complex.Gamma z * ∑ i ∈ s, c i * (a i : ℂ) ^ (-z)) x =
      ∑ i ∈ s, c i * (Real.exp (-(x * a i)) : ℂ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 finite truncation supply. Mellin inversion
of a finite character style exponential sum evaluates every positive frequency
with its exponential damping. No infinite sum interchange occurs. -/

name: mixed_character_mass442
header:
theorem mixed_character_mass442 (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          (∫ α in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))..
              (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))),
            ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N α‖ *
              ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖) ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 7
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.3, weakened to log power seven using
the elementary principal mass bound two N. The printed log power six
uses the stronger prime counting bound N over log N. CONDITIONAL on
the explicit MellinBound280 input. No additional analytic leaf is used. -/

name: LowBitsRep
header: def LowBitsRep (θ : ℝ) (k N : ℕ) : Prop
doc:
/-- `N = p + q + 2^{ν₁} + … + 2^{ν_k}` with primes `p, q`, every `ν i ≥ 1`, every `2^{ν i} ≤ N^θ`.
Twin: `N` is a sum of two primes and exactly `k` powers of two, each power at most `N^θ`. -/

name: lowBitsRep_exact
header: theorem lowBitsRep_exact {θ : ℝ} {k N : ℕ} (h : LowBitsRep θ k N) : LinnikExact k N
doc: /-- A restricted representation is a representation of Linnik's kind. -/

name: lowBitsRep_instance
header: theorem lowBitsRep_instance : LowBitsRep (3 / 4) 1 16
doc: /-- Vacuity instance for `LowBitsRep` at a θ in the range: `16 = 7 + 7 + 2^1` and `2 ≤ 16^(3/4) = 8`. -/

name: linnik_low_bits
header:
theorem linnik_low_bits (_hG : GRH) :
    ∀ θ : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ → θ < 1 → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, k₀ ≤ k → AllLargeEven (LowBitsRep θ k)
doc:
/-- LEAF. OPEN. Unit U-1620. Twin: assume GRH. For every real θ with 1/2 < θ < 1 there is `k₀` such that
for every `k ≥ k₀`, every sufficiently large even `N` is two primes plus exactly `k` powers of two, each
power at most `N^θ`. So `N` reaches a Goldbach number by changing about `k` of its low θ log₂ N bits.
Source of the claim: research/novelty/Linnik1951-20261102T1240Z.md section 6 Result 5. Compare P0093 page
154, equation 2.1, where the exponents are free. Route to try: pages 164 and 165, Lemmas 4 and 5, where
the measure bound `N^{ε(η) - 1}` for the set where `|T|` is large must be redone for a sum of θ log₂ N
terms, and it can then be no smaller than about `N^{-θ}`. GRH is not satisfiable here by an instance;
`lowBitsRep_instance` shows the conclusion's predicate holds at one point. -/

name: entropy_cost_explicit435
header:
theorem entropy_cost_explicit435 :
    (1 / 1048576 : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.exp 1 / (1 / 1048576 : ℝ)) ≤
      (1 / 200 : ℝ) * Real.log 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 the small entropy exponent choice after 7.19.
The explicit fraction two to negative twenty has entropy cost below
one two hundredth times log two. This is a parameter consequence,
not a constant printed in the paper. -/

name: binary_unit_explicit_fraction435
header:
theorem binary_unit_explicit_fraction435 (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) :
    volume {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧
      (1 - (1 / 1048576 : ℝ)) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M 4 α).card} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * ((1 / 200 : ℝ) - 1)))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 measure conclusion after 7.19. At radius one
sixteenth and exceptional fraction two to negative twenty, the one
period concentration set has measure at most four times two to M
times one two hundredth minus one for every M at least two. -/

name: binary_three_period_explicit435
header:
theorem binary_three_period_explicit435 (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) :
    volume.real {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 2 ∧
      (1 - (1 / 1048576 : ℝ)) * (M : ℝ) ≤ (nearIntegerIndices412 M 4 α).card} ≤
        12 * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((M : ℝ) * ((1 / 200 : ℝ) - 1))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 measure conclusion after 7.19. The same explicit
fraction and radius give the three period real measure bound with
constant twelve. The concentration set has positive measure for every
finite M by binary_set_positive_measure412. -/

name: power_exceeds_relative_log435
header:
theorem power_exceeds_relative_log435 (C a : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      C * Real.sqrt (Real.log N) < (N : ℝ) ^ a
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7, audit of a proposed majorant.
Replacing the singular factor by any fixed positive power of N does
not give a negligible relative correction after division by the
square root of log N. Every such power eventually exceeds any fixed
constant times that square root. This is a bound comparison only. -/

name: small_power_not_relative_decay439
header:
theorem small_power_not_relative_decay439 (a C : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hC : 0 < C) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      C < (N : ℝ) ^ a / Real.sqrt (Real.log N)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7, comparison of candidate bounds.
A positive power upper bound does not become small after division by
the square root of a logarithm. The ratio exceeds every positive
constant eventually. This does not assert that the paper estimate fails. -/

name: interval_packing412
header:
theorem interval_packing412 (s t : Set ℝ) (hs : s ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1)
    (ht : volume t ≠ ⊤) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hthick : ∀ x ∈ s, Set.Icc (x - δ) (x + δ) ⊆ t) :
    ∃ I : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), (I.card : ℝ) * δ ≤ volume.real t ∧
      (∀ p ∈ I, p.2 - p.1 ≤ δ) ∧ s ⊆ ⋃ p ∈ I, Set.Icc p.1 p.2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, the measure divided by length step.
A set in the unit interval with radius delta neighborhoods in a finite
measure set has a finite interval cover of length delta and cardinality
at most the larger measure divided by delta. -/

name: adjacent_pair435
header:
theorem adjacent_pair435 (M : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : S ⊆ range M)

doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 after equation 7.10. More than half of a finite
interval, with its endpoint allowance, contains an adjacent pair. -/

name: rotation_removal435
header:
theorem rotation_removal435 (α φ ρ : ℝ) (S : Finset ℕ)
    (hcluster : ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ, |α * (2 : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) - φ - z| ≤ ρ)

/-- P0093 page 163 the two displays after equation 7.10 and equation
7.11. If a set of dyadic phases clusters within rho of a common
rotation and contains an adjacent pair, all its phases lie within
four rho of integers. This uses no Fourier or measure estimate. -/

name: cluster_to_near_indices435
header:
theorem cluster_to_near_indices435 (M r : ℕ) (hM : 4 ≤ M) (α φ ε : ℝ)

    (hS : S ⊆ range M) (hc : (1 - ε / 2) * (M : ℝ) ≤ S.card)
    (hp : ∀ m ∈ S, ∃ z : ℤ,

doc:
/-- P0093 page 163 equation 7.11. A common rotation cluster of
fraction at least one minus epsilon over two gives the required
near integer index count, once epsilon is below one half and M is
at least four. The radius is one quarter of the desired radius. -/

name: phase_distance_deficit439

doc:

theorem unit_square_deficit439 (w z : ℂ) (hw : ‖w‖ = 1) (hz : ‖z‖ = 1) :

/-- P0093 page 163 consecutive phase comparison before equation 7.11.
For unit phases, the distance from z to one is controlled by the two
rotated deficits at z and z squared. This avoids choosing a good pair. -/

name: consecutive_phase_deficit_sum439

theorem consecutive_phase_deficit_sum439 (M : ℕ) (w : ℂ) (hw : ‖w‖ = 1)

/-- P0093 page 163 passage to equation 7.11. Summing the consecutive
phase comparison controls all unrotated deficits. The last phase costs
at most two and each rotated deficit occurs at most twice. -/

The sum over primes beyond a positive integer cutoff K is at most
two over K, by the injective map p to p minus one and the natural tail. -/

/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6, large prime part. For a positive
integer n and cutoff Y at least three and at least log n, the odd
prime factor product beyond Y is bounded by exp of two over log two.
Each local factor is bounded by exp of two over Y. -/

name: odd_prime_product_log_cutoff442

name: prime_reciprocal_square_cutoff439

name: outer_kernel_scaled_decay487
