name: character_integral_le
header:
private lemma character_integral_le (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (a : ℝ) :
    (∫ z in a..(a + 1), ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
      2000 * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N)
doc: /-- Mean square of any character series over an interval of length one. -/

name: doubled_system_characters435
header:
theorem doubled_system_characters435 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (τ : ℝ), 1 ≤ N → 2 ≤ q → 4 ≤ τ →
      (∫ α in arcSystem111 q τ ∩ Set.Icc 0 1, ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
        B / (q.totient : ℝ) *
          ((∫ z in -(2 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))..(2 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)),
              ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) +
            (∑ χ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
              ∫ z in -(2 / ((q : ℝ) * τ))..(2 / ((q : ℝ) * τ)),
                ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2)) +
        B * (2 / τ) * Real.log N ^ 6
doc:
/-- LEAF. The character orthogonality chain of page 160 before equation 5.4
applied to the square norm on one doubled system: the square integral over the
system in the unit interval is at most a constant over the totient of q times the
principal square integral over the doubled interval of radius two over q tau, plus
the same constant over the totient of q times the sum of the nonprincipal square
integrals over that interval, plus a constant times two over tau times the sixth
power of log N from the section two error. Unconditional, for any modulus q at
least two and any tau at least four. -/

name: principal_mass435
header:
theorem principal_mass435 :
    ∃ P : ℝ, 0 < P ∧ ∀ (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (r : ℝ), 3 ≤ N → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 / 2 →
      (∫ z in -r..r, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
        P * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N)
doc:
/-- LEAF. The principal square mass of page 159 before equation 5.3 with the
logarithmic saving: for the trivial character the square integral over any
interval of radius at most one half is at most a constant times N over log N.
This is the full period square sum, so the saving is the reciprocal of log N and
no power of N is lost. Unconditional, for every modulus. -/

name: nonprincipal_sum435
header:
theorem nonprincipal_sum435 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ X : ℝ, 0 < X ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 2 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∑ χ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
            ∫ z in -(2 / R)..(2 / R), ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
          X * (q.totient : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 13)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Page 159 equation 5.2 summed over the nonprincipal characters, under
the hypothesis of page 154: the sum of the nonprincipal square integrals over an
interval of radius two over R is at most a constant times the totient of q times
N over R times the thirteenth power of log N, for R between one and N to the two
sevenths. This is the Mellin estimate alone, with no integral over the doubled
system and no prime square mass. -/

name: one_denominator_mass435
header:
theorem one_denominator_mass435 :
    ∃ Q : ℝ, 0 < Q ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      (∫ α in arcSystem111 1 ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ∩ Set.Icc 0 1,
        ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤ Q * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Page 166 equation 9.1 at denominator one, the case the character chain
cannot reach because the totient of one has no nonprincipal character. The
square integral over the single doubled system of denominator one is at most a
constant times N over log N. Unconditional. -/

name: expansion_absorb435
header:
private theorem expansion_absorb435 (B P X Q : ℝ) (N q : ℕ)
    (hB : 0 < B) (hP : 0 < P) (hX : 0 < X) (hQ : 0 < Q)
    (hN3 : 3 ≤ N) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hlog : 1 ≤ Real.log N)
    (h2B : 2 * B ≤ (B * P + B * X + 2 * B + Q) * (N : ℝ)) :
    B / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (P * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N) +
          X * (q.totient : ℝ) *
            ((N : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 13)) +
      B * (2 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 6 ≤
      (B * P + B * X + 2 * B + Q) *
        ((N : ℝ) / q.totient / Real.log N +
          (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
              2 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))))
doc:
/-- Page 166 equation 9.1 at a modulus at least two. With the radius two over
q tau, the principal and nonprincipal supplies inserted and the constants of the
split, the local expression is at most the printed principal totient term plus
the printed error term. Pure real arithmetic: each of the three pieces is at
most its own term once N exceeds the constant scale of the split. -/

name: doubled_system_expansion435_split
header:
theorem doubled_system_expansion435_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∫ α in arcSystem111 q ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) ∩ Set.Icc 0 1,
          ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
          C * ((N : ℝ) / q.totient / Real.log N +
            (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
              (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) +
                2 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))))
doc:
/-- Page 166 equation 9.1. The exact statement of
doubled_system_expansion435, proved from the four supplies above without using
it. -/

name: exceptional_cover357
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of the exceptional set analysis: the rational arc cover and its
weight. For one absolute positive threshold, every point of the exceptional set
lies on a short arc around a rational written in lowest terms, whose denominator
is at most N to the one seventh and whose half width is the reciprocal of that
denominator times N to the one seventh. The covering rationals carry total
reciprocal weight that gains the power saving one twentieth over the trivial
weight N to the one seventh of all rationals of that size. This is the covering
and counting input only: it carries no integral and no hypothesis. -/

name: local_prime_mass357
header:
theorem local_prime_mass357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ a : ℤ, ¬ ((q : ℤ) ∣ a) →
          (∫ α in Set.Icc ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) - 1 / ((q : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))))
              ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) + 1 / ((q : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))),
            ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
          B * (N : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) * Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ 13
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of the exceptional set analysis: the mass of the primes on one
short arc. At a rational with denominator one at most q not dividing the
numerator, the square mean of the damped prime series over the arc of half width
the reciprocal of q times N to the one seventh is at most a constant times N
divided by both q and N to the one seventh, with a fixed power of the logarithm
of N. This is one arc only, not the whole exceptional set, and it excludes the
principal arcs where the mean is of size N. -/

name: cover_sum_bound_wip
header:
private theorem cover_sum_bound_wip (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) (hfn : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x)
    (s : Set ℝ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hsb : s ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1)
    (F : Finset (ℕ × ℤ)) (lo hi : ℕ × ℤ → ℝ)
    (hsub : s ⊆ ⋃ p ∈ F, Set.Icc (lo p) (hi p)) :
    (∫ x in s, f x) ≤ ∑ p ∈ F, ∫ x in Set.Icc (lo p) (hi p), f x
doc:
/-- The measure theory core: for a nonnegative continuous `f`, the mass over a set covered by
finitely many closed arcs is at most the sum of the masses of the arcs. -/

name: cover_mass_summation357
header:
theorem cover_mass_summation357 (N : ℕ) (η : ℝ) (F : Finset (ℕ × ℤ)) (B : ℝ)
    (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hq : ∀ p ∈ F, 1 ≤ p.1)
    (hcover : exceptionalArcs280 N η ⊆
      ⋃ p ∈ F, Set.Icc ((p.2 : ℝ) / (p.1 : ℝ) - 1 / ((p.1 : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))))
        ((p.2 : ℝ) / (p.1 : ℝ) + 1 / ((p.1 : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))))
    (harc : ∀ p ∈ F,
      (∫ α in Set.Icc ((p.2 : ℝ) / (p.1 : ℝ) - 1 / ((p.1 : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))))
          ((p.2 : ℝ) / (p.1 : ℝ) + 1 / ((p.1 : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))),
        ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
      B * (N : ℝ) / ((p.1 : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))) * Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ 13) :
    (∫ α in exceptionalArcs280 N η, ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
      B * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ 13 *
        (∑ p ∈ F, 1 / (p.1 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of the exceptional set analysis: the finite cover sum. The square
mean of the prime series over a set contained in the union of finitely many closed
arcs is at most the sum over those arcs of the square mean on the arc, so a
per-arc estimate turns into an estimate for the whole exceptional set with the
reciprocal denominators factored out. This is subadditivity of the integral over a
finite cover; it contains no arithmetic and no hypothesis. -/

name: log_power_absorption357
header:
theorem log_power_absorption357 :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      Real.log (N : ℝ) ^ 13 ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 40 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of the exceptional set analysis: the logarithm is absorbed by the
saving. Beyond some point a fixed power of the logarithm of N is at most N to the
one fortieth, which is what the cover weight leaves free. This is one elementary
numeric inequality about the real logarithm and a real power. -/

name: exceptional_prime_mass357_split
header:
theorem exceptional_prime_mass357_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ,
      ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
        (∫ α in exceptionalArcs280 N η, ‖primeFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (1 / 100 : ℝ))
doc: /-- The target assembled from the four leaves above. -/

name: line_bound_lnL519
header:
theorem line_bound_lnL519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          Continuous (fun t : ℝ =>
            Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine519 N t))) ∧
          ∀ t : ℝ, ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine519 N t))‖ ≤
            B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Line bound step. Under the hypothesis on the zeros of the Riemann zeta
function and of the Dirichlet L-functions, the function sending a real t to the
logarithm of the L-function of a nonprincipal character, taken at the point
1/2 + 1/ln N + i t of the vertical line, is continuous in t and is bounded by a
constant that does not depend on the character or on N, times the cube of the
logarithm of N times the absolute value of t plus two. This is the only step
that uses the zero hypothesis. It carries no difference of two sums, no Mellin
integral and no prime power. -/

name: mellin_log_expansion519
header:
theorem mellin_log_expansion519 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q →
      ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ,
        characterPrime519 χ N α -
            mellinU519 N
              (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log
                (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine519 N t))) α
          = -∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
              (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
                (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                  Complex.exp
                    ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Prime power expansion step. The difference between the damped character
prime series and the Mellin integral, along the vertical line, of the logarithm
of the L-function of the same character is exactly minus the double sum over all
primes and all exponents at least two, each term carrying the value of the
character at the prime power, the exponential damping at that power and the
oscillating exponential at that power. This is an identity for every real alpha;
the zero hypothesis only serves to keep the logarithm on one branch and to move
the line past the zeros. -/

name: prime_power_tail519
header:
theorem prime_power_tail519 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, ∀ α : ℝ,
        ‖∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
          ≤ B * Real.sqrt N
doc:
/-- LEAF. Prime power tail step. The part of the prime power double sum with
exponents at least two, summed over all primes and all such exponents, is at
most a constant independent of N, of the character and of alpha, times the
square root of N. The exponential damping at the prime powers is what makes the
double sum absolutely convergent. No zero hypothesis, no Mellin integral and no
estimate on the character occur here. -/

name: grh_mellin_transfer519_split
header:
theorem grh_mellin_transfer519_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ∃ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
            ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ∧ ∀ α : ℝ,
              ‖characterPrime519 χ N α - mellinU519 N M α‖ ≤ B * Real.sqrt N
doc:
/-- The three leaves together give the transfer of the nonprincipal character
prime series to a Mellin integral whose coefficient is the logarithm of the
L-function on the line, with the prime power part paid for by a square root of N
error. -/

name: outer_square_integrable519
header:
theorem outer_square_integrable519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R →
      R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2)
            (Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Integrability half of the outer interval.  For a positive line constant
B0, once N is large enough, and for every inverse radius R between one and the
two sevenths power of N, every continuous coefficient obeying the cubic
logarithmic line bound has square norm integrable over the outer interval from
four over N to one over R.  This is the first conjunct alone: it carries no
constant, no factor of N over R and no power of the logarithm, so it is strictly
weaker than the sealed estimate. -/

name: outer_square_small_R519
header:
theorem outer_square_small_R519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R →
      R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 10)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Mass bound on the small inverse radius range, from one up to the seventh
root of N.  Here the outer interval is at least as long as the central one, so
this is the case of the estimate in which the inverse radius is short and the
interval reaches back to the central scale four over N.  It is one case of the
sealed mass bound, with the same conclusion and a restricted range of R, and it
says nothing about the complementary range nor about integrability. -/

name: outer_square_large_R519
header:
theorem outer_square_large_R519 (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R →
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 10)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Mass bound on the large inverse radius range, from the seventh root of N
up to the two sevenths power of N.  Here the outer interval lies far from the
central scale, which is the case in which the double frequency calculation is
cut off only by the two sevenths power of N in the statement of Lemma 2.  It is
the complementary case of the sealed mass bound, again with the same conclusion
and a restricted range of R, and it carries no integrability claim. -/

name: lemma2_outer_square519_split
header:
theorem lemma2_outer_square519_split (B0 : ℝ) (hB0 : 0 < B0) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ M : ℝ → ℂ, (Continuous M ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖M t‖ ≤ B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) →
          IntegrableOn (fun α : ℝ => ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2)
            (Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) ∧
          (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R), ‖mellinU519 N M α‖ ^ 2) ≤
            C * ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 10)
doc:
/-- The three leaves together give the outer square estimate: the square of the
Mellin transform is integrable on the outer interval, and its mass there is at
most the larger of the two range constants times N over R times the tenth power
of the logarithm of N. -/

name: lnL_ne_zero_on_line1622
header:
theorem lnL_ne_zero_on_line1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 1 < N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
      ∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ≠ 0
doc:
/-- LEAF. Vanishing step. Under the hypothesis on the zeros of the L-functions, the
L-function of a nonprincipal character does not vanish anywhere on the line
1/2 + 1/ln N + i t, for N at least two. The line lies to the right of the critical
line, so a zero there would either be a zero of the open strip with real part
different from one half, which the hypothesis excludes, or a zero with real part at
least one, where the Euler product converges. This step carries no continuity
statement and no size estimate. -/

name: continuous_lnL_line1622
header:
theorem continuous_lnL_line1622 :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q), χ ≠ 1 →
      (∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ≠ 0) →
        Continuous fun t : ℝ =>
          Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Continuity step. The logarithm of the L-function of a nonprincipal character,
followed along the line, is continuous in the height as soon as it is nowhere zero
there: the L-function is differentiable, the line is continuous in the height, and the
logarithm is continuous away from zero. This step carries no estimate at all. -/

name: lnL_growth_bounded_height1622
header:
theorem lnL_growth_bounded_height1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ t : ℝ, |t| ≤ 2 →
          ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
            B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Size step, bounded height. Under the hypothesis on the zeros, the logarithm
of the L-function on the line is at most a constant independent of everything, times
ln cubed of N times the sum of the height and two, as long as the height stays in the
fixed window of absolute value at most two. The height window is compact, so this is
the part of the size estimate where the height does not grow. -/

name: lnL_growth_short_height1622
header:
theorem lnL_growth_short_height1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ t : ℝ, 2 ≤ |t| → |t| ≤ (N : ℝ) →
          ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
            B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Size step, short height. Under the hypothesis on the zeros, the logarithm of
the L-function on the line is at most a constant times ln cubed of N times the sum of
the height and two, as long as the height is at least two and at most N. Here the
height dominates neither the modulus nor the logarithm of the modulus, so the bound is
read against ln of N alone. -/

name: lnL_growth_tall_height1622
header:
theorem lnL_growth_tall_height1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ t : ℝ, (N : ℝ) ≤ |t| →
          ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
            B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Size step, tall height. Under the hypothesis on the zeros, the logarithm of
the L-function on the line is at most a constant times ln cubed of N times the sum of
the height and two, as long as the height is at least N. Here the height dominates the
modulus, so the bound is read against ln of the height alone, and the modulus enters
only through the conductor bound. -/

name: lineBound_lnL1622_split
header:
theorem lineBound_lnL1622_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          LineBound1622 N B0
            (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t)))
doc:
/-- The five leaves together give the line bound of the logarithm of the L-function:
the line meets no zero, so the logarithm is continuous there, and the three height
ranges carry the size estimate with constants joined by a maximum. -/

name: two_pow_split
header: private lemma two_pow_split {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) : 2 ^ e = 2 ^ (e - 1) + 2 ^ (e - 1)
doc: /-- `2 ^ e` is two copies of `2 ^ (e - 1)` when `1 ≤ e`. -/

name: two_rpow_pred_le
header: private lemma two_rpow_pred_le {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) : (2 : ℝ) ^ (e - 1) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ e
doc: /-- The real power `2 ^ (e - 1)` does not exceed `2 ^ e`. -/

name: two_le_rpow
header:
private lemma two_le_rpow {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 / 2 ≤ θ) {N : ℕ} (hN : 4 ≤ N) :
    (2 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ θ
doc:
/-- `2 ≤ N ^ θ` for `N ≥ 4` and `θ ≥ 1 / 2`, the numeric side condition of step 3:
`2 = 4 ^ (1 / 2) ≤ 4 ^ θ ≤ N ^ θ`. -/

name: sum_pow_of_all_one
header:
private lemma sum_pow_of_all_one (l : List ℕ) :
    (∀ e ∈ l, e = 1) → (l.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum = 2 * l.length
doc: /-- A list all of whose entries are `1` has power-sum `2 * length`. -/

name: split_list_step
header:
private lemma split_list_step {X : ℝ} (l : List ℕ) :
    (∀ e ∈ l, 1 ≤ e) → (∀ e ∈ l, (2 : ℝ) ^ e ≤ X) → (∃ e ∈ l, 2 ≤ e) →
      ∃ l' : List ℕ, l'.length = l.length + 1 ∧
        (l'.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum = (l.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum ∧
          (∀ e ∈ l', 1 ≤ e) ∧ (∀ e ∈ l', (2 : ℝ) ^ e ≤ X)
doc:
/-- One split step. A list of exponents with `1 ≤ e`, `2 ^ e ≤ X` and some entry `2 ≤ e` is
replaced by a longer list with the same power-sum, all conditions preserved: the entry `e ≥ 2`
becomes two copies of `e - 1`. -/

name: split_list_iter
header:
private lemma split_list_iter {X : ℝ} {K : ℕ} (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (l : List ℕ), (∀ e ∈ l, 1 ≤ e) → (∀ e ∈ l, (2 : ℝ) ^ e ≤ X) →
      2 * K ≤ (l.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum → l.length + n ≤ K →
      ∃ l' : List ℕ, l'.length = l.length + n ∧
        (l'.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum = (l.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum ∧
          (∀ e ∈ l', 1 ≤ e) ∧ (∀ e ∈ l', (2 : ℝ) ^ e ≤ X)
doc:
/-- Iterating `split_list_step`: from a list of length at most `K - n` one reaches a list `n` terms
longer with the same power-sum and the same pointwise bounds. The step is possible because a list
of `1`s has power-sum `2 * length`, so `2 * K ≤ power-sum` forces a `2` somewhere while the length
is below `K`. -/

name: exists_rep_of_list
header:
private lemma exists_rep_of_list {X : ℝ} {n M : ℕ} (l : List ℕ) (hlen : l.length = n)
    (h1 : ∀ e ∈ l, 1 ≤ e) (h2 : ∀ e ∈ l, (2 : ℝ) ^ e ≤ X)
    (hsum : M = (l.map (fun e => 2 ^ e)).sum) :
    ∃ ν' : Fin n → ℕ, (∀ i, 1 ≤ ν' i ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ν' i) ≤ X) ∧ M = ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν' i)
doc:
/-- A list of exponents of length `n` whose powers are all `≥ 1` and at most `X` gives the
`Fin n`-indexed family of `LowBitsRep`, with the same power-sum. -/

name: leaf_grh_powers_within_window
header:
theorem leaf_grh_powers_within_window (hG : GRH) :
    ∀ θ : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ → θ < 1 →
      ∃ K N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N₀ < N →
        ∃ p q : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧
          ∃ t : ℕ, t ≤ K ∧ ∃ ν : Fin t → ℕ,
            (∀ i, 1 ≤ ν i ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ν i) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ θ) ∧
              N = p + q + ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i) ∧ 2 * K ≤ ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of the split, the analytic input. Assume GRH. For every real `θ` with
`1 / 2 < θ < 1` there are `K` and `N₀` such that every even `N > N₀` is a sum of two primes and
at most `K` powers of two `2 ^ ν i` with `1 ≤ ν i` and `2 ^ ν i ≤ N ^ θ`, and the powers sum to at
least `2 * K`. The count `K` is one fixed number, not yet the exact count `k` of the target. -/

name: leaf_split_at_most_to_exact
header:
theorem leaf_split_at_most_to_exact {K M : ℕ} {X : ℝ} (hX : 0 ≤ X)
    (hK : 2 * K ≤ M) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ K) (ν : Fin t → ℕ)
    (hν : ∀ i, 1 ≤ ν i ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ν i) ≤ X)
    (hM : M = ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν i)) :
    ∃ ν' : Fin K → ℕ, (∀ i, 1 ≤ ν' i ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ν' i) ≤ X) ∧ M = ∑ i, 2 ^ (ν' i)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of the split, the binary splitting estimate. Let `0 ≤ X`, let `M` be a sum of
`t ≤ K` powers of two `2 ^ ν i` with `1 ≤ ν i` and `2 ^ ν i ≤ X`, and let `2 * K ≤ M`. Then `M` is
also a sum of exactly `K` powers of two with `1 ≤ ν' i` and `2 ^ ν' i ≤ X`. Splitting `2 ^ e` with
`2 ≤ e` into `2 ^ (e - 1) + 2 ^ (e - 1)` raises the count by one and lowers no single power, so
every count from `t` up to `M / 2` is reached, and `2 * K ≤ M` puts `K` in that range. -/

name: leaf_rep_add_one_power
header:
theorem leaf_rep_add_one_power {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 / 2 ≤ θ) {k N : ℕ} (hN : 4 ≤ N)
    (h : LowBitsRep θ k (N - 2)) : LowBitsRep θ (k + 1) N
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of the split, one step in the count. For `1 / 2 ≤ θ` and `4 ≤ N`, a
representation of `N - 2` as two primes plus `k` powers of two, each at most `(N - 2) ^ θ`, gives a
representation of `N` as two primes plus `k + 1` powers of two each at most `N ^ θ`: append the
power `2 ^ 1 = 2`, and `(N - 2) ^ θ ≤ N ^ θ` because `θ ≥ 0`. -/

name: leaf_rpow_ge_two
header:
theorem leaf_rpow_ge_two {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 / 2 ≤ θ) {N : ℕ} (hN : 4 ≤ N) :
    (2 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ θ
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of the split, the numeric side condition of step 3 and nothing more:
`2 ≤ N ^ θ` for every `N ≥ 4` and every `θ ≥ 1 / 2`, since `2 = 4 ^ (1 / 2) ≤ 4 ^ θ ≤ N ^ θ`. -/

name: linnik_low_bits_split
header:
theorem linnik_low_bits_split (_hG : GRH) :
    ∀ θ : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ → θ < 1 → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, k₀ ≤ k → AllLargeEven (LowBitsRep θ k)
doc:
/-- `linnik_low_bits` of `Novelty1620`, assembled from the four leaves above: the analytic leaf
gives the count `K` for all large even `N`, the splitting leaf makes the count exact, and the
count-raising leaf covers every `k ≥ K`. -/

name: leaves
header:
class leaves only the residue zero, so the resolved core sum is the unshifted core
integral over the interval of length two over N around the origin. -/
doc: /-- At the unit modulus the filter over the reduced residues of the single residue

name: local_arc_unit_sum1622
header:
private theorem local_arc_unit_sum1622 (N : ℕ) (q : ℕ) (hq1 : q = 1) (n : ℤ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (Finset.range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ∫ z in -(1 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / (N : ℝ)),
          primeFourier111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z) ^ 2 *
            Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      ∫ z in -(1 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / (N : ℝ)),
        primeFourier111 N z ^ 2 *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- At the unit modulus the filter over the reduced residues of the single residue
class leaves only the residue zero, so the resolved core sum is the unshifted core
integral over the interval of length two over N around the origin. -/

name: local_arc_unit_coefficient1622
doc:
/-- At the unit modulus the square of the Moebius function and the square of the
totient both equal one, and the Ramanujan sum of the unit modulus at any residual
also equals one, so the modulus of their product is one. -/

name: local_arc_core_unit_integral1622
header:
theorem local_arc_core_unit_integral1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → q = 1 → ∀ n : ℤ,
        (4 : ℤ) ≤ n →
        n ≤ N →
        ‖(∫ z in -(1 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / (N : ℝ)),
            primeFourier111 N z ^ 2 *
              Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * z : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))‖ ≤
          c * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) + 1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The size of the core integral at the unit modulus. The squared prime Fourier
series against the phase of the residual, integrated over the interval of length two
over N around the origin, is bounded by the local square mean value alone, which is N
log N to the thirteenth times the sum of the two errors. There is no main term, no
damped convolution and no Ramanujan sum in this step; the residual enters only through
the phase. -/

name: local_arc_core_unit_main1622
header:
theorem local_arc_core_unit_main1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → q = 1 → ∀ n : ℤ,
        (4 : ℤ) ≤ n →
        n ≤ N →
        ‖((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          c * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) + 1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The size of the target main term at the unit modulus. The exponentially
damped convolution of the residual, with the damping of minus the residual over N, is
at most a constant times N log N to the thirteenth times the sum of the two errors.
This is the elementary estimate of the convolution, and it carries no prime Fourier
series, no integral and no Ramanujan sum. -/

name: local_arc_core_unit1622_split
header:
theorem local_arc_core_unit1622_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → q = 1 → ∀ n : ℤ,
        (4 : ℤ) ≤ n →
        n ≤ N →

Route. Every index of the convolution lies in the finite interval Icc 2 (n - 2), so
m is at least 2 and the complementary index n - m is at least 2 as well, the
subtraction being the one on the naturals. A logarithm of an integer at least 2 is
positive, and a product of two positive reals is positive. Four leaves: the two
lower bounds on the indices, the positivity of a logarithm, and the final product
step. Degenerate values are covered by the same leaves: for n at most 3 the
interval is empty, so the hypothesis is not available and no case is left; m = 1 or
n - m = 1 cannot occur under the hypothesis, which is what makes the two
logarithms strictly positive.
-/

/-- LEAF. Lower bound on the first index: membership in the index interval forces
2 <= m. This is the step that puts the first logarithm at an argument at least 2,
and it is also what rules out m = 0 and m = 1. -/

Route. Write u = log m, v = log (n - m) and L = log n, so that the summand is
1 / (u * v) and the shift is 2L - u - v, the logarithm of n^2 / (m (n - m)). The
summand is at most 1/L^2 + 2 (2L - u - v)/L^3 wherever the shift is at most L/2,
and the shift has total at most a constant times n over the whole range. The two
ends of the range, where the shift is large, hold only about the square root of n
terms of size at most a constant over L, which is again at most a constant times
n / L^3. Adding the three pieces gives the excess with one constant.
-/
import LeanLab.Linnik1951.SPLIT_log_convolution_estimate1622

namespace LeanLab.Linnik1951

/-- LEAF. Positivity of the shift: for every index of the convolution the logarithm
of m (n - m) is at most twice the logarithm of n, that is the shift 2 log n minus
log m minus log (n - m) is nonnegative. This is the step that lets the shift be
weight summed over the range without a sign condition. -/

name: logConv_shift_nonneg1622
header:
theorem logConv_shift_nonneg1622 (n m : ℕ) (hm : m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)) :
    0 ≤ 2 * Real.log (n : ℝ) - (Real.log m + Real.log (n - m : ℕ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Positivity of the shift: for every index of the convolution the logarithm
of m (n - m) is at most twice the logarithm of n, that is the shift 2 log n minus
log m minus log (n - m) is nonnegative. This is the step that lets the shift be
weight summed over the range without a sign condition. -/

name: logConv_shift_sum1622
header:

          (2 * Real.log (n : ℝ) - (Real.log m + Real.log (n - m : ℕ))))
        ≤ K * (n : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Total of the shift: summed over the whole range 2 <= m <= n - 2 the shift
2 log n - log m - log (n - m) is at most a constant times n. The shift is the
logarithm of n^2 / (m (n - m)), and the sum of the logarithms is read off a lower
bound for the logarithm of the factorial (n - 2)!, so the constant is absolute. -/

name: logConv_term_majorant1622

theorem logConv_term_majorant1622 (u v L : ℝ) (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (hL : 0 < L)

    1 / (u * v) ≤ 1 / L ^ 2 + (2 / L ^ 3) * (2 * L - (u + v))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Termwise majorant: for positive u, v and L with u + v at most 2 L and with
the shift 2 L - u - v at most L / 2, the reciprocal product 1 / (u v) is at most
1 / L^2 plus twice the shift over L^3. This is the elementary inequality
4 u v <= (u + v)^2 together with a quadratic estimate for the reciprocal of
1 - shift / L. -/

    1 / Real.log n ≤ 1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)
doc:
/-- The parent statement, assembled from the leaves above with no remaining gap:
the logarithm of n is at least one, its square root lies between one and the
logarithm itself, and the reciprocal reverses that order. -/

name: logConv_small_initial1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_initial1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hn3 : n ≤ 3) :
    |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
      500 * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The empty end of the range: for 2 <= n <= 3 the index set 2 <= m <= n - 2 is empty,
so the convolution is zero and the claim holds with constant 500. This is the step that keeps
n equal to 2 and n equal to 3 out of the index count n - 3, which needs n at least 4. -/

name: logConv_small_term_upper1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_term_upper1622 (n m : ℕ) (hm : m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)) :
    1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ 1 / Real.log 2 ^ 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. Termwise upper bound: for an index m of the convolution sum,
1 / (log m * log (n - m)) is at most 1 / (log 2)^2, because the two indices are at least 2 and
give both logarithms at least log 2 while their product stays positive. This is the step that
turns the index count into an upper bound for the whole sum. -/

name: logConv_small_term_lower1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_term_lower1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (m : ℕ)
    (hm : m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)) :
    1 / Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Termwise lower bound: for 2 <= n and an index m of the convolution sum,
1 / (log m * log (n - m)) is at least 1 / (log n)^2, because both indices are at most n and
make both logarithms positive and at most log n. This is the step that turns the index count
into a lower bound for the whole sum. -/

name: logConv_small_scale_upper1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_scale_upper1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hn1000 : n ≤ 1000) :
    (n : ℝ) * (1 / Real.log 2 ^ 2) - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤
      500 * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Scale comparison, upper side: for 4 <= n <= 1000 the crude upper bound n / (log 2)^2
of the convolution overshoots the main term n / (log n)^2 by at most 500 times the main term
times 1 / sqrt (log n). Only the two constants log n <= 7 and log 2 >= 0.69 are used, and no
property of the convolution. -/

name: logConv_small_scale_lower1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_scale_lower1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hn1000 : n ≤ 1000) :
    -(500 * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))) ≤
      -(3 / Real.log n ^ 2)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Scale comparison, lower side: for 4 <= n <= 1000 the loss 3 / (log n)^2 by which the
index count n - 3 falls short of n is at most 500 times the main term times
1 / sqrt (log n). This is the step that closes the absolute value from below, and it uses no
property of the convolution. -/

name: logConv_small_range1622_split
header:
theorem logConv_small_range1622_split :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ 1000 →
      |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
        B * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- The target statement of the parent file, assembled from the five leaves above with no
remaining gap: constant 500, the empty end 2 <= n <= 3, and for 4 <= n <= 1000 the sum
sandwiched between (n - 3) / (log n)^2 and (n - 3) / (log 2)^2, which the two scale leaves
compare with 500 times the main term times 1 / sqrt (log n). -/

name: log_convolution_estimate1622_split.
header:
theorem log_convolution_estimate1622_split. No statement of the parent file is
changed; no definition is added.
AI wrote the Lean code. Binary Goldbach is open.

Route. Write A(n) for n / (log n)^2 and L(n) for the convolution
logConvolution1622 n, a sum over 2 <= m <= n-2. For n at most 10^3 the claim is a
finite range statement, carried by one leaf. For n at least 10^3 the sum dominates
A(n) and exceeds it only by O(n / (log n)^3), which is A(n) times 1/log n. There
log n is at least one, so 1/log n is at most 1/sqrt(log n), which is the relative
weight of the target. The two ranges cover every n at least 2 and give one pair of
constants.

doc: /-- `log 3` is at most `2 log 2 - 1/4`, from `log (3/4) ≤ 3/4 - 1`. -/

name: logConv_denominator_pos1622
header:
theorem logConv_denominator_pos1622 (n m : ℕ) (hm : m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2)) :
    0 < Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Well-definedness of the summand: every index of the convolution sum has
both logarithms positive, so the summand is defined and no factor vanishes. This is
the step that lets the two one-sided leaves divide by log m and log (n - m). -/

name: logConv_main_le1622
header:
theorem logConv_main_le1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) :
    (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ logConvolution1622 n
doc:
/-- LEAF. Scale control, main term is dominated: from n equal to 4 upwards the
convolution sum is at least n / (log n)^2. The sum has about n terms each of size
about 1 / (log n)^2, and this leaf asserts only the one-sided floor, with no error
term. It is the step that removes the absolute value in the large range. -/

name: log_two_pos_l3
header: private lemma log_two_pos_l3 : 0 < Real.log 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. Scale control, main term is dominated: from n equal to 4 upwards the
convolution sum is at least n / (log n)^2. The sum has about n terms each of size
about 1 / (log n)^2, and this leaf asserts only the one-sided floor, with no error
term. It is the step that removes the absolute value in the large range. -/
theorem logConv_main_le1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) :
    (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ logConvolution1622 n := by
  have h2pos : 0 < Real.log 2 := log_two_pos1622
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hn with h4 | h4
  · -- n = 4: the sum is the single term at m = 2, and log 4 = 2 log 2
    subst h4
    rw [logConvolution_four1622]
    push_cast
    rw [log_four_eq1622]
    have h2 : Real.log 2 ≠ 0 := h2pos.ne'
    field_simp
    norm_num
  · rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (show 5 ≤ n by omega) with h5 | h5
    · -- n = 5: two terms, both equal to 1 / (log 2 * log 3)
      subst h5
      have hval : logConvolution1622 5 = 2 / (Real.log 2 * Real.log 3) := by
        have hset : Finset.Icc 2 (5 - 2) = ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) := by decide
        rw [logConvolution1622, hset, Finset.sum_pair (by norm_num)]
        norm_num
        field_simp
        try ring
      rw [hval]
      push_cast
      have ha1 : (0.6931471803 : ℝ) < Real.log 2 := Real.log_two_gt_d9
      have ha2 : Real.log 2 < 0.6931471808 := Real.log_two_lt_d9
      have h3 : Real.log 3 ≤ 2 * Real.log 2 - 1 / 4 := log_three_le1622
      have h5b : 2 * Real.log 2 + 1 / 5 ≤ Real.log 5 := log_five_ge1622
      have hL3 : 0 < Real.log 3 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
      have hL5 : 0 < Real.log 5 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
      have h3' : 5 * Real.log 2 * Real.log 3 ≤ 5 * Real.log 2 * (2 * Real.log 2 - 1 / 4) := by
        apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h3
        linarith
      have h5sq : (2 * Real.log 2 + 1 / 5) ^ 2 ≤ Real.log 5 ^ 2 := by
        have hpos : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.log 5 - (2 * Real.log 2 + 1 / 5) := by linarith
        have hsum : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.log 5 + (2 * Real.log 2 + 1 / 5) := by linarith
        nlinarith [hpos, hsum]
      rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)]
      nlinarith [h3', h5sq, ha1, ha2]
    · -- n ≥ 6: two end terms of size 1 / (log 2 * log (n-2)), the rest at 1 / L^2
      have hn6 : 6 ≤ n := h5
      set L : ℝ := Real.log (n : ℝ) with hL
      have hnR : (1 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < n)
      have hLpos : 0 < L := by rw [hL]; exact Real.log_pos hnR
      have hdecomp : Finset.Icc 2 (n - 2) = insert 2 (insert (n - 2) (Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3))) := by
        ext m
        simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_insert]
        omega
      have hmem1 : (2 : ℕ) ∉ insert (n - 2) (Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3)) := by
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_Icc]
        omega
      have hmem2 : (n - 2) ∉ Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3) := by
        simp only [Finset.mem_Icc]
        omega
      have hmid : ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3),
          1 / L ^ 2 ≤ 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ)) := by
        intro m hm
        simp only [Finset.mem_Icc] at hm
        obtain ⟨hm3, hmn⟩ := hm
        have hm1 : (1 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < m)
        have hnm1 : (1 : ℝ) < ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < n - m)
        have hmpos : 0 < Real.log (m : ℝ) := Real.log_pos hm1
        have hnmpos : 0 < Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ) := Real.log_pos hnm1
        have h1 : Real.log (m : ℝ) ≤ L := by
          rw [hL]
          exact Real.log_le_log (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < m))
            (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : m ≤ n))
        have h2 : Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ L := by
          rw [hL]
          exact Real.log_le_log (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < n - m))
            (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : n - m ≤ n))
        have hprod : Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ L * L :=
          mul_le_mul h1 h2 hnmpos.le hLpos.le
        have hpos : 0 < Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ) := mul_pos hmpos hnmpos
        have h := one_div_le_one_div_of_le hpos hprod
        simpa [pow_two] using h
      have hcard : (Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3)).card = n - 5 := by
        rw [Nat.card_Icc]
        omega
      have hsum_ge : ((n - 5 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / L ^ 2) ≤
          ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3), 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ)) := by
        have h := Finset.sum_le_sum hmid
        rw [Finset.sum_const, hcard, nsmul_eq_mul] at h
        exact h
      have hlogend : 0 < Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
        Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < n - 2))
      have hleend : Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ L := by
        rw [hL]
        exact Real.log_le_log (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < n - 2))
          (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : n - 2 ≤ n))
      have hend1 : 1 / (Real.log 2 * L) ≤ 1 / (Real.log 2 * Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)) :=
        one_div_le_one_div_of_le (mul_pos h2pos hlogend)
          (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hleend h2pos.le)
      have hend2 : 1 / (L * Real.log 2) ≤ 1 / (Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log 2) :=
        one_div_le_one_div_of_le (mul_pos hlogend h2pos)
          (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hleend h2pos.le)
      have h5a : 5 * Real.log 2 ≤ 2 * L := by
        have h6 : 5 / 2 * Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log 6 := log_six_ge1622
        have h6n : Real.log 6 ≤ L := by
          rw [hL]
          exact Real.log_le_log (by norm_num) (by exact_mod_cast hn6)
        linarith
      have h5div : (5 : ℝ) / L ^ 2 ≤ 2 / (Real.log 2 * L) := by
        rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by nlinarith [hLpos] : (0 : ℝ) < L ^ 2) (mul_pos h2pos hLpos)]
        have hh := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h5a hLpos.le
        nlinarith [hh]
      have htwo : 2 / (Real.log 2 * L) = 1 / (Real.log 2 * L) + 1 / (L * Real.log 2) := by
        have h2 : Real.log 2 ≠ 0 := h2pos.ne'
        field_simp
        try ring
      have hkey : (n : ℝ) / L ^ 2 ≤ 2 / (Real.log 2 * L) + ((n - 5 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / L ^ 2) := by
        have hc : ((n - 5 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) - 5 := by
          rw [Nat.cast_sub (show 5 ≤ n by omega)]
          push_cast
          ring
        have hid1 : (n : ℝ) / L ^ 2 = (5 : ℝ) / L ^ 2 + ((n : ℝ) - 5) * (1 / L ^ 2) := by
          field_simp
          try ring
        rw [hid1, hc]
        linarith [h5div]
      have hgoal : (n : ℝ) / L ^ 2 ≤
          1 / (Real.log 2 * Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)) +
            (1 / (Real.log ((n - 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log 2) +
              ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 3 (n - 3),
                1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ) * Real.log ((n - m : ℕ) : ℝ))) := by
        linarith [hkey, htwo, hend1, hend2, hsum_ge]
      rw [logConvolution1622, hdecomp, Finset.sum_insert hmem1, Finset.sum_insert hmem2]
      rw [show n - (n - 2) = 2 from by omega]
      exact hgoal
