        (1 / (Real.log x) ^ 2 - 2 * (1 / (Real.log x) ^ 3)) x := by
    intro x hx
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le h2N] at hx
    exact hasderiv_l3 x hx.1
  have h := intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
    (f := fun y : ℝ => y * (1 / (Real.log y) ^ 2))
    (f' := fun x : ℝ => 1 / (Real.log x) ^ 2 - 2 * (1 / (Real.log x) ^ 3))
    (a := (2 : ℝ)) (b := (N : ℝ)) hderiv (h2i.sub (h3i.const_mul 2))
  have h1 : ∫ x in (2 : ℝ)..(N : ℝ), (1 / (Real.log x) ^ 2 - 2 * (1 / (Real.log x) ^ 3))
      = (∫ x in (2 : ℝ)..(N : ℝ), 1 / (Real.log x) ^ 2)
        - 2 * ∫ x in (2 : ℝ)..(N : ℝ), 1 / (Real.log x) ^ 3 := by
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub h2i (h3i.const_mul 2), intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul]
  rw [h1] at h
  have hNval : (N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 2)
      = (N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 2) := rfl
  linarith [h]

name: log_cube_le_sqrt_l3
header:
private lemma log_cube_le_sqrt_l3 (N : ℕ) (hN : 4 ≤ N) :
    (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3 ≤ 216 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)
doc: /-- `log N ^ 3 ≤ 216 * sqrt N`, from `log x ≤ 6 x ^ (1/6)`. -/

name: sum_inv_log_sq_l3
header:
private lemma sum_inv_log_sq_l3 (N : ℕ) (hN : 4 ≤ N) :
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2
      ≤ (N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 2)
        + 2000 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3))
doc: /-- The sum of `1 / log^2` over `2..N`, with a second order error. -/

name: log_four_eq_l3
header: private lemma log_four_eq_l3 : Real.log 4 = 2 * Real.log 2
doc:
/-- The sum of `1 / log^2` over `2..N`, with a second order error. -/
private lemma sum_inv_log_sq_l3 (N : ℕ) (hN : 4 ≤ N) :
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2
      ≤ (N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 2)
        + 2000 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3)) := by
  have hdecomp : Finset.Icc 2 N = insert 2 (Finset.Icc 3 N) := by
    ext m
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_insert]
    omega
  have hnotmem : (2 : ℕ) ∉ Finset.Icc 3 N := by
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc]
    omega
  have hico : Finset.Ico 3 (N + 1) = Finset.Icc 3 N := by
    ext m
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_Ico]
    omega
  have hsplit : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2
      = 1 / (Real.log 2) ^ 2
        + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 3 N, 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2 := by
    rw [hdecomp, Finset.sum_insert hnotmem]
    simp
  rw [hsplit, ← hico]
  have hNpos : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by
    have : (0 : ℕ) < N := by omega
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hN1 : (1 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < N)
  have hLpos : 0 < Real.log (N : ℝ) := Real.log_pos hN1
  have h1 : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Ico 3 (N + 1), 1 / (Real.log (m : ℝ)) ^ 2
      ≤ ∫ x in (2 : ℝ)..(N : ℝ), 1 / (Real.log x) ^ 2 := sum_le_integral_l3 N hN
  have h2 := integral_inv_log_sq_l3 N hN
  have h3 := int_cube_l3 N hN
  have h4 : (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3 ≤ 216 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) := log_cube_le_sqrt_l3 N hN
  have hL3pos : (0 : ℝ) < (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3 := by positivity
  have hs0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hs2 : Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) := by
    rw [← sq, Real.sq_sqrt hNpos.le]
  have h6 : 8 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ≤ 1728 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3)) := by
    have hstep : 8 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) * (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3 ≤ 1728 * (N : ℝ) := by
      have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h4 (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 8 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ))
      nlinarith [hm, hs2, hs0]
    have hrw : 1728 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3))
        = 1728 * (N : ℝ) / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3 := by
      field_simp
    rw [hrw, le_div_iff₀ hL3pos]
    linarith [hstep]
  have hNL3 : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3) := by positivity
  have hlog2sq : 0 < (1 : ℝ) / (Real.log 2) ^ 2 := by positivity
  have h5 : 2 * (4 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 8 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3)))
      = 8 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 16 * ((N : ℝ) * (1 / (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ 3)) := by ring
  linarith [h1, h2, h3, h5, h6, hlog2sq, hNL3]

name: excess_core_l3
doc: /-- The convolution is bounded by the main term plus `20000 n / log^3 n`. -/

name: logConv_excess1622
header:
theorem logConv_excess1622 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1000 ≤ n →
      logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤
        C * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 3)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Scale control, second order excess: from n equal to 10^3 upwards the
excess of the convolution over n / (log n)^2 is bounded by a constant times
n / (log n)^3, that is by the main term times 1 / log n. One-sided only, and no
absolute value. -/

name: logConv_small_range1622
header:
theorem logConv_small_range1622 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ 1000 →
      |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
        B * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The finite range: for 2 <= n <= 10^3 the whole claim of the target holds
with one constant, in absolute value and with the relative weight 1/sqrt(log n).
Finitely many cases and no asymptotic content. -/

name: logConv_log_cube_split1622
header:
theorem logConv_log_cube_split1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 3 = ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.log n)
doc:
/-- LEAF. The power identity that turns the excess into the relative weight:
n / (log n)^3 is n / (log n)^2 times 1 / log n, for every n at least 2, where the
logarithm does not vanish. -/

name: logConv_recip_log_le_sqrt1622
header:
theorem logConv_recip_log_le_sqrt1622 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1000 ≤ n) :
    1 / Real.log n ≤ 1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)
doc:
/-- LEAF. The logarithmic weight comparison: for n at least 10^3 the logarithm is at
least one, so 1 / log n is at most 1 / sqrt(log n). This is what converts the
second order excess into the exact weight of the target. -/

name: log_convolution_estimate1622_split
header:
theorem log_convolution_estimate1622_split :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤ B * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))
doc:
/-- The target statement of the parent file, assembled from the leaves above with no
remaining gap: one constant covering the finite range 2 <= n <= 10^3 and the half
line 10^3 <= n. -/

name: major_bookkeeping_sharp1622
header:
theorem major_bookkeeping_sharp1622 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B)
    (N0 : ℕ) (hL : LocalExpansion1622 B N0) (B' : ℝ) (hB' : 0 < B')
    (hC : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
        B' * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∃ N1 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N1 < N →
      |arcContribution280 k N (majorArcs280 N) - truncatedMain357 k N| ≤
        A * majorRelative376 k N +
          A * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (3 / 140 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ (k + 13) +
            A * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (1 / 1000 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ (k + 13)
doc:
/-- LEAF: the bookkeeping in the form the arcs give it, with the sharper saving
N to one minus three over one hundred and forty and the weakened tail the
target already allows. -/

name: power_saving_absorb1622
header:
theorem power_saving_absorb1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (3 / 140 : ℝ)) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (1 / 1000 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF: the sharper power saving of N is at most the weaker one at every N
from one on. -/

name: log_power_nonneg1622
header:
theorem log_power_nonneg1622 (k N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    0 ≤ Real.log N ^ (k + 13)
doc: /-- LEAF: the logarithmic factor of the error is nonnegative. -/

name: major_relative_nonneg1622
header:
theorem major_relative_nonneg1622 (k N : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ majorRelative376 k N
doc: /-- LEAF: the relative correction is nonnegative. -/

name: major_bookkeeping1622_split
header:
theorem major_bookkeeping1622_split (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B) (N0 : ℕ)
    (hL : LocalExpansion1622 B N0) (B' : ℝ) (hB' : 0 < B')
    (hC : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      |logConvolution1622 n - (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2| ≤
        B' * ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n))) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∃ N1 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N1 < N →
      |arcContribution280 k N (majorArcs280 N) - truncatedMain357 k N| ≤
        A * majorRelative376 k N +
          A * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - (1 / 1000 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ (k + 13)
doc:
/-- Assembly of major_bookkeeping1622 from the four leaves above. Take the
constant and the threshold of the bookkeeping, double the threshold to at least
one, and at a large even N compare the two powers of N with the power saving
leaf, multiply by the nonnegative logarithmic factor and the positive constant,
and use the nonnegativity of the relative correction to pay for the doubled
coefficient on both summands. The two contributions of the bookkeeping are then
the first and the third summand of the target after that replacement. No step
uses major_bookkeeping1622 itself. -/

name: major_error_remainder357
header:
theorem major_error_remainder357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N0 < N →
      |arcContribution280 k N (majorArcs280 N) - truncatedMain357 k N| ≤
        ε / 2 * scale111 k N + C * (N : ℝ) / Real.log N
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3: the major arc error with a crude additive tail.  For
every fixed exponent parameter at least three and every positive tolerance
there is a constant and a threshold beyond which the major arc contribution
differs from the truncated main term by at most the demanded fraction of the
scale plus the absolute tail with one factor of the logarithm only.  This is
the whole analytic content of the major arc expansion, exponent tuple counting
and geometric tail; it is weaker than the target because the tail summand is
nonnegative, and it is the step that has to be supplied by the sections on the
local prime square, the singular series and the counting of exponent tuples. -/

name: log_power_dominates357
header:
theorem log_power_dominates357 (C δ : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → C ≤ δ * Real.log N ^ p
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3: growth of the logarithm against a constant.  For every
positive constant, every positive coefficient and every positive natural power
the logarithm of N raised to that power eventually dominates the constant.  No
arithmetic and no major arcs occur here; it is the real-variable statement that
supplies the pointwise hypothesis of step 3. -/

name: major_absorption_algebra357
header:
theorem major_absorption_algebra357 {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N)
    {C ε : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (h : C ≤ ε / 2 * Real.log N ^ (k - 1) / Real.log 2 ^ (k - 2)) :
    C * (N : ℝ) / Real.log N ≤ ε / 2 * scale111 k N
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3: the algebraic bookkeeping.  At a point N at least three,
a bound of the constant by a suitable positive multiple of the logarithm to the
power one less than the exponent parameter is exactly what is needed to turn
the crude additive tail of step 1 into the demanded multiple of the scale.
Both sides are positive here, because N is at least three forces the logarithm
of N to be positive, and the scale is the product of N with the exponent
parameter minus two power of the logarithmic ratio. -/

name: major_to_truncated357_split
header:
theorem major_to_truncated357_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, Even N → N0 < N →
      |arcContribution280 k N (majorArcs280 N) - truncatedMain357 k N| ≤
        ε * scale111 k N
doc:
/-- Assembly of `major_to_truncated357` from the three leaves above: take the
constant and the threshold of step 1, feed the constant into the growth of the
logarithm of step 2 with coefficient half of the tolerance over the logarithm
of two to the exponent parameter minus two, and absorb the additive tail into
the scale with step 3.  The triangle step is the single line
`abs_sub_le`-free comparison: the bound of step 1 is already the difference
itself, so only the addition of the two halves of the tolerance remains, and
`scale111` has to be nonnegative there.  No step uses `major_to_truncated357`
itself. -/

name: log_L_prime_power_series1622
header:
theorem log_L_prime_power_series1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
      ∀ t : ℝ, Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))
        = ∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
            ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
              (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Euler product step. Under the hypothesis on the zeros, the logarithm of
the L-function of a nonprincipal character at the point one half plus one over
the logarithm of N plus i t is the double series over all primes and all
exponents at least one, the coefficient of an exponent being the character value
at the corresponding prime power divided by that exponent, times the negative
power of the prime power. No Mellin integral and no character prime sum occur
here. -/

name: mellin_prime_power_series1622
header:
theorem mellin_prime_power_series1622 :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, ∀ α : ℝ,
      mellinU1622 N
          (fun t : ℝ => ∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
            ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
              (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t))) α
        = ∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
            ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (m + 1))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Mellin step. The Mellin integral of the prime power double series is
the same double series with every term carrying the prime power damping and the
character twist at that prime power, the pair of parameters being the reciprocal
of N and twice pi alpha. This is the termwise evaluation of the integral against
the kernel and carries no L-function, no character prime sum and no zero
hypothesis. -/

name: prime_power_series_summable1622
header:
theorem prime_power_series_summable1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
    (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (α : ℝ) :
    Summable (fun x : Nat.Primes × ℕ =>
      ‖((x.2 : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((x.1 : ℕ) ^ (x.2 + 1)) *
        (Real.exp (-(((x.1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (x.2 + 1) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp
            ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((x.1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (x.2 + 1))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Size estimate. The damped prime power double series is absolutely
summable on the product of the primes and the exponents: the character factor has
modulus at most one, the exponent factor is at most one over the exponent, and
the damping falls off geometrically in the exponent. This is an estimate only,
with no identity, no Mellin integral and no zero hypothesis. -/

name: prime_power_split1622
header:
theorem prime_power_split1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
    (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (α : ℝ) :
    ∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
        ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
          (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (m + 1) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp
              ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (m + 1))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
      = characterPrime280 χ N α +
          ∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Bookkeeping step. The damped prime power double series splits at the
exponent one: that slice is exactly the character prime sum, and the remaining
exponents, shifted by two, are the tail of the statement. A sum rearrangement
only, with no analysis. -/

name: mellinU1622_congr_local
header:
private lemma mellinU1622_congr_local (N : ℕ) (M M' : ℝ → ℂ) (α : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, M t = M' t) : mellinU1622 N M α = mellinU1622 N M' α
doc:
/-- The Mellin integral only sees the coefficient as a function of the line
parameter, so two coefficients that agree at every point give the same integral. -/

name: mellin_lnL_expansion1622_split
header:
theorem mellin_lnL_expansion1622_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ,
      characterPrime280 χ N α -
          mellinU1622 N
            (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))) α
        = -∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- The Euler product step and the Mellin step evaluate the two sides against
each other, and the bookkeeping step separates the character prime sum from the
prime power tail of exponents at least two. -/

name: near_half_integral_le_sup357
header:
theorem near_half_integral_le_sup357 {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (N : ℕ)
    (M u v : ℝ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (huv : u ≤ v)
    (hM : ∀ α : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Icc u v → ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ M) :
    (∫ α in u..v, ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2) ≤ M * (v - u)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: interval arithmetic only. The square norm of the damped
character prime sum is continuous for positive N, so if it is at most M at every
point of the interval from u to v with u at most v, its integral over that
interval is at most M times the length v minus u. This is the step that turns an
integral estimate into a pointwise estimate and back; it carries no character
information. -/

name: near_positive_sup357
header:
theorem near_positive_sup357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ) →
          ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ C * (N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4: the pointwise bound on the positive side of zero. There
is a fixed positive constant C such that for every large N, every modulus q with
1 at most q at most N to the one seventh, and every nonprincipal character mod q,
the square norm of the damped character prime sum at a phase between 0 and 4 over
N is at most C times N over q times log N to the fifth. This is the local
uniform bound; the integral over the short interval comes later, from step 1. -/

name: near_negative_sup357
header:
theorem near_negative_sup357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ, -(4 / (N : ℝ)) ≤ α →
          α ≤ 0 →
          ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ C * (N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4: the pointwise bound on the negative side of zero. Same
exponent and same shape as step 2, on the reflected interval from minus 4 over N
to 0. The reflection of the phase conjugates the character and replaces it by its
conjugate character, which is again nonprincipal, so this side has its own
constant; it is kept as a separate leaf because it is a separate interval. -/

name: near_constant_selection357
header:
theorem near_constant_selection357 (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (8 : ℝ) * C * Real.log N ^ 5 / (q : ℝ) ≤
          (8 * C) * (N : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 6
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4: the constant and the logarithmic bookkeeping. For every
positive C there is N0 such that for every N beyond N0 and every modulus q at
least one with q at most N to the one seventh, eight C times log N to the fifth
divided by q is at most eight C times N over q times N to the one seventh times
log N to the sixth. The content is the single real inequality: for N at least
two, N to the six sevenths times log N is at least one. -/

name: mellin_near357_split
header:
theorem mellin_near357_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          (∫ α in -(4 / (N : ℝ))..(4 / (N : ℝ)),
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
              B * (N : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 6
doc:
/-- Assembly of `mellin_near357` from the four leaves above: split the central
interval at zero, bound each half through the two pointwise leaves and the
interval-length leaf, and absorb the factor N to the six sevenths through the
constant leaf. No step uses `mellin_near357` itself. -/

name: far_integral_le_sup_length357
header:
theorem far_integral_le_sup_length357 {q : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (N : ℕ)
    (M u v : ℝ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (huv : u ≤ v)
    (hM : ∀ α : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Icc u v → ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ M) :
    (∫ α in u..v, ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2) ≤ M * (v - u)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: interval arithmetic only. If the square norm of the damped
character prime sum is at most M at every point of the interval from u to v, and u
is at most v, then its integral over that interval is at most M times the length
v minus u. This is the step that turns a pointwise estimate into an integral
estimate; it carries no character information and no arithmetic input. -/

name: far_positive_sup357
header:
theorem far_positive_sup357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ,
          4 / (N : ℝ) ≤ α → α ≤ 1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) →
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 10
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4: the pointwise bound on the outer positive interval. There
is a fixed positive constant C such that for every large N, every modulus q with
1 at most q at most N to the one seventh, every nonprincipal character mod q, and
every phase α between 4 over N and 1 over q times N to the one seventh, the square
norm of the damped character prime sum is at most C times N times log N to the
tenth. This is the local uniform estimate; the integral over the interval comes
later, from step 1 and the interval length. -/

name: far_left_endpoint_le_right357
header:
theorem far_left_endpoint_le_right357 (N : ℕ) (hN : 8 ≤ N) :
    ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
      4 / (N : ℝ) ≤ 1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4: the outer positive interval is nonempty. For N at least
eight and every modulus q with 1 at most q at most N to the one seventh, the left
endpoint 4 over N is at most the right endpoint 1 over q times N to the one
seventh. The content is q times N to the one seventh at most N to the two
sevenths, against 4 at most N to the five sevenths; eight is the small case
threshold. -/

name: far_length_le_inverse357
header:
theorem far_length_le_inverse357 (N q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) - 4 / (N : ℝ) ≤
      1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4: the length of the outer positive interval. For every N and
every modulus q at least one, the length 1 over q times N to the one seventh minus
4 over N is at most 1 over q times N to the one seventh. This is the elementary
last step, which discards the left endpoint contribution. -/

name: mellin_positive_far357_split
header:
theorem mellin_positive_far357_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))),
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2) ≤
              B * (N : ℝ) / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) * Real.log N ^ 10
doc:
/-- Assembly of `mellin_positive_far357` from the four leaves above: the assembly
reads the pointwise constant C as the final constant B, checks that the outer
positive interval is nonempty, bounds the integral by the pointwise bound times
the interval length, and discards the left endpoint contribution. No step uses
`mellin_positive_far357` itself. -/

name: lineBound_lnL1622
header:
theorem lineBound_lnL1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          LineBound1622 N B0
            (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Line bound step. Under the hypothesis on the zeros, the logarithm of the
L-function of a nonprincipal character, taken on the line 1/2 + 1/ln N + i t, is
continuous in t and bounded by a constant independent of N times ln cubed of N
times (|t| + 2). This is the only step that uses the zero hypothesis. It carries
no estimate on the difference of the two sums and no Mellin integral. -/

name: mellin_lnL_expansion1622
header:
theorem mellin_lnL_expansion1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ,
      characterPrime280 χ N α -
          mellinU1622 N
            (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))) α
        = -∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Prime power expansion step. The difference between the character prime
sum and the Mellin integral of the logarithm of the L-function is exactly minus
the sum over all primes and all exponents at least two, each term carrying the
value of the character at the prime power and the exponential damping at that
power. This is an identity for every real alpha, with the zero hypothesis only
used to keep the logarithm on one branch and to move the line past the zeros. -/

name: exp_neg_mul_sq_le1622
header:
private lemma exp_neg_mul_sq_le1622 {c x y : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxy : x ≤ y) :
    Real.exp (-(c * y ^ 2)) ≤ Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Prime power expansion step. The difference between the character prime
sum and the Mellin integral of the logarithm of the L-function is exactly minus
the sum over all primes and all exponents at least two, each term carrying the
value of the character at the prime power and the exponential damping at that
power. This is an identity for every real alpha, with the zero hypothesis only
used to keep the logarithm on one branch and to move the line past the zeros. -/
theorem mellin_lnL_expansion1622 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ,
      characterPrime280 χ N α -
          mellinU1622 N
            (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))) α
        = -∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) := by
  sorry

name: exp_neg_mul_sq_antitone1622
header:
private lemma exp_neg_mul_sq_antitone1622 {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    AntitoneOn (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2))) (Set.Ici 0)
doc:
/-- The Gaussian majorant `x ↦ exp (-(c x^2))` is antitone on the nonnegative
half line for a positive `c`. -/

name: summable_exp_neg_mul_sq1622
header:
private lemma summable_exp_neg_mul_sq1622 {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Summable (fun n : ℕ => Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)))
doc:
/-- The Gaussian majorant `x ↦ exp (-(c x^2))` is antitone on the nonnegative
half line for a positive `c`. -/

private lemma exp_neg_mul_sq_antitone1622 {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    AntitoneOn (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2))) (Set.Ici 0) := by
  intro x hx y hy hxy
  simp only
  exact exp_neg_mul_sq_le1622 hc hx hxy

name: tsum_exp_prime_gauss1622
doc:
/-- Summing the Gaussian factor over the primes costs at most half the Gaussian
integral. The primes are a subset of the positive integers, so the sum over the
lattice points below the curve is bounded by the integral test. -/

name: norm_inv_add_two1622
header:
private lemma norm_inv_add_two1622 (k : ℕ) :
    ‖((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹‖ = ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹
doc:
/-- Summing the Gaussian factor over the primes costs at most half the Gaussian
integral. The primes are a subset of the positive integers, so the sum over the
lattice points below the curve is bounded by the integral test. -/

private lemma tsum_exp_prime_gauss1622 {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(c * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2))) ≤
      Real.sqrt (Real.pi / c) / 2 := by
  classical
  have hanti := exp_neg_mul_sq_antitone1622 hc
  have hnonneg : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), 0 ≤ Real.exp (-(c * t ^ 2)) :=
    fun t _ => (Real.exp_pos _).le
  have hint : MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2))) (Set.Ioi 0) :=
    by simpa only [neg_mul] using (integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq hc).integrableOn
  have hsum : Summable (fun n : ℕ => Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2))) :=
    summable_exp_neg_mul_sq1622 hc
  set g1 : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => if 1 ≤ n then Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) else 0 with g1def
  have hg1nn : ∀ n, 0 ≤ g1 n := by
    intro n; simp only [g1def]; split_ifs <;> positivity
  have hg1_le : ∀ n, g1 n ≤ Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) := by
    intro n; simp only [g1def]; split_ifs with h <;> (first | exact le_rfl | positivity)
  have hsum_g1 : Summable g1 := Summable.of_nonneg_of_le hg1nn hg1_le hsum
  -- the prime sum is the sum of `g1` over the primes
  have h1 : (∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(c * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2)))
      = ∑' p : {n : ℕ // n.Prime}, g1 (p : ℕ) := by
    apply tsum_congr
    intro p
    simp only [g1def, ite_eq_left p.property.one_le]
  -- `g1` is the Gaussian sequence with its value at zero removed
  have hg1eq : (fun n : ℕ => g1 n) = fun n : ℕ =>
      if n = 0 then (0 : ℝ) else Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) := by
    funext n
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with h | h
    · subst h; simp [g1def]
    · simp only [g1def, ite_eq_left (show 1 ≤ n from h), ite_eq_right h.ne']
  have hsum' : Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
      if n = 0 then (0 : ℝ) else Real.exp (-(c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2))) := by
    apply Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => by split_ifs <;> positivity)
      (fun n => by split_ifs with h <;> (first | positivity | exact le_rfl)) hsum
  have hshift : (∑' n : ℕ, g1 n) = ∑' k : ℕ, Real.exp (-(c * (((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ 2)) := by
    rw [hg1eq, hsum'.tsum_eq_zero_add]
    simp only [ite_true, zero_add, Nat.succ_ne_zero, ite_false]
  calc (∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(c * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2)))
      = ∑' p : {n : ℕ // n.Prime}, g1 (p : ℕ) := h1
    _ ≤ ∑' n : ℕ, g1 n :=
        hsum_g1.tsum_subtype_le g1 {n : ℕ | Nat.Prime n} hg1nn
    _ = ∑' k : ℕ, Real.exp (-(c * (((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ 2)) := hshift
    _ ≤ ∫ x in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2)) :=
        AntitoneOn.tsum_add_one_le_integral hanti hint hnonneg
    _ = Real.sqrt (Real.pi / c) / 2 := by
        simpa only [neg_mul] using integral_gaussian_Ioi c

name: exp_factor_le1622
doc:
/-- The exponential factor of the `(p, k)` term is at most the Gaussian factor
with the exponent `p^2 2^k`, since `p` is at least two. -/

name: chi_nat_norm_le_one1622
header:
private lemma chi_nat_norm_le_one1622 {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (m : ℕ) : ‖χ m‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- The exponential factor of the `(p, k)` term is at most the Gaussian factor
with the exponent `p^2 2^k`, since `p` is at least two. -/

private lemma exp_factor_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k : ℕ) :
    Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) ≤
      Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))) := by
  apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
  have hp2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  have h2k : (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ k := pow_le_pow_left₀ (by norm_num) hp2 k
  have hkey : (p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) = (p : ℝ) ^ k * (p : ℝ) ^ 2 := by rw [pow_add]
  have hNpos : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hN
  rw [neg_le_neg_iff, hkey]
  apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hNpos.le
  rw [mul_comm ((p : ℝ) ^ 2) ((2 : ℝ) ^ k)]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h2k (by positivity)

name: norm_term_le1622
header:
private lemma norm_term_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) {q : ℕ} [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (α : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k : ℕ) :
    ‖(((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ (p ^ (k + 2)) *
        (Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * ((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
      ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- The exponential factor of the `(p, k)` term is at most the Gaussian factor
with the exponent `p^2 2^k`, since `p` is at least two. -/

private lemma exp_factor_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k : ℕ) :
    Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) ≤
      Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))) := by
  apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
  have hp2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  have h2k : (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ k := pow_le_pow_left₀ (by norm_num) hp2 k
  have hkey : (p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) = (p : ℝ) ^ k * (p : ℝ) ^ 2 := by rw [pow_add]
  have hNpos : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hN
  rw [neg_le_neg_iff, hkey]
  apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hNpos.le
  rw [mul_comm ((p : ℝ) ^ 2) ((2 : ℝ) ^ k)]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h2k (by positivity)


private lemma chi_nat_norm_le_one1622 {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (m : ℕ) : ‖χ m‖ ≤ 1 := by
  have := DirichletCharacter.norm_le_one χ (m : ZMod q)
  simpa using this

name: sqrt_pow1622
header:
private lemma sqrt_pow1622 {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (k : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt (x ^ k) = (Real.sqrt x) ^ k
doc:
/-- The exponential factor of the `(p, k)` term is at most the Gaussian factor
with the exponent `p^2 2^k`, since `p` is at least two. -/

private lemma exp_factor_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k : ℕ) :
    Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) ≤
      Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))) := by
  apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
  have hp2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  have h2k : (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ k := pow_le_pow_left₀ (by norm_num) hp2 k
  have hkey : (p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) = (p : ℝ) ^ k * (p : ℝ) ^ 2 := by rw [pow_add]
  have hNpos : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hN
  rw [neg_le_neg_iff, hkey]
  apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hNpos.le
  rw [mul_comm ((p : ℝ) ^ 2) ((2 : ℝ) ^ k)]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h2k (by positivity)


private lemma chi_nat_norm_le_one1622 {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (m : ℕ) : ‖χ m‖ ≤ 1 := by
  have := DirichletCharacter.norm_le_one χ (m : ZMod q)
  simpa using this

private lemma norm_term_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) {q : ℕ} [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (α : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k : ℕ) :
    ‖(((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ (p ^ (k + 2)) *
        (Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * ((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
      ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))) := by
  have h1 : ‖((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹‖ = ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ := norm_inv_add_two1622 k
  have h2 : ‖χ (p ^ (k + 2))‖ ≤ 1 := by
    simpa [Nat.cast_pow] using chi_nat_norm_le_one1622 χ (p ^ (k + 2))
  have h3 : ‖((Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ =
      Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) := by
    rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _)]
  have h4 : ‖Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * ((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ = 1 :=
    Complex.norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I _
  have hA : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ := by positivity
  have hE : (0 : ℝ) < Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) := Real.exp_pos _
  have hstep : ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * ‖χ (p ^ (k + 2))‖ *
      Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) * 1 ≤
        ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * 1 * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) * 1 := by
    gcongr
  calc ‖(((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ (p ^ (k + 2)) *
        (Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * ((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
      = ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * ‖χ (p ^ (k + 2))‖ *
          Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) * 1 := by
        rw [norm_mul, norm_mul, norm_mul, h1, h3, h4]
    _ ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * 1 * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) * 1 := hstep
    _ = ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) := by ring
    _ ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (exp_factor_le1622 N hN p hp k) (by positivity)

name: sqrt_halves1622
doc:
/-- The square root of the `k`-th power of two is at least the `k`-th power of
three quarters. -/

name: sqrt_pi_mul_le1622
header:
private lemma sqrt_pi_mul_le1622 (N : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt (Real.pi * (N : ℝ)) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)
doc: /-- The Gaussian square root at `N` is at most twice the square root of `N`. -/

name: kterm_bound1622
doc:
/-- Each `k`-th term of the prime power majorant, after the prime sum, is at most
`sqrt N` times the `k`-th power of three quarters. -/

name: summable_majorant_k1622
header:
private lemma summable_majorant_k1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) :
    Summable (fun k : ℕ => ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))))
doc:
/-- The `k`-series of the majorant of the prime power sum is summable: it is
dominated by a geometric series with ratio `exp (-(p^2 / N))`. -/

name: tsum_majorant_le1622
doc: /-- The `k`-series of the majorant is at most `N / p^2`. -/

name: summable_tsum_majorant1622
doc:
/-- The `k`-sums of the majorant are summable over the primes, by comparison
with `N / p^2`. -/

name: summable_majorant_p1622
doc:
/-- For each `k` the majorant is summable over the primes, by comparison with an
inverse square. -/

name: tsum_majorant_p_le1622
header:
private lemma tsum_majorant_p_le1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (k : ℕ) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ *
        Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k / (N : ℝ))))
      ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 2)⁻¹ * (Real.sqrt (Real.pi * (N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ k) / 2)
doc: /-- The prime sum of the majorant at a fixed `k` is at most the Gaussian bound. -/

name: prime_power_tail_bound1622
header:
private lemma prime_power_tail_bound1622 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) {q : ℕ} [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (α : ℝ) :
    ‖∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
        (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
          (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp
              ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
      ≤ 4 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ)
doc:
/-- The prime power tail is at most four times the square root of `N`. The
exponential damping at the prime powers makes every inner series summable, the
prime sums are bounded by the Gaussian integral, and the remaining series in the
exponent is geometric with ratio three quarters. -/

name: prime_power_tail1622
header:
theorem prime_power_tail1622 :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, ∀ α : ℝ,
        ‖∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' k : ℕ,
            (((k : ℂ) + 2)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (k + 2)) *
              (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2) / (N : ℝ))) : ℂ) *
                Complex.exp
                  ((-(2 * Real.pi * α * (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))) : ℝ) * Complex.I))‖
          ≤ B * Real.sqrt N
doc:
/-- LEAF. Prime power tail step. The part of the prime power sum with exponents at
least two, summed over all primes and all such exponents, is at most a constant
times the square root of N. The exponential damping at the powers is what makes
the sum absolutely convergent. No zero hypothesis, no character estimate and no
Mellin integral occur here. -/

name: mellin_transfer1622_split
header:
theorem mellin_transfer1622_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ∃ M : ℝ → ℂ, LineBound1622 N B0 M ∧ ∀ α : ℝ,
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N α - mellinU1622 N M α‖ ≤ B * Real.sqrt N
doc:
/-- The three leaves together give the transfer of the character prime sum to a
Mellin integral on the line, with the coefficient the logarithm of the
L-function. -/

name: mixed_card491
header:
theorem mixed_card491 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] :
    (univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1)).card ≤ q.totient
doc:
/-- LEAF. Counting step of equation 5.5. The number of nonprincipal characters
at a positive modulus is at most the totient of that modulus. At modulus one the
filtered set is empty, so the bound reads zero at most one. No estimate on the
characters themselves and no integral occurs here. -/

name: mixed_principal_gauss491
header:
theorem mixed_principal_gauss491 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    ‖conjugateGauss491 q (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- LEAF. Modulus step of equation 5.5. The conjugate Gauss coefficient of the
principal character at a positive modulus is the Moebius value at the modulus in
absolute value, hence has norm at most one. It carries no frequency, no size of
N, and no character other than the principal one. -/

name: mixed_mass491
header:
theorem mixed_mass491 (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          (∫ α in -(1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))..
              (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))),
            ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N α‖ *
              ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖) ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 6 /
              Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Mass step of equation 5.5. The mixed character mass of one
nonprincipal character: the integral of the principal character prime series
against the nonprincipal one over the local window is at most the scale N times
the sixth power of the logarithm of N over the square root of q times tau. This
is the sixth power form of the mixed mass and it carries no conjugate Gauss
coefficient, no residue sum and no outer character sum. -/

name: mixed_pair_bound491
header:
theorem mixed_pair_bound491 (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        ∀ n : ℤ, ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ‖characterPair491 N q n 1 χ + characterPair491 N q n χ 1‖ ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 6 /
              ((q.totient : ℝ) * Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Pair step of equation 5.5. One nonprincipal character contributes, in
its two orders with the principal character, at most the scale N times the sixth
power of the logarithm of N divided by the totient of q and by the square root of
q times tau. This is the per character form of the displayed mixed bound; it
carries the two conjugate Gauss coefficients, the residue sum and the two
integrals. -/

name: mixed_bound491_split
header:
theorem mixed_bound491_split (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        letI : NeZero q
doc:
/-- The four leaves together give the mixed character estimate of equation 5.5:
the term is a sum over the nonprincipal characters of pairs of ordered character
pairs, so the triangle inequality, the count of those characters and the per
character estimate give the displayed bound. -/

name: near_sup357_origin357
header:
theorem near_sup357_origin357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ‖characterPrime280 χ N 0‖ ^ 2 ≤ C * (N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: the damped character prime sum at phase zero. There is a fixed
positive constant C such that for every large N, every modulus q with 1 at most q at
most N to the one seventh, and every nonprincipal character mod q, the square norm of
the sum at phase zero is at most C times N over q times log N to the fifth. This fixes
the value at one endpoint of the phase range and says nothing about any other phase. -/

name: near_sup357_local_variation357
header:
theorem near_sup357_local_variation357 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 →
          ∀ α : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ) →
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N α - characterPrime280 χ N 0‖ ^ 2 ≤
              C * (4 * α * (N : ℝ)) * ((N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4: the variation of the damped character prime sum across the
permitted phase range. There is a fixed positive constant C such that for every large
N, every modulus q with 1 at most q at most N to the one seventh, every nonprincipal
character mod q and every phase alpha between 0 and 4 over N, the square norm of the
difference between the values at alpha and at zero is at most C times the scaled phase
4 alpha N times N over q times log N to the fifth. The scaled phase is the quantity
that step 4 keeps at most 16; at alpha equal to zero the left side is zero and the
bound is immediate. -/

name: near_sup357_weight_nonneg357
header:
theorem near_sup357_weight_nonneg357 {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) {q : ℕ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4: the weight is nonnegative. For N at least one and q at least
one the product of N over q with log N to the fifth is nonnegative. Both estimates of
steps 1 and 2 are multiplied by this weight in the assembly, so its sign is needed
before the two of them are added. -/

name: near_sup357_phase_length357
header:
theorem near_sup357_phase_length357 {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 ≤ α)
    (hαu : α ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ)) :
    4 * α * (N : ℝ) ≤ 16
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4: the permitted phase range is short. For N at least one and a
phase alpha between 0 and 4 over N, the scaled phase 4 alpha N is at most 16. The
content is that multiplying the phase bound by N gives a bound independent of N; it
carries no character information. -/

name: near_sup357_sq_split357
header:
private lemma near_sup357_sq_split357 (a b : ℂ) :
    ‖a‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ‖b‖ ^ 2 + 2 * ‖a - b‖ ^ 2
doc:
/-- Private helper for the assembly: the square of a norm is at most twice the square
of the norm at a chosen point plus twice the square of the norm of the difference. -/

name: near_sup357_absorb357
doc:
/-- Private helper for the assembly: adding the two leaf estimates, the second one
carrying the extra factor 16, gives the combined constant 2 C plus 32 C'. -/

name: near_positive_sup357_split
header:
theorem near_positive_sup357_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ α : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 4 / (N : ℝ) →
          ‖characterPrime280 χ N α‖ ^ 2 ≤ C * (N : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 5
doc:
/-- Assembly of `near_positive_sup357` from the four leaves above: write the value at
phase alpha as the value at phase zero plus the difference, bound the two parts by
steps 1 and 2, use step 4 to replace the scaled phase by 16 and step 3 for the sign of
the weight, and collect 2 C plus 32 C' as the new constant. No step uses
`near_positive_sup357` itself. -/

name: nonprincipal_character_count491
header:
theorem nonprincipal_character_count491 (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    letI : NeZero q
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step one of the nonprincipal block, the counting step. The nonprincipal
characters of a positive modulus number at most the totient of the modulus, so
the outer sum of the block has at most that many terms. -/

name: nonprincipal_principal_product491
header:
theorem nonprincipal_principal_product491 (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        letI : NeZero q
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step two of the nonprincipal block, the pairs with a principal product,
for one fixed nonprincipal character. The reduced residue phase of such a pair is
an untwisted Ramanujan phase, bounded by the residue count, so this block of
pairs is bounded with one factor of the totient in the denominator and without
any character square saving. -/

name: nonprincipal_off_product491
header:
theorem nonprincipal_off_product491 (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        letI : NeZero q
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step three of the nonprincipal block, the pairs with a nonprincipal
product, for one fixed nonprincipal character. Here the twisted reduced residue
phase is a character sum of nonprincipal product, and the character square
estimate saves the factor of the modulus needed for modulus uniformity, so this
block also carries one factor of the totient in the denominator. -/

name: nonprincipal_bound491_split
header:
theorem nonprincipal_bound491_split (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, ∀ hq : 1 ≤ q, (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        letI : NeZero q
doc:
/-- The nonprincipal block, assembled from the two one-index estimates and the
character count. Each fixed nonprincipal character contributes its principal
product block and its nonprincipal product block, both bounded by the same
quantity, and there are at most a totient of such characters, so the totient
cancels and the modulus disappears from the bound. -/

name: outer_kernel_decay442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_decay442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (α : ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) :
    ∃ K δ : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
      ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
          (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ ≤
        K * Real.exp (-(δ * |t|))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: exponential decay of the kernel factor in the variable of
integration. For N at least three and a frequency in the outer interval, the
complex power and the Gamma factor together are dominated by one exponential
with a positive rate, the two constants depending on N, R and the frequency but
not on the integration variable. No logarithm weight and no coefficient
occurs. -/

name: log_weight_cubic442
header:
theorem log_weight_cubic442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
      Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3 ≤ C * (1 + |t|) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4: the cube of the logarithm weight is bounded by a cubic
polynomial in the absolute value of the integration variable. The constant
depends on N only, and there is no kernel factor here. -/

name: exp_decay_cubic_integrable442
header:
theorem exp_decay_cubic_integrable442 :
    ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → Integrable (fun t : ℝ =>
      Real.exp (-(δ * |t|)) * (1 + |t|) ^ 3)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4: for every positive rate the exponential decay times the
cubic polynomial is integrable on the line. This is the model estimate that the
dominating function has to satisfy, and it carries no kernel, no Gamma factor
and no logarithm of N. -/

name: outer_kernel_aestronglyMeasurable442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_aestronglyMeasurable442 (N : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (α : ℝ) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t : ℝ =>
      ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
          (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
        Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4: strong measurability of the log weighted kernel. The base
is a fixed nonzero complex number, the line is continuous in the variable of
integration and the Gamma factor is continuous on the half plane of positive
real part, which is where the shifted line lies. This is the measurability half
of the conclusion, without any bound. -/

name: outer_kernel_integrable442_split
header:
theorem outer_kernel_integrable442_split (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (α : ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ =>
      ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
          (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
        Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3)
doc:
/-- Assembly of `outer_kernel_integrable442` from the four leaves. The decay
constants and the polynomial constant of the two bounds multiply into the
dominating exponential times cubic, which is integrable by the model estimate,
and the weighted kernel is measurable, so the dominated convergence inequality
for the Bochner integral gives the conclusion. -/

name: outer_kernel_pointwise_mass442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_pointwise_mass442 :
    ∃ G : ℝ, 0 < G ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 3 ≤ N → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R →
      R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
      ∀ α ∈ Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R),
        (∫ t : ℝ,
          ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
              (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
            Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ≤
          G * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4, the pointwise mass bound on the outer interval. There is a
positive constant G such that for N at least three, for every radius R in the
admissible range, and for every frequency α between four over N and one over R,
the absolute Mellin kernel weighted by the cube of the logarithm of N times the
sum of absolute t and two has mass at most G times the square root of N times the
cube of log N. The real part of the Mellin line is at most one for N at least
eight, and the frequency lower bound keeps the imaginary part of the logarithm of
the kernel base away from pi over two by a fixed gap, so the Gamma decay survives
the frequency shift. No square of the mass, no integration over α and no kernel
occurs. -/

name: base_im442
doc: /-- The imaginary part of the Mellin kernel base. -/

name: base_re442
doc: /-- The real part of the Mellin kernel base. -/

name: base_arg_bounds442
doc:
/-- The argument of the Mellin kernel base stays a fixed distance away from both ends of
the upper half axis, uniformly on the outer interval. -/

name: log_cube_le_self442
header: private lemma log_cube_le_self442 {y : ℝ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) : Real.log y ^ 3 ≤ y ^ 3

name: inv_log_le_one442
header: private lemma inv_log_le_one442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) : 1 / Real.log N ≤ 1
doc: /-- One over `log N` is at most one for `N ≥ 3`. -/

name: one_le_log442
header: private lemma one_le_log442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) : (1 : ℝ) ≤ Real.log N

name: mellin_re442
header:
private lemma mellin_re442 (N : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (mellinLine1622 N t).re = 1 / 2 + 1 / Real.log N
doc: /-- The real part of the Mellin line. -/

name: mellin_im442
header: private lemma mellin_im442 (N : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : (mellinLine1622 N t).im = t
doc: /-- The imaginary part of the Mellin line. -/

name: norm_rpow_le442
doc: /-- `‖z‖ ^ (-σ) ≤ N ^ (3/2)` for the Mellin base of the outer interval. -/

name: step_bound442
header:
private lemma step_bound442 (N : ℕ) (t E A : ℝ) (hA : A ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) (hE : 0 ≤ E) :
    A * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * (3 + |t|) * E ≤
      ((N : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) *
          (Real.Gamma (1 / 2) + Real.Gamma (3 / 2) + 4 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))) *
        (1 + |t|) * E
doc: /-- The crude product estimate that absorbs the polynomial factor into the constant. -/

name: integrable_dominant442
header:
private lemma integrable_dominant442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (K δ : ℝ) (hK : 0 ≤ K)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ =>
      K * (1 + |t|) * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3 * Real.exp (-(δ) * |t|))
doc:
/-- The dominating function is integrable on the whole line: a power of `log` times
`1 + |t|` times an exponential decay. -/

name: mellinLine_cont442
header: private lemma mellinLine_cont442 (N : ℕ) : Continuous (mellinLine1622 N)
doc: /-- The Mellin line is continuous in the frequency. -/

name: mellinLine_cont_pair442
header:
private lemma mellinLine_cont_pair442 (N : ℕ) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × ℝ => mellinLine1622 N p.2
doc:
/-- The Mellin line is continuous in the frequency. -/
private lemma mellinLine_cont442 (N : ℕ) : Continuous (mellinLine1622 N) := by
  unfold mellinLine1622
  fun_prop

name: base_cont_pair442
doc: /-- The Mellin kernel base is continuous in the frequency. -/

name: base_slitPlane442
doc: /-- The Mellin kernel base avoids the cut of the complex power. -/

name: gamma_cont_at442
header:
private lemma gamma_cont_at442 {s : ℂ} (h1 : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ s.re) :
    ContinuousAt Complex.Gamma s
doc: /-- The Gamma function is continuous at every point of the right half plane. -/

name: gamma_cont_line442
header:
private lemma gamma_cont_line442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)
doc: /-- The Gamma function is continuous along the Mellin line. -/

name: gamma_cont_pair442
header:
private lemma gamma_cont_pair442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N p.2)
doc:
/-- The Gamma function is continuous along the Mellin line. -/
private lemma gamma_cont_line442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t) := by
  rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
  intro t
  have hlogpos : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log N := by
    have h := one_le_log442 N hN
    linarith
  have hinv : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / Real.log N := by positivity
  have h1 : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ (mellinLine1622 N t).re := by
    rw [mellin_re442]
    linarith
  exact (gamma_cont_at442 h1).comp (mellinLine_cont442 N).continuousAt

name: log_factor_cont_pair442
header:
private lemma log_factor_cont_pair442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :

doc: /-- The logarithm weight is continuous on the product. -/

name: integrand_cont_pair442
header:
private lemma integrand_cont_pair442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :

doc:
/-- The uncurried Mellin integrand is continuous on the plane, so it is jointly
strongly measurable and each frequency slice is continuous in the integration variable. -/

name: arg_lower442
header:
private lemma arg_lower442 (N : ℕ) {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)
    (him : 2 * Real.pi * c ≤ z.im) (hzn : ‖z‖ ≤ 1 + 4 * Real.pi) (hz0 : z ≠ 0)
    (hc : 1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤ 2 * Real.pi * c / (1 + 4 * Real.pi)) :
    1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤ z.arg
doc:
/-- A positive lower bound for the frequency forces a positive lower bound for the
argument of the kernel base, uniform in the frequency. -/

name: kernel_bound_arg442
header:
private lemma kernel_bound_arg442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) {z : ℂ}
    (hre : z.re = 1 / (N : ℝ)) (him : 0 ≤ z.im) (hzn : ‖z‖ ≤ 1 + 4 * Real.pi)
    (harglow : 1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤ z.arg)
    (hargup : z.arg ≤ Real.pi / 2 - 1 / (100 * (N : ℝ))) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖z ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ ≤
      ((N : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) *
          (Real.Gamma (1 / 2) + Real.Gamma (3 / 2) + 4 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))) *
        (1 + |t|) * Real.exp (-(1 / (100 * (N : ℝ))) * |t|)
doc:
/-- A positive lower bound for the frequency forces a positive lower bound for the
argument of the kernel base, uniform in the frequency. -/
private lemma arg_lower442 (N : ℕ) {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)
    (him : 2 * Real.pi * c ≤ z.im) (hzn : ‖z‖ ≤ 1 + 4 * Real.pi) (hz0 : z ≠ 0)
    (hc : 1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤ 2 * Real.pi * c / (1 + 4 * Real.pi)) :
    1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤ z.arg := by
  have hznpos : (0 : ℝ) < ‖z‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hz0
  have h2pic : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.pi * c := by positivity
  have him0 : 0 ≤ z.im := le_trans h2pic him
  have harg0 : 0 ≤ z.arg := Complex.arg_nonneg_iff.mpr him0
  have hsin : Real.sin z.arg = z.im / ‖z‖ := Complex.sin_arg z
  have h1 : Real.sin z.arg ≤ z.arg := Real.sin_le harg0
  have hstep1 : 2 * Real.pi * c / (1 + 4 * Real.pi) ≤ 2 * Real.pi * c / ‖z‖ :=
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_left h2pic hznpos hzn
  have hstep2 : 2 * Real.pi * c / ‖z‖ ≤ z.im / ‖z‖ := by
    rw [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hznpos]
    exact him
  rw [hsin] at h1
  linarith

name: base_norm_le_two442
header:
private lemma base_norm_le_two442 (N : ℕ) (hN1 : 1 ≤ N) {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 ≤ α)
    (hα2 : α ≤ 2) :
    ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖
      ≤ 1 + 4 * Real.pi
doc: /-- The base is bounded in modulus as soon as the frequency is at most two. -/

name: c_bounds442
header:
private lemma c_bounds442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) {R : ℝ} (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)) :
    0 < min (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R) ∧
      1 / (100 * (N : ℝ)) ≤
        2 * Real.pi * min (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R) / (1 + 4 * Real.pi)
doc:
/-- The minimum of the two interval endpoints is positive and supplies the uniform
argument gap of the kernel bound. -/

name: mass_le_dominant442
header:
private lemma mass_le_dominant442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) {R α : ℝ} (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ))
    (hα : α ∈ Set.uIoc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) :
    (∫ t : ℝ,
        ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ≤
      ∫ t : ℝ,
        ((N : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) *
            (Real.Gamma (1 / 2) + Real.Gamma (3 / 2) + 4 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))) *
          (1 + |t|) * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3 *
            Real.exp (-(1 / (100 * (N : ℝ))) * |t|)
doc:
/-- At every frequency of the outer interval the log weighted Mellin kernel mass is
bounded by the integral of the dominating exponential. -/

name: outer_kernel_mass_sq_intervalIntegrable442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_mass_sq_intervalIntegrable442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N)
    (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 ≤ R) (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun α : ℝ =>
      (∫ t : ℝ,
        ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ^ 2) volume
      (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4, the integrability of the squared mass in the frequency.
For N at least three and every admissible radius, the square of the absolute log
weighted Mellin kernel mass is interval integrable over the outer frequency
interval. This is the measure theoretic half of the parent conclusion and
carries no estimate. -/

name: outer_kernel_mass_constant_integral442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_mass_constant_integral442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 8 ≤ N)
    (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 ≤ R) (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)) (G : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G)
    (hmass : ∀ α ∈ Set.Icc (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R),
      (∫ t : ℝ,
        ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ≤
        G * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 3)
    (hInt : IntervalIntegrable (fun α : ℝ =>
      (∫ t : ℝ,
        ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ^ 2) volume
      (4 / (N : ℝ)) (1 / R)) :
    (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R),
      (∫ t : ℝ,
        ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ^ 2) ≤
      G ^ 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.log N ^ 6 * (1 / R - 4 / (N : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4, the frequency integral of a uniform bound. Assume the
weighted mass is at most G times the square root of N times the cube of log N at
every frequency of the outer interval, and assume the square of the mass is
interval integrable there. Then the frequency integral of the squared mass is at
most the square of that bound times the length of the interval, written as one
over R minus four over N. This is the monotonicity of the interval integral
against a constant, and it is the only step where the factor one over R is
produced. -/

name: cont_kernel_inner442
header:
private lemma cont_kernel_inner442 (T : ℝ) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => ∫ u in (-T)..T, 1 / (1 + |t - u|)
doc:
/-- The reciprocal difference kernel on the square box, as a function of the outer
variable, is continuous: the integrand `1 / (1 + |t - u|)` is bounded by one. -/

name: differenceKernel376_self_le
header:
private lemma differenceKernel376_self_le (T : ℝ) (hT : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ T) :
    T ≤ differenceKernel376 T
doc:
/-- The reciprocal difference kernel dominates its own radius once the radius is at
least one half: on the square of radius `T` the bracket is at most `1 + 2 T`, so the
double integral is at least `4 T ^ 2 / (1 + 2 T)`, and that exceeds `T` as soon as
`T ≥ 1/2`. -/

name: sumKernel376_nonneg
header: private lemma sumKernel376_nonneg (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) : 0 ≤ sumKernel376 T
doc: /-- The exponentially decreasing sum kernel is nonnegative. -/

name: outer_kernel_mass_absorb442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_mass_absorb442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (R : ℝ) (hR : 1 ≤ R)
    (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)) (G : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G) :
    G ^ 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.log N ^ 6 * (1 / R - 4 / (N : ℝ)) ≤
      (G ^ 2 + 1) * Real.log N ^ 6 *
          differenceKernel376 ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 3) +
        (G ^ 2 + 1) * Real.log N ^ 7 *
          sumKernel376 ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 3) + (G ^ 2 + 1)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4, absorption by the difference kernel term. For N at least
three, every admissible radius, and every positive G, the crude bound of step
three is at most one plus the square of G times the log sixth power times the
reciprocal difference kernel at radius N over R times log cubed N, plus the same
multiple of the log seventh power times the sum kernel at that radius, plus one.
The radius is at least one, the difference kernel dominates its own radius there,
and log N is at least one, so the log ninth power supplied by the difference
kernel term covers the log sixth power of the crude bound together with the
factor N over R. The sum kernel term is only used as a nonnegative quantity. -/

name: outer_kernel_mass_bound442_split
header:
theorem outer_kernel_mass_bound442_split :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R →
      R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) →
        (∫ α in (4 / (N : ℝ))..(1 / R),
          (∫ t : ℝ,
            ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^
                (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
              Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) ^ 2) ≤
          C * Real.log N ^ 6 * differenceKernel376 ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 3) +
            C * Real.log N ^ 7 * sumKernel376 ((N : ℝ) / R * Real.log N ^ 3) + C
doc:
/-- The parent statement `outer_kernel_mass_bound442`, reassembled from the four
leaves. The constant is one plus the square of the mass constant of step one, and
the threshold is eight so that four over N does not exceed one over R and log N
is at least one. No use of the parent theorem, no sorry. -/

name: exp_neg_abs_le_inv_sq
header:
private lemma exp_neg_abs_le_inv_sq (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (t : ℝ) :

name: integrable_exp_neg_abs_mul

doc:

the absolute kernel mass is dominated by one integrable function of the line
variable, uniformly over the whole outer frequency interval. -/

name: outer_kernel_weight_continuous_alpha442
header:
theorem outer_kernel_weight_continuous_alpha442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (t : ℝ) :

      ‖(((1 / (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((2 * Real.pi * α : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) ^

name: outer_kernel_mass_integrable442_split
header:
theorem outer_kernel_mass_integrable442_split (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (R : ℝ)
    (hR : 1 ≤ R) (hR2 : R ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)) :

    (hZre : ∀ α, (Z α).re = 1 / (N : ℝ)) :
    Continuous (fun α : ℝ =>
      ∫ t : ℝ, ‖Z α ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
        Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3)

name: continuous_kernel_prod442
doc:
/-- The absolute kernel mass is continuous in the frequency. -/
private theorem continuous_mass442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 3 ≤ N) (Z : ℝ → ℂ) (hZc : Continuous Z)
    (hZre : ∀ α, (Z α).re = 1 / (N : ℝ)) :
    Continuous (fun α : ℝ =>
      ∫ t : ℝ, ‖Z α ^ (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
        Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3) := by
  have hN2 : 2 ≤ N := by omega
  have hNr0 : (0 : ℝ) < (N : ℝ) := by
    have h3 : (3:ℝ) ≤ N := by exact_mod_cast hN
    linarith
  have h1N : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / (N : ℝ) := div_pos one_pos hNr0
  have hZslit : ∀ α, Z α ∈ Complex.slitPlane := fun α => Or.inl (by rw [hZre α]; exact h1N)
  rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
  intro α₀
  set a₀ : ℝ := |(Z α₀).arg| with ha₀
  have ha₀lt : a₀ < Real.pi / 2 := by
    rw [ha₀]
    exact Complex.abs_arg_lt_pi_div_two_iff.mpr (Or.inl (by rw [hZre α₀]; exact h1N))
  set δ₀ : ℝ := (Real.pi / 2 - a₀) / 2 with hδ₀def
  have hδ₀ : 0 < δ₀ := by rw [hδ₀def]; linarith
  have hargc : ContinuousAt (fun α => |(Z α).arg|) α₀ :=
    ((Complex.continuousAt_arg (hZslit α₀)).comp hZc.continuousAt).abs
  have hev : ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 α₀, |(Z α).arg| ≤ a₀ + δ₀ := by
    have hlt : ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝 α₀, |(Z α).arg| < a₀ + δ₀ :=
      hargc.eventually_lt continuousAt_const (by linarith)
    filter_upwards [hlt] with α hα using hα.le
  have hboundint : Integrable (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp 1 * Real.sqrt (N:ℝ) * Real.sqrt (2*Real.pi) *

doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3, the kernel layer. On the outer range the log weighted
absolute kernel mass is bounded by one positive constant that does not depend on
the frequency. The frequency enters the kernel only through the base one over N
plus two pi alpha i on the shifted line; the shifted real part is fixed and
positive there, so the complex power and the Gamma factor depend continuously on
the frequency, and a continuous real function is bounded on the closed interval.
No coefficient, no Mellin integral and no integral over the frequency occur. -/

name: line_bound_norm_integral442

      B0 * ∫ t : ℝ,

            (-(mellinLine1622 N t)) * Complex.Gamma (mellinLine1622 N t)‖ *
          Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3, the coefficient layer. The line bound removes the
coefficient from the Mellin integral: the norm of the integral of the kernel
times the coefficient is at most B0 times the log weighted kernel mass. This is
the norm integral inequality together with the pointwise line bound, and it
carries no integrability of the square and no integral over the frequency. It
is not vacuous: the integrability hypothesis is met on the outer range by the
previous step. -/

name: mellinU_sq_aemeasurable442

doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3, the measurable layer. For a coefficient continuous and
bounded by the line bound, the squared norm of the Mellin integral is a
strongly measurable function of the frequency, restricted to the outer range.
This is the measurability half of the conclusion and nothing about size. The
frequency enters only through the base one over N plus two pi alpha i on the
shifted line, where the complex power and the Gamma factor are continuous in
the line variable and dominated by one integrable weight, so the Mellin
integral is continuous and hence strongly measurable in the frequency. PROVED.
It is not vacuous: the coefficient identically one on a large N satisfies the
line bound. -/

name: outer_tail_integrable487

theorem outer_tail_integrable487 :
