header:
theorem prime_phase_periodic442_counterexample468 :
    Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + 0) * (3 : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) ≠
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((1 : ℝ) * (((3 : ℕ) % 2) : ℝ)) / (2 : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * 0 * (3 : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc:
/-- Audit of the sealed phase type at q two, a one, z zero and prime three.
The expected real type makes the remainder a real field remainder. -/

name: prime_phase_periodic442_not_forall468
header:
theorem prime_phase_periodic442_not_forall468 : ¬ (∀ (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (a : ℕ) (z : ℝ) (p : Nat.Primes),
Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * ((a : ℝ) / q + z) * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) =
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (((p : ℕ) % q) : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I))
doc:
/-- The exact quantified type of the sealed phase leaf is false.
This audits the Lean annotation of page 155 equation 2.3. -/

name: nonunit_prime_coset_eq_sum475
header:
theorem nonunit_prime_coset_eq_sum475 (q b : ℕ) (hq : q ≠ 0)
    (hb : ¬ Nat.Coprime b q) (w : ℕ → ℂ) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if (p : ℕ) % q = b then w p else 0) =
      ∑ p ∈ q.primeFactors, if p % q = b then w p else 0
doc:
/-- A noncoprime residue class contains only primes dividing the modulus.
This exact finite identity supplies the omitted classes in page 155 equation 2.3,
and holds for arbitrary complex weights without a convergence premise. -/

name: nonunit_prime_residue_value475
header:
theorem nonunit_prime_residue_value475 (q b : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hb : b < q)
    (hnc : ¬ Nat.Coprime b q) (p : Nat.Primes) (hp : (p : ℕ) % q = b) :
    (p : ℕ) = if b = 0 then q else b
doc:
/-- On a nonunit canonical residue class, the only eligible prime is the
residue itself, except that residue zero can contain the modulus as a prime.
This spells out the support assertion behind page 155 equation 2.3. -/

name: nonunit_prime_coset_eq_term475
header:
theorem nonunit_prime_coset_eq_term475 (q b : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hb : b < q)
    (hnc : ¬ Nat.Coprime b q) (w : ℕ → ℂ) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if (p : ℕ) % q = b then w p else 0) =
      if Nat.Prime (if b = 0 then q else b) then w (if b = 0 then q else b) else 0
doc:
/-- A canonical nonunit prime coset series has at most one term, with any
complex weights. The candidate is the residue, or the modulus for residue zero.
This is an exact form of the support estimate on page 155 equation 2.3. -/

name: nonunit_coset_norm_le_primeFactors442
header:
theorem nonunit_coset_norm_le_primeFactors442 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (z : ℝ) (a : ℕ) :
    ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖
      ≤ ∑ p ∈ q.primeFactors, ‖(Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * (p : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3: the support and norm bound for the non unit residue
classes. The coset phase has modulus one, a finite sum of coset series is at
most the sum of their norms, and only the prime divisors of the modulus can have
a residue class that is not invertible modulo the modulus, so the whole non unit
coset sum is dominated by the sum over the prime divisors of the modulus of the
modulus of the damped prime term. No estimate in the number of divisors and no
summation over residues occurs. -/

name: prime_class_term_norm_le_one442
header:
theorem prime_class_term_norm_le_one442 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (z : ℝ) (p : ℕ) :
    ‖(Real.exp (-((p : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * (p : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3: the damping bound for a single prime class term. The
exponential damping has modulus `exp (-(p/N))` at most one because the exponent
is nonpositive, and the oscillating factor in the shift has modulus one because
its real part vanishes, so the product has modulus at most one. This holds for
every natural index, including zero, and involves no division in the exponent by
zero since the bound does not need the modulus to be positive. -/

name: nonunit_prime_coset_norm_le_one475
header:
theorem nonunit_prime_coset_norm_le_one475 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (z : ℝ) (b : ℕ) (hb : b < q) (hnc : ¬ Nat.Coprime b q) :
    ‖∑' p : Nat.Primes, if (p : ℕ) % q = b then
      (Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) else 0‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- Each canonical nonunit prime coset has norm at most one. This is the
individual class estimate used in the error on page 155 equation 2.3. -/

name: prime_factors_card_le_log442
header:
theorem prime_factors_card_le_log442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    ((q.primeFactors.card : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.log q
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3: the count of the prime divisors of the modulus. Their
product divides the modulus and each of them is at least two, so the modulus is
at least `2` to the number of them; taking logarithms and using that the
logarithm of two exceeds one half gives the number of prime divisors at most
twice the logarithm of the modulus. This is elementary arithmetic on divisors
and needs no prime series. -/

name: prime_divisor_class_mass442_split
header:
theorem prime_divisor_class_mass442_split (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      (q.totient : ℝ) * (2 * Real.log q) ^ 2
doc:
/-- Assembly of `prime_divisor_class_mass442` from the three leaves. Each non
unit coset sum is dominated by the prime divisors of the modulus, each of those
terms has modulus at most one, and there are at most `2 log q` of them, so every
reduced residue contributes at most the square of `2 log q`; summing over the
reduced residues multiplies by the totient. -/

name: principal_integral_amplitude491
header:
theorem principal_integral_amplitude491 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The size step. The principal square integral over the short arc, taken in
absolute value, is bounded by the two printed error sizes alone: the reciprocal of
the arc length and the reciprocal of the square root of the arc length, both times N
and the thirteenth power of the logarithm. Nothing is subtracted from the integral,
no character twist occurs, and the residual may be any integer at most N. -/

name: principal_convolution_unit_modulus491
header:
theorem principal_convolution_unit_modulus491 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → q = 1 → ∀ n : ℤ, 4 ≤ n → n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n -
          ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The unit modulus step. At modulus one the reduced residue set is the single
residue zero, the principal character series is the full prime Fourier series, and
the arc is the longest one the parameter range allows. For every residual from four
up to N the square integral differs from the exactly damped logarithmic convolution
by at most the two printed error sizes. -/

name: principal_convolution_intermediate_modulus491
header:
theorem principal_convolution_intermediate_modulus491 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        2 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 20 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, 4 ≤ n → n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n -
          ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The intermediate modulus step. For a modulus between two and the one
twentieth power of N, a reduced residue twist is present but the arc is still long,
so both printed error sizes are needed. For every residual from four up to N the
square integral differs from the exactly damped logarithmic convolution by at most
the two printed error sizes. -/

name: principal_convolution_large_modulus491
header:
theorem principal_convolution_large_modulus491 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) →
        2 ≤ q → (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 20 : ℝ) ≤ (q : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, 4 ≤ n → n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n -
          ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- LEAF. The large modulus step. For a modulus at least the one twentieth power of N
the arc is short and the reciprocal length term is the smaller of the two printed
error sizes, while the square root term and the thirteenth power of the logarithm are
the ones that survive. For every residual from four up to N the square integral
differs from the exactly damped logarithmic convolution by at most the two printed
error sizes. -/

name: scale_const_le491
header:
private theorem scale_const_le491 {c d N lg L : ℝ} (hcd : c ≤ d) (hN : 0 ≤ N)
    (hlg : 0 ≤ lg) (hL : 0 ≤ L) : c * N * lg * L ≤ d * N * lg * L
doc: /-- Folding a constant into a larger one, at a fixed nonnegative error size. -/

name: principal_convolution491_split
header:
theorem principal_convolution491_split (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (hM : MellinBound280) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ) → ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ N →
        ‖principalIntegral491 N q n -
          ((Real.exp (-(n.toNat : ℝ) / N) * logConvolution1622 n.toNat : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) * Real.log N ^ 13 *
            (1 / ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) +
              1 / Real.sqrt ((q : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- The principal convolution estimate, assembled from the four case steps. The
statement is the sealed one, unchanged. At a residual at most three the convolution
is the empty sum, so the size step alone suffices; above three the four modulus cases
cover every positive modulus, and the constants are added. -/

name: principal_mass435_local_mass
header:
theorem principal_mass435_local_mass (N q : ℕ) (r : ℝ)
    (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr : r ≤ 1 / 2) :
    (∫ z in -r..r, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
      ∫ z in -(1 / 2)..(1 / 2),
        ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. The first step of the proof: the local interval is enlarged to the full
period of radius one half. The squared norm kernel is nonnegative and
continuous in the frequency variable, so the integral over the smaller interval
is at most the integral over the larger one. This is the point where the radius r
leaves the statement; what remains is the full period at radius one half. True
also at r equal to zero, where the left side is the empty interval integral and
vanishes. -/

name: principal_mass435_period_shift
header:
theorem principal_mass435_period_shift (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∫ z in -(1 / 2)..(1 / 2),
        ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) =
      ∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. The second step of the proof: the half open period of radius one half
carries the same mass as the unit interval. Every summand of the prime series is
a character value times a decaying weight times a complex exponential of period
one in the frequency variable, so the squared norm kernel is periodic with period
one and the two interval integrals agree. This is an identity, not an estimate. -/

name: principal_mass435_orthogonality
header:
theorem principal_mass435_orthogonality (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
      ∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(2 * (p : ℝ)) / N)
doc:
/-- LEAF. The third step of the proof: Fourier orthogonality over one full period
turns the squared norm integral of the prime series into the diagonal sum of the
squared weights. The trivial character takes the value one on every prime, so
each squared weight is the square of the exponential damping, and the
interference terms of distinct primes integrate to zero. This is where the
character disappears from the bound; the radius one half is what makes the
period complete. -/

name: principal_mass435_full_period_eq477
header:
theorem principal_mass435_full_period_eq477 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∫ z in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) N z‖ ^ 2) =
      ∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(2 * (p : ℝ)) / N)
doc:
/-- Page 159 before equation 5.3. Exact Parseval diagonal at modulus one.
Every prime has principal character value one, so the squared damping is
exp of negative twice the prime over N. -/

name: principal_mass435_exponential_sum
header:
theorem principal_mass435_exponential_sum :
    ∃ P : ℝ, 0 < P ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 3 ≤ N →
      (∑' p : Nat.Primes, Real.exp (-(2 * (p : ℝ)) / N)) ≤
        P * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N)
doc:
/-- LEAF. The fourth step of the proof: the diagonal prime sum is at most a
constant times N over log N. The exponential damping gives geometric decay past
the scale N, and partial summation against the prime count converts the surviving
range into the reciprocal logarithm. This is the only analytic input of the
split and it is why the saving over N is a logarithm rather than a power; it
carries the whole unconditional content of the principal mass. -/

name: principal_mass435_split
header:
theorem principal_mass435_split :
    ∃ P : ℝ, 0 < P ∧ ∀ (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (r : ℝ), 3 ≤ N → 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 / 2 →
      (∫ z in -r..r, ‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2) ≤
        P * ((N : ℝ) / Real.log N)
doc:
/-- Page 159 before equation 5.3. The exact statement of principal_mass435,
proved from the four supplies above without using it: enlarge the local interval
to the half open period, shift to the unit interval, apply orthogonality, and pay
the prime sum by the reciprocal logarithm. -/

name: prime_class_split1622
header:
theorem prime_class_split1622 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) (a : ℕ) :
    primeFourier111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z) =
      (∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q),
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)) +
      (∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q),
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3, the residue class splitting identity. The prime series at the
shifted reduced fraction is the sum of its unit coset part and its non unit coset part,
where the coset of residue `b` carries the phase `exp (-2 pi i a b / q)` and the coset
series holds the damping and the oscillation in the shift only. Each coset series is
absolutely convergent, so the regrouping of the prime series by the residue of the prime
modulo `q` is an identity and no estimate occurs. -/

name: unit_character_orthogonality1622
header:
theorem unit_character_orthogonality1622 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q),
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
            Complex.I) *
          (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
            ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
              Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      1 / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2 +
            (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
              ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3, unit orthogonality with the Gauss numbers. On the cosets coprime to
the modulus the coset phases form the character table up to Gauss numbers, so the sum over
the reduced residues of the squared moduli of the unit coset sums is at most one over the
totient times the principal character square plus `q` times the nonprincipal character
squares. The principal Gauss number has modulus at most one, every other one has squared
modulus at most the modulus, and the coset sums of the unit part are the character prime
sums of the statement. No integral and no shift estimate occurs. -/

name: prime_divisor_class_mass1622
header:
theorem prime_divisor_class_mass1622 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q),
          Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
            Complex.I) *
          (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
            ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
              Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      (q.totient : ℝ) * (2 * Real.log q) ^ 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3, the mass of the residue cosets that are not coprime to the modulus.
A prime in such a coset is divisible by the greatest common divisor of that coset and the
modulus, hence equals one of the prime divisors of the modulus, so only one coset per
prime divisor is nonempty. There are at most `log q / log 2` of those, each nonempty coset
series holds a single damped term and so has modulus at most one, and therefore the sum
over the reduced residues of the squared moduli of the non unit coset sums is at most the
totient times the square of `2 log q`. -/

name: rational_pointwise_characters1622_split
header:
theorem rational_pointwise_characters1622_split :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ N → 2 ≤ q → ∀ z : ℝ,
      (∑ a ∈ (Finset.range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ‖primeFourier111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      B / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2 +
          (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2) +
        B * (q.totient : ℝ) * Real.log q ^ 2
doc:
/-- The pointwise finite character estimate, from the three layers below it. The splitting
identity writes each prime series as a unit part plus a non unit part, the square of a sum
is at most twice the sum of the squares, and the constants `2` and `8` absorb the two leaf
bounds into the single constant `8`. The statement is unchanged. -/

name: geom_exp_sum442
doc: /-- The finite geometric sum of the `m`-th roots of unity vanishes for `m ≥ 2`. -/

name: stdAddChar_nat442
doc: /-- The standard additive character on `ZMod q`, evaluated at a natural number. -/

name: stdAddChar_nat_neg_mul442
doc: /-- The standard additive character at a negated product of natural numbers. -/

name: sum_units_eq_filter442
doc:
/-- Reindexing: a sum over the unit group of `ZMod q` is a sum over the reduced
residue system in `range q`. -/

name: sum_units_eq_filter_real442
doc:
/-- Reindexing: a sum over the unit group of `ZMod q` is a sum over the reduced
residue system in `range q`, real valued form. -/

name: sum_zmod_eq_units442
header:
private lemma sum_zmod_eq_units442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (G : ZMod q → M) (hG : ∀ x, ¬ IsUnit x → G x = 0) :
    (∑ x : ZMod q, G x) = ∑ u : (ZMod q)ˣ, G (u : ZMod q)
doc:
/-- A sum over `ZMod q` of a function vanishing off the units is a sum over the
unit group. -/

name: star_stdAddChar442
header:
private lemma star_stdAddChar442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (x : ZMod q) :
    star (ZMod.stdAddChar x) = ZMod.stdAddChar (-x)
doc: /-- The conjugate of the standard additive character is its negative. -/

name: char_orth_pair442
header:
private lemma char_orth_pair442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ ξ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    [Decidable (χ = ξ)] :
    (∑ u : (ZMod q)ˣ, χ (u : ZMod q) * star (ξ (u : ZMod q)))
      = if χ = ξ then (q.totient : ℂ) else 0
doc: /-- Orthogonality of the character table of the unit group, in conjugate form. -/

name: star_char_apply442
doc: /-- The conjugate of a character value at a unit is its value at the inverse. -/

name: gauss_twist442
header:
private lemma gauss_twist442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (u : (ZMod q)ˣ) :
    (∑ v : ZMod q, ZMod.stdAddChar (-(v * (u : ZMod q))) * χ⁻¹ v)
      = star (gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar) * χ (u : ZMod q)
doc:
/-- Twisting the standard additive character by a unit and summing against the
inverse character multiplies the Gauss sum by the character value. -/

name: parseval_char442
header:
private lemma parseval_char442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (f : DirichletCharacter ℂ q → ℂ) :
    (∑ u : (ZMod q)ˣ,
        (∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, f χ * χ (u : ZMod q))
          * star (∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, f χ * χ (u : ZMod q)))
      = (q.totient : ℂ) * ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, f χ * star (f χ)
doc:
/-- Parseval for the character table of the unit group: the mean square of a
character combination is the totient times the squared coefficients. -/

name: char_expansion442
doc: /-- Expansion of a function on `ZMod q` in the character table of the unit group. -/

name: norm_char_apply442
header:
private lemma norm_char_apply442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (u : (ZMod q)ˣ) : ‖χ (u : ZMod q)‖ = 1
doc: /-- Unit character values have modulus one. -/

name: parseval_zmod442
doc: /-- Parseval for the discrete Fourier transform on `ZMod q`, in conjugate form. -/

name: parseval_norm_zmod442
header:
private lemma parseval_norm_zmod442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (F : ZMod q → ℂ) :
    (∑ k : ZMod q, ‖ZMod.dft F k‖ ^ 2) = (q : ℝ) * ∑ j : ZMod q, ‖F j‖ ^ 2
doc: /-- Parseval for the discrete Fourier transform on `ZMod q`, in norm form. -/

name: gauss_bound_nonprincipal442
doc: /-- The non principal Gauss number has squared modulus at most the modulus. -/

name: moebius_sum_eq442
header:
private lemma moebius_sum_eq442 (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius d : ℤ) : ℂ)) = if n = 1 then 1 else 0
doc: /-- The sum of the Möbius function over the divisors of a positive integer. -/

name: gauss_principal_eq442
doc: /-- The principal Gauss number is a Möbius value. -/

name: gauss_bound_principal442
header:
private lemma gauss_bound_principal442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    ‖gaussSum (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) ZMod.stdAddChar‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1
doc: /-- The principal Gauss number has modulus at most one. -/

name: parseval_norm_char442
doc: /-- Parseval for the character table of the unit group, in norm form. -/

name: core_orthogonality442
header:
private lemma core_orthogonality442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 2 ≤ q) (G : ZMod q → ℂ)
    (hG : ∀ x, ¬ IsUnit x → G x = 0) :
    (∑ u : (ZMod q)ˣ, ‖∑ v : ZMod q,
        (ZMod.stdAddChar (-(v * (u : ZMod q))) : ℂ) * G v‖ ^ 2)
      ≤ 1 / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (‖∑ x : ZMod q, G x‖ ^ 2
          + (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
              ‖∑ x : ZMod q, χ x * G x‖ ^ 2)
doc:
/-- The mean square of the transformed coset series is bounded by the totient
inverse of the character prime sums, the principal one with weight one and the
others with weight the modulus. -/

name: fiber442
header:
private lemma fiber442 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ)
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    characterPrime280 χ N z
      = ∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q),
          χ (b : ZMod q) * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
            ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
              Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)
doc: /-- The character prime series is the character weighted sum of the coset series. -/

name: circle_exp_coset442
header:
private lemma circle_exp_coset442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (z : ℝ) (a : ℕ) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    Circle.exp (-(2 * Real.pi * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) + z) * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ))) =
      Circle.exp (-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * ((((p : ℕ) % q : ℕ)) : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ)))) *
        Circle.exp (-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)))
doc:
/-- The phase of the prime term at the shifted reduced fraction is the coset
phase of the residue class of the prime, times the phase of the shift alone, on
the unit circle: only the exponent modulo `2 pi` matters. -/

name: exp_arg_coset442
header:
private lemma exp_arg_coset442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (z : ℝ) (a : ℕ) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) + z) * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I) =
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * ((((p : ℕ) % q : ℕ)) : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc: /-- The same identity for the complex exponential. -/

name: prime_class_split442
header:
theorem prime_class_split442 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) (a : ℕ) :
    primeFourier111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z) =
      (∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)) +
      (∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3: the residue coset splitting identity. The prime series at
the shifted reduced fraction is the sum, over the residue cosets of the
modulus, of the coset phase times the coset series, the latter carrying the
damping and the oscillation in the shift but not the shift by the fraction.
Each coset series is absolutely convergent, so the regrouping is an identity and
no estimate is involved. -/

name: unit_character_orthogonality442
header:
theorem unit_character_orthogonality442 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      1 / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2 +
            (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
              ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3: unit character orthogonality with the Gauss numbers. On
the cosets coprime to the modulus the coset phases form the character table up
to Gauss numbers, so the sum of squared coset sums over the reduced residues is
the squared character prime sums weighted by the squared Gauss numbers, divided
by the totient. The principal Gauss number has modulus at most one, every other
one has squared modulus at most the modulus, and the coset sums are exactly the
character prime sums of the statement, the characters themselves vanishing on
the prime divisors of the modulus, so the two sides are identified character by
character. No integral and no shift estimate occurs. -/

name: mem_primeFactors_iff_not_coprime_mod442
header:
private lemma mem_primeFactors_iff_not_coprime_mod442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    ¬ Nat.Coprime ((p : ℕ) % q) q ↔ (p : ℕ) ∈ q.primeFactors
doc:
/-- Membership of a prime in the prime divisors of the modulus, detected on its
residue class: a prime residue class is non invertible modulo the modulus exactly
when the prime divides the modulus. -/

name: primeFactors_card_le_log442
header:
private lemma primeFactors_card_le_log442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    ((q.primeFactors.card : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.log q
doc:
/-- The number of distinct prime divisors of the modulus is at most twice its
logarithm, for `q >= 2`. -/

name: sum_coset_swap442
header:
private lemma sum_coset_swap442 (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (s : Finset ℕ) (hs : s ⊆ Finset.range q)
    (Ψ : ℕ → ℂ) (hΨ : ∀ b ∈ s, ‖Ψ b‖ ≤ 1) (w : Nat.Primes → ℂ) (hw : Summable w) :
    (∑ b ∈ s, Ψ b * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then w p else 0)) =
      ∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q) ∈ s then Ψ ((p : ℕ) % q) * w p else 0
doc:
/-- Summing a coset-supported prime series over a set of residues and then summing
the coset sums exchanges the two summations. -/

name: prime_divisor_class_mass442
header:
theorem prime_divisor_class_mass442 (N q : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => ¬ Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) *
          Complex.I) *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then
          ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) *
            Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      (q.totient : ℝ) * (2 * Real.log q) ^ 2
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3: the mass of the residue cosets that are not coprime to
the modulus. A prime in such a coset is divisible by the greatest common divisor
of the coset and the modulus, hence equals one of the prime divisors of the
modulus, so only one coset per prime divisor is nonempty. There are at most
`log q / log 2` of those, each coset series has modulus at most one because it
holds a single damped term, and therefore the squared sum over the reduced
residues of the non unit coset sums is at most the totient times the square of
`2 log q`. -/

name: rational_pointwise_characters442_split
header:
theorem rational_pointwise_characters442_split :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ N → 2 ≤ q → ∀ z : ℝ,
      (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
        ‖primeFourier111 N ((a : ℝ) / q + z)‖ ^ 2) ≤
      B / (q.totient : ℝ) *
        (‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2 +
          (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1),
            ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2) +
        B * (q.totient : ℝ) * Real.log q ^ 2
doc:
/-- Assembly of `rational_pointwise_characters442` from the three leaves. The
splitting identity writes each prime series as a unit part plus a non unit part,
the square of a sum is at most twice the squares, and the constants `2` and `8`
absorb the two leaf bounds into the single constant `8` of the statement. -/

name: primeTailTermLe357
header:
private lemma primeTailTermLe357 (x m : ℕ) :
    (if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0) ≤ 4 / (m : ℝ) ^ 2
doc:
/-- The tail function on the natural numbers, `1/(m-1)²` past the cut off, is summable:
it is dominated by `4/m²`, and `m ≤ 2(m-1)` for `m ≥ 2`. -/

name: primeTailSummable357
header:
private lemma primeTailSummable357 (x : ℕ) :
    Summable (fun m : ℕ => if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0)
doc:
/-- The tail function on the natural numbers, `1/(m-1)²` past the cut off, is summable:
it is dominated by `4/m²`, and `m ≤ 2(m-1)` for `m ≥ 2`. -/
private lemma primeTailTermLe357 (x m : ℕ) :
    (if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0) ≤ 4 / (m : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  by_cases hxm : x < m
  · rw [if_pos hxm]
    have hm1 : 1 ≤ m := by omega
    rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hm1 with h | h
    · subst h
      norm_num
    · have hm2 : 2 ≤ m := h
      have hmR : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm2
      have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by linarith
      have hpos' : (0 : ℝ) < ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 := by nlinarith
      rw [div_le_div_iff₀ hpos' (by positivity)]
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg ((m : ℝ) - 1)]
  · rw [if_neg hxm]
    positivity

name: primeTailTsumLe357
header:
private lemma primeTailTsumLe357 (x : ℕ) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes,
        (if x < (p : ℕ) then 1 / (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0)) ≤
      ∑' m : ℕ, (if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0)
doc:
/-- The sum over the primes is at most the sum over the natural numbers, since the
latter dominates term by term. -/

name: hasSum_shift_diff357
header:
private lemma hasSum_shift_diff357 (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    HasSum (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + a) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + a + 1)) (1 / a)
doc:
/-- Telescoping: the difference of consecutive reciprocal shifts sums to the first
term. -/

name: tailShift357
doc: /-- The tail is the sum of `1/(k+x)²` over `k`, with the cut off removed. -/

name: primeTailNatLe357
header:
private lemma primeTailNatLe357 (x : ℕ) (hx : 2 ≤ x) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, (if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0)) ≤ 2 / (x : ℝ)
doc: /-- The full natural-number tail is at most `2/x` for `x ≥ 2`. -/

name: primePowNotSquarefree357
header:
private lemma primePowNotSquarefree357 {p i : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hi : 2 ≤ i) :
    ¬ Squarefree (p ^ i)
doc:
/-- The full natural-number tail is at most `2/x` for `x ≥ 2`. -/
private lemma primeTailNatLe357 (x : ℕ) (hx : 2 ≤ x) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, (if x < m then 1 / ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0)) ≤ 2 / (x : ℝ) := by
  have hxR : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (x : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hx
  rw [tailShift357 x]
  have ha : (0 : ℝ) < (x : ℝ) - 1 := by linarith
  have htel := hasSum_shift_diff357 ((x : ℝ) - 1) ha
  have hsumtel : Summable (fun k : ℕ =>
      1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1)) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1) + 1)) := htel.summable
  have hpoint : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤
      1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1)) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1) + 1) := by
    intro k
    have ht : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) := by
      have hk : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg k
      linarith
    have hd : (0 : ℝ) < (k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1 := by linarith
    have hd' : (0 : ℝ) < (k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) := by linarith
    have hkey : 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ))
        = 1 / (((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) * ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ))) := by
      field_simp
      ring
    have hden : (0 : ℝ) < ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) * ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) := by positivity
    have hstep : 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) ^ 2
        ≤ 1 / (((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) * ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ))) := by
      rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) hden]
      nlinarith
    calc 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) ^ 2
        ≤ 1 / (((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) * ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ))) := hstep
      _ = 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ) - 1) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) := hkey.symm
      _ = 1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1)) - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + ((x : ℝ) - 1) + 1) := by
          ring_nf
  have hsumlhs : Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) ^ 2) :=
    Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (g := fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + (x : ℝ)) ^ 2) (fun k => by positivity)
      hpoint hsumtel
  have hle := Summable.tsum_le_tsum (L := SummationFilter.unconditional ℕ) hpoint hsumlhs hsumtel
  rw [htel.tsum_eq] at hle
  refine hle.trans ?_
  rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) < (x : ℝ))]
  linarith

/-! ### The Ramanujan weight of the singular series as the Heath-Brown coefficient -/

name: ramWeightMul357
header:
private lemma ramWeightMul357 (n a b : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hcop : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius (a * b) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (((a * b).totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum (a * b) n =
      ((((ArithmeticFunction.moebius a : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((a.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum a n) *
        ((((ArithmeticFunction.moebius b : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((b.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum b n)
doc: /-- The Ramanujan weight is multiplicative across coprime moduli, in `ℂ`. -/

name: ramWeightPrime357
header:
private lemma ramWeightPrime357 (n p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius p : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((p.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum p n
      = (LeanLab.HeathBrown1985.vloc n p : ℂ)
doc: /-- At a prime modulus the Ramanujan weight is the local factor of the singular series. -/

name: ramWeightEqGm357
header:
private lemma ramWeightEqGm357 (n q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((q.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re
      = LeanLab.HeathBrown1985.gm n q
doc: /-- The Ramanujan weight of the singular series is the Heath-Brown coefficient `g_n`. -/

name: ramWeightMulReal357
header:
private lemma ramWeightMulReal357 (n a b : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    (ArithmeticFunction.moebius (a * b) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (((a * b).totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum (a * b) n).re
      = ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius a : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((a.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
          (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum a n).re) *
        ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius b : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((b.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
          (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum b n).re)
doc: /-- The Ramanujan weight is multiplicative on coprime moduli, in `ℝ`. -/

name: ramWeightSummable357
header:
private lemma ramWeightSummable357 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Summable (fun q : ℕ =>
      ‖(ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((q.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re‖)
doc:
/-- The Ramanujan weight is summable in absolute value, because it is the Heath-Brown
coefficient `g_n` and `Σ_q |g_n(q)|` converges. -/

name: ramWeightLocalFactor357
header:
private lemma ramWeightLocalFactor357 (n p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    1 + (ArithmeticFunction.moebius p : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((p.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum p n).re
      = (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)
doc: /-- At a prime modulus the local factor of the Euler product is the singular-series factor. -/

name: succLeTwoPow357
header:
private lemma succLeTwoPow357 (a : ℕ) :
    (a : ℝ) + 1 ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (50 : ℕ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ ((a : ℝ) / 50)
doc:
/-- At a prime modulus the local factor of the Euler product is the singular-series factor. -/
private lemma ramWeightLocalFactor357 (n p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    1 + (ArithmeticFunction.moebius p : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((p.totient : ℝ)) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum p n).re
      = (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2) := by
  have hφ : (p.totient : ℝ) = (p : ℝ) - 1 := by
    rw [Nat.totient_prime hp, Nat.cast_sub hp.one_le]
    norm_num
  have hμ : ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius p : ℝ)) = -1 := by
    rw [ArithmeticFunction.moebius_apply_prime hp]
    norm_num
  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) < (p : ℝ) - 1 := by
    have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp.two_le
    linarith
  have hne : ((p : ℝ) - 1) ≠ 0 := h1.ne'
  have hc : (((p : ℂ) - 1)).re = (p : ℝ) - 1 := by
    rw [show ((p : ℂ) - 1) = (((p : ℝ) - 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) by push_cast; ring]
    simp
  rw [hμ, hφ, LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum_prime p n hp,
    show ((-1 : ℝ) ^ 2) = 1 by norm_num, one_div, one_div]
  by_cases hd : p ∣ n
  · simp only [if_pos hd, hc]
    field_simp
  · simp only [if_neg hd]
    norm_num
    field_simp
    ring

doc:

private lemma ramWeightOne357 (n : ℕ) :

name: ramWeightCoprime357
header:
private lemma ramWeightCoprime357 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) {a b : ℕ} (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    (fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *

doc: /-- The Ramanujan weight is multiplicative on coprime moduli. -/

name: ramWeightSubtypeLe357
header:
private lemma ramWeightSubtypeLe357 (n x : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (T : Set ℕ) (hT : ∀ m : ℕ, m ∈ T → ‖(fun q : ℕ =>
      (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) m‖ =
      (if x < m then ‖(fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 /
        (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) m‖ else 0)) :
    ‖∑' m : ↑T, (fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 /
      (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) ↑m‖
      ≤ ∑' q : ℕ, if x < q then
          ‖(fun r : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius r : ℝ) ^ 2 / (r.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
            (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum r n).re) q‖ else 0
doc:
/-- The Ramanujan weight is multiplicative on coprime moduli. -/
private lemma ramWeightCoprime357 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) {a b : ℕ} (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    (fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) (a * b) =
      (fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
          (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) a *
        (fun q : ℕ => (ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 *
          (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) b := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos a with h0 | ha
  · subst h0
    have hb : b = 1 := (Nat.coprime_zero_left b).mp hab
    subst hb
    simp [ramWeightZero357, ramWeightOne357]
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b with h0 | hb
  · subst h0
    have ha1 : a = 1 := (Nat.coprime_zero_right a).mp hab
    subst ha1
    simp [ramWeightZero357, ramWeightOne357]
  · exact ramWeightMulReal357 n a b hn ha hb hab

name: singular_series_has_sum357
header:
theorem singular_series_has_sum357 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    HasSum (fun q : ℕ =>
      ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2) *
        (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re) (singularSeries111 n)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 3: the Euler product identity. The weight sending q to the
square of the Moebius function at q over the square of the totient of q, times
the real part of the Ramanujan sum of q at n, is multiplicative across coprime
moduli and is supported on squarefree q, so the series over all q converges and
its sum is the Euler product over the primes that defines the singular series.
This is the identity alone: it carries no truncation, no rate and no uniformity
in N. -/

name: truncated_sum_euler_error357
header:
theorem truncated_sum_euler_error357 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
        |truncatedSingular357 N n -
          (∏ p ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊).filter Nat.Prime,
            (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2))| ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 100 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 3: the truncated sum against the finite product of local
factors. The finite Ramanujan sum over the moduli from one to N to the one tenth
differs from the product over the primes up to N to the one tenth of the local
factor 1 plus 1 over p minus 1 at a prime dividing n and 1 minus the inverse
square of p minus 1 at a prime not dividing n, by at most an absolute constant
times N to the minus one hundredth. The content is the divisor expansion of the
Ramanujan sum, which makes the squarefree weight multiplicative, together with
the bound on the squarefree moduli beyond the cut off. The saving one hundredth
is far weaker than the one tenth power of the cut off that the argument leaves
free. -/

name: prime_product_series_tail357
header:
theorem prime_product_series_tail357 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
        |(∏ p ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊).filter Nat.Prime,
            (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)) -
          (∑' q : ℕ, ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2) *
            (LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n).re)| ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 100 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 3: the finite product against the full series. The product
over the primes up to N to the one tenth of the same local factors differs from
the sum of the full Ramanujan weight series by at most an absolute constant
times N to the minus one hundredth. The content is that every local factor is at
most 1 plus the reciprocal square of p minus 1, so the product over the primes
beyond the cut off differs from one by at most the tail of those reciprocal
squares, which is the fourth leaf below. -/

name: prime_reciprocal_square_tail357
header:
theorem prime_reciprocal_square_tail357 :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      (∑' p : Nat.Primes,
        if ⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ < (p : ℕ) then
          1 / (((p : ℕ) : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2 else 0) ≤
        2 / ((⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℝ))
doc:
/-- LEAF. Ingredient of step 3: the prime reciprocal square tail. Beyond some
point the sum of the reciprocal squares of p minus 1 over the primes larger than
N to the one tenth is at most twice the reciprocal of the integer cut off. This
is an elementary estimate on primes alone: it names no singular series, no
Ramanujan sum and no even integer, and it is the only place where the cut off is
compared with a convergent prime series. -/

name: singular_tail357_split
header:
theorem singular_tail357_split :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
        |truncatedSingular357 N n - singularSeries111 n| ≤
          C * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 100 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- Assembly of `singular_tail357` from the leaves above: write the singular
series as the sum of the full Ramanujan weight series through step 1, insert the
finite product of local factors as an intermediate term, and bound the two
halves by step 2 and step 3, with the two constants added. No step uses
`singular_tail357` itself. -/

the series over primes is an identity and no estimate is involved. -/

/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: the character prime series is the character weighted sum
of the residue coset series. Classify each prime by its residue class modulo
the modulus and pull the character value out of each class: a prime and its

name: character_coset_expansion442
header:
theorem character_coset_expansion442 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (z : ℝ) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    characterPrime280 χ N z = ∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), χ b * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 1 of 4: the character prime series is the character weighted sum
of the residue coset series. Classify each prime by its residue class modulo
the modulus and pull the character value out of each class: a prime and its
class have the same character value, a character vanishes at the prime
divisors of the modulus, whose class is not a reduced residue, and the class
series is absolutely convergent, so exchanging the finite residue sum with
the series over primes is an identity and no estimate is involved. -/

name: coset_orthogonality442
header:
theorem coset_orthogonality442 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) =
      1 / (q.totient : ℝ) * (‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), ((1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) c) * Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 * ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), ((1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) b) * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2 + ∑ χ ∈ univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1), ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), χ c * Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 * ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), χ b * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 2 of 4: the orthogonality identity of the reduced residue classes
with the Gauss numbers. Expanding each coset series in the character table of
the unit group writes the transformed coset sums as the character prime sums
weighted by Gauss numbers divided by the totient, and character orthogonality
over the reduced residues collapses the square of that sum, so the mean square
of the transformed coset series is the totient inverse times the squared
character prime sums weighted by the squared Gauss numbers, the principal
term separated from the rest. This is an identity: no bound on a Gauss number
and no estimate on a prime sum enters, those are the next two leaves. -/

name: gauss_principal442
header:
theorem gauss_principal442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), ((1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) c) * Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 3 of 4: the principal Gauss number has modulus at most one. It
is the sum of the unit phases, that is the Ramanujan sum of the reduced
residue system, whose value is a product of minus ones over the prime divisors
of the modulus, so its modulus is one at a squarefree modulus and zero
otherwise, in particular at most one. -/

name: gauss_nonprincipal442
header:
theorem gauss_nonprincipal442 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 2 ≤ q)
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) :
    ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), χ c * Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤ (q : ℝ)
doc:
/-- LEAF. Step 4 of 4: every non principal Gauss number has squared modulus at
most the modulus. The unit phases summed against a non principal character
form its Gauss sum, whose modulus is the square root of the conductor of the
character, and the conductor divides the modulus, so the squared modulus is
the conductor and at most the modulus. -/

name: unit_character_orthogonality442_split
header: theorem unit_character_orthogonality442_split (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (z : ℝ) : (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q), ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (q.totient : ℝ) * (‖characterPrime280 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) N z‖ ^ 2 + (q : ℝ) * ∑ χ ∈ univ.filter (fun χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q => χ ≠ 1), ‖characterPrime280 χ N z‖ ^ 2)
doc:
/-- Assembly of `unit_character_orthogonality442` from the four leaves: the
orthogonality identity, the two modulus bounds on the Gauss numbers and the
identification of the character prime sums with the coset series. Only the
principal weight is replaced by `1` and every other weight by the modulus, so
the mean square is at most the totient inverse times the principal squared
character prime sum plus the modulus times the non principal ones. -/

name: negative_modes_sum111
header:
theorem negative_modes_sum111 (a : ℕ → ℂ) (f : ℤ → ℂ)
    (hf : ∀ i : ℤ, f i = if i ≤ 0 then a i.natAbs else 0) :
    (∑' i : ℤ, ‖f i‖ ^ 2) = ∑' n : ℕ, ‖a n‖ ^ 2
doc: /-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.4. Reindex a square norm sum supported on nonpositive frequencies. -/

name: fourier_coefficient111
header:
theorem fourier_coefficient111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (i : ℤ) :
    fourierCoeffOn (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)
      (fun α => primeFourier111 N α * powerFourier111 N α) i =
        if i ≤ 0 then
          ((primePowerCount111 i.natAbs : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(i.natAbs : ℝ) / N) : ℂ)
        else 0
doc:
/-- LEAF. P0093 page 162 equation 7.4. Identify the Fourier coefficients of
the product by grouping prime and positive power pairs with the same sum.
Abstract Parseval, convergence and frequency reindexing are proved separately. -/

name: parseval_second_moment111
header:
theorem parseval_second_moment111 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∫ α in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖primeFourier111 N α * powerFourier111 N α‖ ^ 2) =
      ∑' u : ℕ, (primePowerCount111 u : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.exp (-2 * u / N)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.4. CONDITIONAL only on fourier_coefficient111.
Abstract Parseval and the zero extension reindexing are proved. -/

name: lemma_three_decomposed111
header: theorem lemma_three_decomposed111 : LemmaThree111
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 Lemma 3. CONDITIONAL only on the Fourier coefficient identification leaf.
The assembly contains no sorry. -/

name: phase_difference412
header:
theorem phase_difference412 (x y : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.exp ((x : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.exp ((y : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ |x - y|
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, local phase variation.
The distance between two unit complex phases is at most the angle difference. -/

name: power_shift_bound412
header:
theorem power_shift_bound412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (α ξ : ℝ) :
    ‖powerFourier111 N (α + ξ) - powerFourier111 N α‖ ≤
      20 * Real.pi * N * |ξ|
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, the quantitative local variation
behind the shift by Delta. The derivative majorant gives constant twenty pi. -/

name: power_zero_lower412
header:
theorem power_zero_lower412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Real.exp (-2) ≤ ‖powerFourier111 N 0‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5. The first positive term gives a
uniform lower bound for the value at zero for every positive N. -/

name: large_value_stability_proved412
header:
theorem large_value_stability_proved412 (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ α ξ : ℝ,
      |ξ| ≤ 1 / ((N : ℝ) * Real.log N) →
      (1 - η) * ‖powerFourier111 N 0‖ < ‖powerFourier111 N α‖ →
      (1 - 2 * η) * ‖powerFourier111 N 0‖ < ‖powerFourier111 N (α + ξ)‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, the displays for xi and Delta.
Exact large_value_stability412 statement with a clean quantitative proof. -/

name: singular_term_le_m111
header:
theorem singular_term_le_m111 (q n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    |((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ) ^ 2 *
        ∑ a ∈ (Finset.range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
          Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))| ≤
      1 / ((q.totient : ℝ) * (q / Nat.gcd q n).totient)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168, one term of 10.6 in its real cosine form is at most 1 over phi of q
times phi of q over gcd of q and n in size, from Perelli1996 Ramanujan400
norm_weighted_ramanujanSum_le. Proved. -/

name: singular_sum_le_divisors_m111
header:
theorem singular_sum_le_divisors_m111 :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ Q n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      ∑ q ∈ Icc 1 Q, 1 / ((q.totient : ℝ) * (q / Nat.gcd q n).totient) ≤
        (∑ d ∈ n.divisors, 1 / (d.totient : ℝ)) * (2 * K)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168, equation 10.4 style count: writing q as gcd of q and n times the rest,
the sum over q at most Q of the term bounds is at most the sum over divisors d of n of
1 over phi of d times twice the constant K of the sum of 1 over phi squared. Proved. -/

name: divisor_inv_totient_small_m111
header:
theorem divisor_inv_totient_small_m111 (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, 1 / (d.totient : ℝ) ≤ δ * Real.log n + C
doc:
/-- The sum of 1 over phi of d over the divisors d of n is at most delta ln n plus a
constant, for every delta: small divisors by the bound 2 times 1 plus ln M of the sum of
1 over phi up to M, at M equal to n to the delta over 2; large divisors by the divisor
bound and 1 over phi of d at most 2 times 1 plus ln d over d. Proved. -/

name: truncSingular_size_m111
header:
theorem truncSingular_size_m111 (ε0 : ℝ) (hε0 : 0 < ε0) :
    ∃ C0 : ℝ, 0 < C0 ∧ ∀ Q n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      |∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Q,
          ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℤ) : ℝ) ^ 2 / (Nat.totient q : ℝ) ^ 2 *
            ∑ a ∈ (Finset.range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
              Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (n : ℝ) * (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))| ≤
        ε0 * Real.log n + C0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168: the truncated singular series of 10.6 in its real cosine form is at
most epsilon_0 ln n plus C_0 in size, for every epsilon_0, uniformly in the level Q.
Proved. -/

name: finite_euler_smooth439
header:
theorem finite_euler_smooth439 (n Q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    (∏ p ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 Q).filter Nat.Prime,
      (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)) =
        ∑' q : Nat.factoredNumbers (Finset.Icc 1 Q), gm n q
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6. The finite prime product is the full
sum over positive integers whose prime factors lie below the cutoff. -/

name: finite_absolute_tail439
header:
theorem finite_absolute_tail439 (n Q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q)
    (s : Finset ℕ) (hs : ∀ q ∈ s, q = 0 ∨ Q < q) :
    ∑ q ∈ s, |gm n q| ≤
      4 * ((6 + 2 * Real.log Q) * (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ^ 2 / Q)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.5. An arbitrary finite subset of the
absolute coefficient tail obeys the existing Heath Brown divisor bound.
The zero term can be included because its coefficient vanishes. -/

name: finite_product_absolute_error439
header:
theorem finite_product_absolute_error439 (n Q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) :
    |(∏ p ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 Q).filter Nat.Prime,
      (if p ∣ n then 1 + 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) else 1 - 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)) -
        ∑' q : ℕ, gm n q| ≤
          4 * ((6 + 2 * Real.log Q) * (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ^ 2 / Q)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.5. The omitted smooth coefficients all
lie in the ordinary tail. This retains the divisor count squared and the
logarithmic cutoff factor, without asserting a uniform rate in the residual. -/

name: weighted_power_summable412
header:
theorem weighted_power_summable412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Summable (fun m : ℕ => ((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) *
      Real.exp (-((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, differentiation of the damped
series. The first frequency moment converges absolutely for positive N. -/

name: weighted_power_bound412
header:
theorem weighted_power_bound412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∑' m : ℕ, ((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) *
      Real.exp (-((2 ^ (m + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) ≤ 10 * N
doc:
/-- P0093 page 165 proof of Lemma 5, the uniform derivative majorant.
Split the dyadic first moment at the integer logarithm of N. The initial
geometric sum is at most two N and the tail is at most eight N. -/

name: residue_gauss_eq470
header:
theorem residue_gauss_eq470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    (∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), χ c *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) =
      gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 1. The displayed reduced residue sum is the standard Gauss sum. -/

name: residue_gauss_sq_le470
header:
theorem residue_gauss_sq_le470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), χ c *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤ (q : ℝ)
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 1. The residue Gauss bound includes imprimitive characters. -/

name: residue_gauss_principal470
header:
theorem residue_gauss_principal470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] :
    ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q),
      ((1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) c) *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 1. The principal residue Gauss sum has squared norm at most one. -/

name: character_coset_expansion470
header:
theorem character_coset_expansion470 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (z : ℝ) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) :
    characterPrime280 χ N z = ∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), χ b * (∑' p : Nat.Primes, if ((p : ℕ) % q = b) then ((Real.exp (-(((p : ℕ) : ℝ) / N)) : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * z * ((p : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) else 0)
doc: /-- Page 155 equation 2.3. Regroup the character prime series by reduced residue. -/

name: inverse_gauss_twist470
header:
theorem inverse_gauss_twist470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (u : (ZMod q)ˣ) :
    (∑ v : ZMod q, ZMod.stdAddChar (-(v * (u : ZMod q))) * χ⁻¹ v) =
      star (gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar) * χ (u : ZMod q)
doc: /-- Page 155 equation 2.3. The negative additive twist of an inverse character. -/

name: unit_transform_energy470
header:
theorem unit_transform_energy470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (G : ZMod q → ℂ)
    (hG : ∀ b, ¬ IsUnit b → G b = 0) :
    (∑ a : ZMod q, if IsUnit a then
      ‖∑ b : ZMod q, ZMod.stdAddChar (-(b * a)) * G b‖ ^ 2 else 0) =
      1 / (q.totient : ℝ) * ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q,
        ‖gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar‖ ^ 2 * ‖∑ b : ZMod q, χ b * G b‖ ^ 2
doc: /-- Page 160 character orthogonality. The restricted additive transform has exact Gauss energy. -/

name: negative_unit_phase470
header:
theorem negative_unit_phase470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (a b : ℕ) :
    ZMod.stdAddChar (-((b : ZMod q) * (a : ZMod q))) =
      Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)
doc: /-- Page 155 equation 2.3. Natural representatives give the negative product phase. -/

name: residue_transform_energy470
header:
theorem residue_transform_energy470 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (w : ℕ → ℂ) :
    (∑ a ∈ (range q).filter (fun a => Nat.Coprime a q),
      ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q),
        Complex.exp ((-(2 * Real.pi * (((a : ℝ) * (b : ℝ)) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I) * w b‖ ^ 2) =
      1 / (q.totient : ℝ) * ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q,
        ‖∑ c ∈ (range q).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c q), χ c *
          Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ ^ 2 *
        ‖∑ b ∈ (range q).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b q), χ b * w b‖ ^ 2
doc: /-- Page 160 character orthogonality. Exact finite energy for arbitrary reduced residue weights. -/

name: residue_gauss_prime_lift_zero470
header:
theorem residue_gauss_prime_lift_zero470 {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hpm : p ∣ m) (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ m) :
    (∑ c ∈ (range (m * p)).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c (m * p)),
      (DirichletCharacter.changeLevel (Nat.dvd_mul_right m p) χ) c *
      Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / ((m * p : ℕ) : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) = 0
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 1. A prime already dividing the smaller level forces the lifted Gauss sum to zero. -/

name: nonprincipal_zero_gauss_nine470
header:
theorem nonprincipal_zero_gauss_nine470 :
    ∃ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 9, χ ≠ 1 ∧
      (∑ c ∈ (range 9).filter (fun c => Nat.Coprime c 9), χ c *
        Complex.exp (((2 * Real.pi * ((c : ℝ) / (9 : ℝ))) : ℝ) * Complex.I)) = 0
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 1. A nonprincipal imprimitive character modulo nine can have zero Gauss sum. -/

name: LFunction_ne_zero_right471
header:
theorem LFunction_ne_zero_right471 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (s : ℂ) (hs : 1 / 2 < s.re) : DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s ≠ 0
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. GRH excludes every nonprincipal zero right of one half. -/

name: mellinLine_re_gt_half471
header:
theorem mellinLine_re_gt_half471 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 < N) (t : ℝ) :

doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 2. The shifted Mellin line lies strictly right of one half. -/

name: continuous_mellinLine471
header: theorem continuous_mellinLine471 (N : ℕ) : Continuous (mellinLine1622 N)
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 2. The shifted Mellin line is continuous in height. -/

name: continuous_LFunction_line471
header:
theorem continuous_LFunction_line471 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t)
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. Holomorphy gives continuity of L along the line. -/

name: continuous_log_norm_line471
header:
theorem continuous_log_norm_line471 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (hz : ∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ≠ 0) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => Real.log ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t)‖
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The real logarithm of the modulus is continuous on a zero free line. -/

name: continuous_lnL_of_slitPlane471
header:
theorem continuous_lnL_of_slitPlane471 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (hs : ∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ∈ Complex.slitPlane) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The principal logarithm is continuous if the line image avoids its cut. -/

name: norm_log_le_log_norm_add_pi471
header:
theorem norm_log_le_log_norm_add_pi471 (z : ℂ) :
    ‖Complex.log z‖ ≤ |Real.log ‖z‖| + Real.pi
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The principal logarithm costs at most pi beyond its real part. -/

name: norm_LFunction_sub_one471
header:
theorem norm_LFunction_sub_one471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ) (hs : s.re = 2) :
    ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s - 1‖ ≤ 3 / 4
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The absolutely convergent anchor series is within three quarters of one. -/

name: norm_lnL_anchor471
header:
theorem norm_lnL_anchor471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q)
    (s : ℂ) (hs : s.re = 2) : ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s)‖ ≤ 2
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The logarithm is uniformly bounded on the anchor line of real part two. -/

name: log_ball471
header:
theorem log_ball471 {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball c r)) (hz : ∀ z ∈ ball c r, f z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball c r) ∧
      g c = Complex.log (f c) ∧ ∀ z ∈ ball c r, Complex.exp (g z) = f z
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. A nonvanishing holomorphic function on a disk has a normalized holomorphic logarithm. -/

name: norm_lnL_disk471
header:
theorem norm_lnL_disk471 {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R M A : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hM : 0 < M)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 R)) (hn : ∀ z ∈ ball 0 R, f z ≠ 0)
    (hupper : ∀ z ∈ ball 0 R, Real.log ‖f z‖ ≤ M)
    (hanchor : ‖Complex.log (f 0)‖ ≤ A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z ∈ ball 0 R) :
    ‖Complex.log (f z)‖ ≤
      2 * M * ‖z‖ / (R - ‖z‖) + A * (R + ‖z‖) / (R - ‖z‖) + Real.pi
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. Borel Caratheodory turns a modulus upper bound into a principal logarithm norm bound. -/

name: lnL_pointwise_of_strip_upper471
header:
theorem lnL_pointwise_of_strip_upper471
    (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH) (A : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A)
    (hstrip : ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q), χ ≠ 1 →
      ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 ≤ s.re → s.re ≤ 4 →
        Real.log ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s‖ ≤ A * Real.log ((q : ℝ) * (|s.im| + 3)))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 < N) (hlog : 2 ≤ Real.log N)
    (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hqN : (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
      (12 * A + 18 + Real.pi) * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. A polynomial strip upper bound gives the cubic principal logarithm bound. -/

name: lnL_growth_of_strip_upper471
header:
theorem lnL_growth_of_strip_upper471 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (hstrip : ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q), χ ≠ 1 →
      ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 ≤ s.re → s.re ≤ 4 →
        Real.log ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s‖ ≤ A * Real.log ((q : ℝ) * (|s.im| + 3))) :
    ∃ B0 : ℝ, 0 < B0 ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 1 ≤ q → (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ) →
        ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ ≠ 1 → ∀ t : ℝ,
          ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
            B0 * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. The strip upper bound suffices uniformly for every height. -/

name: character_partial_sum_bound471
header:
theorem character_partial_sum_bound471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, χ (k : ZMod q)‖ ≤ (q : ℝ)
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. Every nonprincipal partial character sum has norm at most the modulus. -/

name: bounded_mellin_differentiable471
header:
theorem bounded_mellin_differentiable471 (P : ℝ → ℂ) (Q : ℝ) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q)
    (hP : AEStronglyMeasurable P (volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 1)))
    (hbound : ∀ x : ℝ, 1 < x → ‖P x‖ ≤ Q) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun s : ℂ => ∫ x in Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ), P x * (x : ℂ) ^ (-(s + 1)))
      {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re}
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. The Mellin integral of a bounded measurable function is holomorphic in the positive half plane. -/

name: LFunction_eq_partial_integral471
header:
theorem LFunction_eq_partial_integral471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (s : ℂ) (hs : 0 < s.re) :
    DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s = s * ∫ x in Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ),

doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. Abel summation represents the continued nonprincipal L function on the positive half plane. -/

name: norm_LFunction_of_partial_integral471
header:
theorem norm_LFunction_of_partial_integral471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ) (hs : 0 < s.re)
    (hpartial : ∀ n : ℕ, ‖∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, χ (k : ZMod q)‖ ≤ (q : ℝ))
    (hid : DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s = s * ∫ x in Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ),
