doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. Bounded partial sums give the integral bound q times norm s over real part s. -/

name: log_LFunction_upper_of_norm471
header:
theorem log_LFunction_upper_of_norm471 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ)
    (hs0 : 1 / 2 ≤ s.re) (hs4 : s.re ≤ 4)
    (hb : ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s‖ ≤ ‖s‖ * (q : ℝ) / s.re) :
    Real.log ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s‖ ≤ 2 * Real.log ((q : ℝ) * (|s.im| + 3))
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. The integral norm estimate gives twice the logarithm of q times absolute height plus three on the fixed strip. -/

name: LFunction_strip_log_upper471
header:
theorem LFunction_strip_log_upper471 :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q), χ ≠ 1 →
      ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 ≤ s.re → s.re ≤ 4 →
        Real.log ‖DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s‖ ≤ A * Real.log ((q : ℝ) * (|s.im| + 3))
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. The fixed strip has a uniform one sided upper estimate without GRH. -/

name: principal_log_exp_discontinuous471
header: theorem principal_log_exp_discontinuous471 : ¬ ContinuousAt (fun t : ℝ => Complex.log (Complex.exp ((t : ℂ) * Complex.I))) Real.pi
doc: /-- Branch audit for page 159. Even the nonvanishing entire exponential has a discontinuous principal logarithm along an imaginary line. -/

name: exists_continuous_log_path471
header:
theorem exists_continuous_log_path471 (f f' : ℝ → ℂ)
    (hfd : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt f (f' t) t) (hfc : Continuous f')
    (hz : ∀ t : ℝ, f t ≠ 0) :
    ∃ M : ℝ → ℂ, Continuous M ∧ M 0 = Complex.log (f 0) ∧
      ∀ t : ℝ, Complex.exp (M t) = f t
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. A nonvanishing continuously differentiable real path has a normalized continuous logarithm. -/

name: exists_continuous_lnL_line471
header:
theorem exists_continuous_lnL_line471 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (hz : ∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ M : ℝ → ℂ, Continuous M ∧
      M 0 = Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N 0)) ∧
      ∀ t : ℝ, Complex.exp (M t) = DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t)
doc: /-- Page 159 Section 5. Nonvanishing supplies a continuous chosen logarithm on the Mellin line. -/

name: continuous_norm_log471
header:
theorem continuous_norm_log471 {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Continuous f) (hz : ∀ x : X, f x ≠ 0) :
    Continuous fun x : X => ‖Complex.log (f x)‖
doc: /-- Standard bridge for page 159. The norm of the principal logarithm is continuous along every nonvanishing continuous path. -/

name: intervalIntegrable_lnL_line471
header:
theorem intervalIntegrable_lnL_line471 (N q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1)
    (hz : ∀ t : ℝ, DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t) ≠ 0)
    (a b : ℝ) : IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ =>
      Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))) volume a b
doc: /-- Page 156 Lemma 2 and page 159 Section 5. The principal logarithm along a nonvanishing line is integrable on every compact height interval. -/

name: lnL_explicit_size471
header:
theorem lnL_explicit_size471 (hG : LeanLab.DERZ1997.GRH)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 8 < N) (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hqN : (q : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ))
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ (mellinLine1622 N t))‖ ≤
      (42 + Real.pi) * Real.log ((N : ℝ) * (|t| + 2)) ^ 3
doc: /-- Derived explicit version of page 159 Section 5. Under GRH the coefficient forty two plus pi works for every natural N greater than eight. -/

name: prime_power_index_injective473
header:
theorem prime_power_index_injective473 :
    Function.Injective (fun x : Nat.Primes × ℕ => (x.1 : ℕ) ^ (x.2 + 1))
doc:
/-- Positive prime powers have unique prime and exponent indices. This is the
reindexing used for the absolute convergence before equation 5.1 on page 159. -/

name: prime_power_damping_summable473
header:
theorem prime_power_damping_summable473 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Summable (fun x : Nat.Primes × ℕ =>
      Real.exp (-(((x.1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (x.2 + 1) / (N : ℝ))))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 before equation 5.1. Exponential damping is summable on
all positive prime powers, with each prime power appearing once. -/

name: summable_of_summable_neg_log473
header:
theorem summable_of_summable_neg_log473 {ι : Type*} (z : ι → ℂ)
    (hz : ∀ i, ‖z i‖ < 1)
    (hs : Summable (fun i => -Complex.log (1 - z i))) : Summable z
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 audit. Summability of the analytic logarithms
inside the unit disk forces summability of their inputs. -/

name: prime_power_log_series473
header:
theorem prime_power_log_series473 (s : ℂ) (hs : 0 < s.re) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    ∑' m : ℕ, ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-s)
      = -Complex.log (1 - ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 audit. For positive real part the inner
prime power series equals the negative logarithm of its Euler factor. -/

name: prime_cpow_not_summable473
header:
theorem prime_cpow_not_summable473 (s : ℂ) (hs : s.re ≤ 1) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 audit. An unordered prime Dirichlet series
cannot converge when the real part is at most one. -/

name: prime_power_undamped_tsum_zero473
header:
theorem prime_power_undamped_tsum_zero473 (s : ℂ) (hs0 : 0 < s.re) (hs1 : s.re ≤ 1) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
      ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-s)) = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 audit. The iterated unordered prime power
series is zero by the tsum convention in the critical strip. -/

name: character_prime_cpow_not_summable473
header:
theorem character_prime_cpow_not_summable473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ) (hs : s.re ≤ 1) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => χ (p : ℕ) * ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 annotation audit. For every character the unordered prime Dirichlet series is not summable
when the real part is at most one. Only finitely many primes divide the modulus. -/

name: character_prime_power_log_series473
header:
theorem character_prime_power_log_series473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ)
    (hs : 0 < s.re) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    ∑' m : ℕ, ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
        (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-s)
      = -Complex.log (1 - χ (p : ℕ) * ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 annotation audit. The inner character prime power series is the negative logarithm of its
Euler factor when the real part is positive. -/

name: character_prime_power_undamped_zero473
header:
theorem character_prime_power_undamped_zero473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ) (hs0 : 0 < s.re) (hs1 : s.re ≤ 1) :
    (∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
      ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
        (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-s)) = 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 annotation audit. Every character has zero
unordered prime power tsum in the open critical strip. -/

name: log_L_nonzero_on_vertical473
header:
theorem log_L_nonzero_on_vertical473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (hχ : χ ≠ 1) (σ : ℝ) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, Complex.log (DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ ((σ : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I)) ≠ 0
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 annotation audit. On every vertical line a
nonprincipal L-function has a point whose principal complex logarithm is nonzero. -/

name: prime_power_undamped_summable473
header:
theorem prime_power_undamped_summable473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    Summable (fun x : Nat.Primes × ℕ =>
      ‖((x.2 : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((x.1 : ℕ) ^ (x.2 + 1)) *
        (((x.1 : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (x.2 + 1)) ^ (-s)‖)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 supply. To the right of one the undamped
prime power series is absolutely summable. This is the starting contour range. -/

name: exp_prime_power_eq_LFunction473
header:
theorem exp_prime_power_eq_LFunction473 (q : ℕ) [NeZero q]
    (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    Complex.exp (∑' p : Nat.Primes, ∑' m : ℕ,
      ((m : ℂ) + 1)⁻¹ * χ ((p : ℕ) ^ (m + 1)) *
        (((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (m + 1)) ^ (-s)) = DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s
doc:
/-- P0093 page 159 equation 5.1 supply. In the absolute convergence half plane
the exponential of the prime power logarithm series equals the L-function.
The conclusion avoids choosing an invalid principal logarithm branch. -/

name: ramanujan_eq_perelli_pintz376
header:
theorem ramanujan_eq_perelli_pintz376 (q n : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q n =
      LeanLab.PerelliPintz1992.Decomp1519.ram q (n : ℤ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 167 definition before equation 10.4. The two lab
Ramanujan sums agree at positive moduli despite their residue ranges. -/

name: singular_eq_heath_brown376
header:
theorem singular_eq_heath_brown376 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hev : Even n) :
    singularSeries111 n = LeanLab.HeathBrown1985.singular n
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6. The prime Euler product agrees with
the existing finite odd prime factor form at a positive even residual. -/

name: singular_eq_perelli_pintz376
header:
theorem singular_eq_perelli_pintz376 (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    singularSeries111 (2 * k) = LeanLab.PerelliPintz1992.S2k k
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.6. The even residual product is the
Perelli Pintz singular series at half the residual. -/

name: singular_cutoff_conj376
header:
theorem singular_cutoff_conj376 (k Q : ℕ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Q,
      (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius q : ℝ) ^ 2 / (q.totient : ℝ) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        LeanLab.Perelli1996.Ramanujan103.ramanujanSum q (2 * k)) =
      ∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Q,
        ((LeanLab.PerelliPintz1992.Decomp1519.muφ q ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          LeanLab.PerelliPintz1992.Decomp1519.ram q (-(2 * k : ℤ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 finite singular series. Reversing the phase
conjugates the finite sum, and the real coefficients are unchanged. -/

name: inverse_sqrt_floor376
header:
theorem inverse_sqrt_floor376 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    1 / Real.sqrt (⌊(N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 10 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℝ) ≤
      2 * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 20 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.5 at the integer cutoff. Taking a floor
in Q equal to N to one tenth costs at most a factor two after the inverse
square root. This does not use any singular series input. -/

name: divisor_dependent_tail_proved376
header:
theorem divisor_dependent_tail_proved376 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
        |truncatedSingular357 N n - singularSeries111 n| ≤
          C * (n.divisors.card : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 20 : ℝ))
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equations 10.5 and 10.6. Exact
 divisor_dependent_tail376 statement from the already proved Perelli
Pintz tail theorem and the convention bridges above. -/

name: powerTrunc412
header: noncomputable def powerTrunc412 (N : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ℂ
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. The finite damped polynomial contains
exactly the positive powers of two at most N. -/

name: power_trunc_error412
header:
theorem power_trunc_error412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (α : ℝ) :
    ‖powerFourier111 N α - powerTrunc412 N α‖ ≤ 10
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 passage from equation 7.5 to 7.7 and page 161
7.2. The discarded dyadic tail has uniformly bounded norm. Ten is a
conservative constant from the proved first moment bound. -/

name: power_trunc_zero_lower412
header:
theorem power_trunc_zero_lower412 (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    Real.exp (-1) * Nat.log 2 N ≤ ‖powerTrunc412 N 0‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. At zero every retained damping
weight is at least exp of negative one. Thus the finite polynomial grows
at least linearly in the integer base two logarithm of N. -/

name: large_value_to_trunc412
header:
theorem large_value_to_trunc412 (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ α : ℝ,
      (1 - η / 2) * ‖powerFourier111 N 0‖ < ‖powerFourier111 N α‖ →
      (1 - η) * ‖powerTrunc412 N 0‖ < ‖powerTrunc412 N α‖
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equation 7.7. A fixed large value margin absorbs
the bounded discarded tail once the finite polynomial at zero is large.
Only the finite polynomial remains on the right side. -/

name: log_ceiling_bound442
header:
theorem log_ceiling_bound442 (x : ℝ) (hx : 3 ≤ x) :
    Real.log (⌈x⌉₊ : ℝ) ≤ 5 * x ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7, elementary cutoff calculation.
For x at least three, log of the natural ceiling of x is at most
five times x to one quarter. -/

name: singular_log_quarter442
header:
theorem singular_log_quarter442 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ N n : ℕ, 3 ≤ Real.log N → 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
      singularSeries111 n ≤ C * (Real.log N) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equations 10.6 and 10.7. One absolute positive
C bounds the singular product at every even residual from two
through N by C times log N to one quarter, once log N is at least
three. This follows by a Mertens split at the ceiling of log N. -/

name: tail_coefficient_le_one442
header:
theorem tail_coefficient_le_one442 (D : ℝ) (hD : 0 < D) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → D * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 100 : ℝ)) ≤ 1
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.5. Any fixed positive multiple of
N to negative one hundredth is eventually at most one. -/

name: truncated_log_quarter442
header:
theorem truncated_log_quarter442 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
        |truncatedSingular357 N n| ≤ C * (Real.log N) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7, a sufficient corrected coefficient
upper bound. For large N and every even residual from two through N,
the truncated singular coefficient has absolute value at most C
log N to one quarter for one positive absolute C. -/

name: weighted_rotation_deficit439
header:
theorem weighted_rotation_deficit439 (M : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℝ) (z : ℕ → ℂ)
    (c η : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hη : 0 ≤ η)
    (ha : ∀ m ∈ range M, c ≤ a m) (ha1 : ∀ m ∈ range M, a m ≤ 1)
    (hz : ∀ m, ‖z m‖ = 1)
    (hlarge : (1 - η) * (∑ m ∈ range M, a m) <
      ‖∑ m ∈ range M, (a m : ℂ) * z m‖) :
    ∃ w : ℂ, ‖w‖ = 1 ∧
      (∑ m ∈ range M, (1 - (w * z m).re)) ≤ η * (M : ℝ) / c
doc:
/-- P0093 page 162 equations 7.8 and 7.9. A large weighted sum of unit
phases gives a unit rotation with small total unweighted deficit, when
every retained weight lies between a fixed positive c and one. -/

name: relative_weight_small442
header:
theorem relative_weight_small442 (C ε : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N →
      ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)) *
        (C * (Real.log N) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ ε * (N : ℝ) / Real.log N ^ 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7, uniform residual weight comparison.
For every positive C and epsilon, the residual weight times C log N
to one quarter is at most epsilon N over log squared N, uniformly
for residuals from two through N once N is large. Split the residual
at square root N. There is no singular coefficient in this statement. -/

name: truncated_relative_weight442
header:
theorem truncated_relative_weight442 (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N0 : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N0 < N → ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ N → Even n →
      ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) * (1 / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)) *
        |truncatedSingular357 N n| ≤ ε * (N : ℝ) / Real.log N ^ 2
doc:
/-- P0093 page 168 equation 10.7. The actual finite singular
coefficient satisfies the uniform relative weight comparison. The
pointwise coefficient growth and the weight comparison are proved. -/
